deal_index.bond: Beacon Point DC LLC 6.129% Senior Secured Notes due 30-Nov-2042
deal_index.headline: $4.25bn fully amortizing, non-recourse 144A notes issued 9 Jun 2026 by a Hut 8 SPV to build the 352 MW first phase of the Beacon Point campus in Nueces County, Texas, secured by the project and a 15-year triple-net take-or-pay lease to an unnamed tenant rated AA- or better (reported by the FT to be NVIDIA). Moody's rates the notes Baa2 and they priced at T+165bp. Credit rests on one tenant and on energization and delivery in Q1-Q3 2027; Phase 2 (a second 352 MW lease), NVIDIA's disclosure that it expects to reassign leases to third parties, and the reported Lambda/Anthropic usage raise assignment and end-user questions, with indenture limits on assignment to Qualifying Tenants or Creditworthy Transferees the main protection.

deal_index.bond: Hut 8 DC LLC 6.192% Senior Secured Notes due 15-Nov-2042
deal_index.headline: $3.25bn fully amortizing, non-recourse 144A notes issued 30 Apr 2026 by a Hut 8 SPV to build the 245 MW River Bend campus in West Feliciana Parish, Louisiana, secured by the project and a 15-year triple-net lease to Fluidstack (unrated) whose rent and certain other obligations are backstopped by Google LLC. Rated BBB- by S&P and Fitch (per press). The credit is effectively Google's for rent, but the backstop's cap and conditions are not public; no warrants to Google are disclosed (the company said none were issued). Execution risk remains until the first hall energizes in Q2 2027 at about 95% loan-to-cost.

deal_index.bond: Beignet Investor LLC 6.581% Senior Secured Notes due 30-May-2049
deal_index.headline: A single-tranche, fully amortising 144A project bond (about $27.3bn) issued in Oct 2025 to fund the Hyperion data centre campus in Richland Parish, Louisiana, owned by a joint venture in which Blue Owl funds hold 80% and Meta 20%. Debt service is meant to come from Meta's lease rent plus a Meta residual value guarantee (RVG), so the credit is essentially Meta's; S&P rates it A+ (one notch below Meta), per press reports. Meta consolidates nothing: it treats the JV as an unconsolidated VIE, but discloses $46.0bn of maximum exposure to loss as of 30-Jun-2026. Main watch items are construction and power delivery (the campus was announced in Jul 2026 to scale to 5 GW) and what happens at the end of each four-year lease block.

deal_index.bond: Sopaipilla Investor LLC 7.534% Senior Secured Notes due 30-Nov-2048
deal_index.headline: A roughly $12.3-12.6bn 144A senior secured bond issued in late Jul 2026 to fund Meta's El Paso, Texas data centre campus (about 1 GW, about $14bn total cost), owned by a JV in which BlackRock-managed funds (GIP and HPS) hold 80% and Meta 20%. Meta is sole tenant, developer and operator, pays rent from Dec 2028 whether or not the campus is complete, and provides a residual value guarantee (up to about $13bn per its 10-Q). Ratings reported at A+ (S&P, preliminary) and AA- (Fitch, expected); the one-notch gap reflects the absence of an asset mortgage. Seed 7.534% coupon, ISIN and maturity are confirmed by a fund holdings filing, but almost everything else rests on press and newsletter coverage because the offering memorandum is private and Meta has not yet filed its post-closing 10-Q.

deal_index.bond: RD Michigan Property Owner I LLC 7.50% Senior Secured Notes due 2045 (Related Digital / Blackstone, Oracle campus, Saline Township, MI)
deal_index.headline: $14bn 7.500% senior secured notes due 2045 issued in spring 2026 by a Related Digital/Blackstone SPV to fund a 974MW Oracle data center campus in Saline Township, Michigan, anchored by PIMCO. Cash flows come from four triple-net leases to Oracle America Cloud Services guaranteed by Oracle Corporation, so the credit is essentially Oracle (S&P BBB-, Moody's Baa2 negative per Feb-2026 data) plus construction risk; KBRA rates it BBB Stable. The spread over Oracle's own bonds reflects project, construction, power-approval litigation and 144A illiquidity.

deal_index.bond: QTS Central Issuer LLC 6.625% Senior Secured Notes due 1-Sep-2031 (5NC2)
deal_index.headline: QTSODY is a $3.9bn five-year non-call-2 non-recourse project bond sold by Blackstone's QTS in Aug 2026 (closed 27-Aug) to finance part of the Microsoft-leased Fayetteville, Georgia campus (Project Odyssey). It was reshaped from a larger bond-and-loan package into an investment-grade deal reportedly rated Baa3/BBB-, yet priced at a 7.228% yield. Support is the Microsoft lease and the project; there is little official disclosure because it is a 144A deal with no SEC filings.

deal_index.bond: QTS Fayetteville I DC1-2 LLC 5.70% Senior Secured Notes due 15-Apr-2036
deal_index.headline: QTSQST is a $4.6bn 10-year non-amortising, non-recourse single-asset project bond issued in April 2026 by QualityTech (Blackstone) subsidiaries, refinancing construction credit facilities for two Microsoft-leased data centers on the Fayetteville, Georgia campus. Moody's reportedly assigned Baa2. Support is the Microsoft lease and the project; it moved from a 5.70% issue yield to about 7.2% by Aug-Sep 2026 as AI-infrastructure credit repriced.

deal_index.bond: APLD ComputeCo LLC 9 1/4% Senior Secured Notes due 15-Dec-2030
deal_index.headline: APLD ComputeCo LLC's $2.35bn 9.25% senior secured notes due December 2030 are a ring-fenced, project-style financing of two CoreWeave-leased buildings (100 MW and 150 MW, now both live) at the Polaris Forge 1 campus in Ellendale, North Dakota. Applied Digital provides only a completion guarantee, not a payment guarantee; credit rests on CoreWeave rent (now partly owed by a CoreWeave SPV with springing parent guaranty), a DSRA, and a sculpted amortization that leaves roughly 70-75% to refinance at maturity. The sponsor's own model shows coverage near 1.0x in 2028-2029, which together with CoreWeave credit concerns and a heavy parent funding pipeline explains why the notes carry a high-yield spread despite full delivery of the assets.

deal_index.bond: APLD ComputeCo 2 LLC 6 3/4% Senior Secured Notes due 15-Mar-2031
deal_index.headline: APLD ComputeCo 2 LLC's $2.15bn 6.75% senior secured notes due March 2031 finance the 200 MW Oracle-leased Polaris Forge 2 campus in Harwood, North Dakota, through a ring-fenced chain of lessor SPVs with an Applied Digital completion guarantee. The 15-year take-or-pay lease and sculpted amortization (about 81% balloon, about 1.0x modelled coverage, $148mm DSRA) put the bond between investment-grade-tenant and high-yield sponsor risk; the campus is still under construction, with first ready-for-service now guided to 2H CY2026 after a model date of 1-Oct-2026, and the notes marked in the mid-90s at 31-Aug-2026 after a sell-side downgrade on supply overhang.

deal_index.bond: APLD ComputeCo 3 LLC 7% Senior Secured Notes due 15-Jun-2031
deal_index.headline: APLD ComputeCo 3 LLC's $1.59bn 7.00% senior secured notes due June 2031 fund the third 150 MW building (ELN-04) at Applied Digital's Polaris Forge 1 campus in Ellendale, North Dakota, leased to CoreWeave. The building is still under construction, so the credit combines construction and delivery risk (backstopped by a parent completion guarantee), single-tenant CoreWeave exposure with a possible upgrade path through an unconsummated June-2026 MoU to an investment-grade CoreWeave subsidiary, and an amortization profile that leaves about 85% to refinance in 2031. Sponsor model coverage is 1.2x from 2028, and the bond traded down to about 94 by Oct 2026 amid supply-overhang concerns.

deal_index.bond: Cipher Compute LLC 7.125% Senior Secured Notes due 15-Nov-2030
deal_index.headline: Project-finance notes of Cipher Compute LLC ($1.733bn outstanding) that fund the 207 MW critical IT Barber Lake data center in Colorado City, Texas, leased to Fluidstack with a Google backstop equal to the debt and a Cipher completion guarantee. Credit hinges on on-time delivery (now Q4 2026-Q1 2027 after change orders), Google's backstop, and the parent's ability to fund a cost increase of roughly $0.5bn while its equity has been hit by a heavy 2032 convertible and 2030 exchange. The notes amortize but leave a large balloon at Nov-2030.

deal_index.bond: Black Pearl Compute LLC 6.125% Senior Secured Notes due 15-Feb-2031
deal_index.headline: $2.0bn project notes of Black Pearl Compute LLC funding the retrofit and build-out of a 300 MW gross / 216 MW critical IT campus in Wink, Texas, leased to Amazon Data Services under a 15-year triple-net sublease with an Amazon.com parent guaranty and a $9.5mm per MW tenant cost cap. First capacity was delivered two months early (Aug-2026) and rent has started, but later halls are being re-phased, the notes amortize only 7% a year leaving roughly a 70% balloon at Feb-2031, and loss of the lease or guaranty is an immediate default. Tight pricing reflects Amazon credit and tenant protections against overruns.

deal_index.bond: Stingray Compute LLC 6.000% Senior Secured Notes due 15-Jun-2031
deal_index.headline: $810mm project notes of Stingray Compute LLC financing a 70 MW critical IT / 100 MW gross data center in Andrews, Texas, leased for 15 years triple net to Amazon Data Services with an Amazon.com parent guaranty, a $10.5mm per IT MW tenant cost cap and a Cipher completion guarantee. Rent is targeted for Apr-May 2027, the substation is targeted for Q4 2026, and amortization is sized to a 1.25x DSCR leaving roughly a 70-75% balloon at Jun-2031. The tight 6.00% coupon reflects Amazon credit; risks are energization timing, a mid-stream build and parent funding capacity.

deal_index.bond: Core Scientific Finance I LLC 7.750% Senior Secured Notes due 15-May-2031
deal_index.headline: A $3.3bn five-year 144A/Reg S senior secured issue by a ring-fenced Core Scientific subsidiary, secured on five Core Scientific data-center sites (TX, GA, OK, NC) licensed to CoreWeave under 12-year colocation agreements (about 590 MW leased, 395 MW billing at 30 Jun 2026). Parent Core Scientific gives an uncapped completion guarantee on four sites but does not guarantee the notes, so holders rely on CoreWeave-family rent, a cash DSRA and a large balloon (about $2.5bn, 77%) due May 2031. Spreads are wide because the sole tenant, CoreWeave, was itself sold off to distressed yields on 14-16 Oct 2026.

deal_index.bond: Edged Compute LLC 7.500% Senior Secured Notes due 2031 (144A/Reg S)
deal_index.headline: $1.3bn 5-year senior secured notes of Edged US's SPV financing two build-to-suit data centers: Aurora (Chicago) IL, 72MW, leased 16 years to CoreWeave on a triple-net lease (about 60% of capacity), and Atlanta GA, 42MW, leased 15 years to Alibaba Cloud on a modified-gross lease guaranteed by Alibaba Group Services (about 40%). Fitch expected BB-/Stable, capped by CoreWeave and constrained by US sanctions risk on Alibaba; the notes balloon in 2031 against 15-16 year leases. Both buildings are expected live in H1 2027.

deal_index.bond: SV RNO Property Owner 1, LLC 5.875% Senior Secured Notes due 1-Mar-2031
deal_index.headline: Project-finance 144A notes ($3.8bn) funding a 200 MW critical-IT turnkey data center and substation in Storey County, NV, 100% leased on a 197-month triple net lease to an unnamed AA- tenant reported by Bloomberg to be NVIDIA. Credit rests on the lease and construction/power delivery, not NVIDIA recourse; NVIDIA's 10-Q flags $20bn of leases to be reassigned to third parties without naming Fleet. The NV Energy v. Tract suit concerns the South Valley and Peru Shelf power agreements, a headline risk for energization even though the issuer is not a named party in coverage seen.

deal_index.bond: PR RNO Property Owner 1, LLC 6.500% Senior Secured Notes due 1-May-2031
deal_index.headline: Project-finance 144A notes ($4.585bn) funding a second 200 MW critical-IT turnkey data center and substation in Storey County, NV, 100% leased on a 197-month triple net lease to an unnamed AA- tenant (NVIDIA per seed). Higher leverage than TRACTC (about 91% debt-funded per seed) explains the wider spread. Credit depends on construction, power delivery (218 MW interim gas plant approved 17-Sep-2026) and the lease, while the NV Energy lawsuit touches the Peru Ridge/Peru Shelf agreements.

deal_index.bond: Flash Compute LLC 7.250% Senior Secured Notes due 31-Dec-2030
deal_index.headline: $1.3bn senior secured notes issued by Flash Compute LLC, the project company for the 168MW Abernathy, Texas data center that FS CS I LLC (originally TeraWulf 50.1% / Fluidstack 49.9%) is building for a 25-year lease to Fluidstack with a roughly $1.3bn Google backstop. TeraWulf sold its entire stake in July 2026 for about $530mm, leaving a Fluidstack-led owner group and a capped $100mm completion guarantee behind the notes. Because of the 2030 maturity, a balloon of several hundred million dollars remains if the lease runs as modeled.

deal_index.bond: Meridian Arc Holdco LLC 6.25% Senior Secured Notes due 30-Apr-2031
deal_index.headline: $5.7bn 6.25% five-year senior secured notes of Meridian Arc HoldCo, a Fluidstack and Next Frontier (Coatue) joint venture building two data centers (245MW and 185MW) at New Lebanon, Indiana for a 15-year triple-net Fluidstack lease guaranteed by Google. Credit rests on the Google guarantee of an unrated private tenant, about 92% debt-to-cost, no GMP contract and a first-time sponsor-contractor team (Fitch BB as reported).

deal_index.bond: Zenith Arc LLC 8.875% Senior Secured Notes due 31-Aug-2031
deal_index.headline: $2.25bn 8.875% five-year green senior secured notes of Zenith Arc LLC financing a 149MW data center in Okmulgee County, Oklahoma, leased for 15 years triple-net to Jane Street with a lease guaranty, developed by Fluidstack. A county floodplain permit was denied without prejudice in late August 2026 and no resolution is evident by 16-Oct-2026; the bonds fell from 99.5 at pricing to about 91.5 by 30-Sep-2026 on fund collateral marks, with yields near 11% reported.

deal_index.bond: Galaxy Helios Data Centers II LLC 9.875% Senior Secured Notes due 1-Aug-2031
deal_index.headline: A $3.507bn five-year senior secured high-yield bond from a ring-fenced Galaxy Digital subsidiary financing Helios Phase II (400 MW utility / 260 MW critical IT, Dickens County TX), fully leased to CoreWeave for 15 years plus two 5-year options with about $10.4bn of minimum contracted rent. Galaxy's parent gives an uncapped completion guarantee tied to rent commencement (targeted Q2 2027) but no payment guarantee, and the company's own schedule leaves about $3.0bn due at the Aug 2031 maturity. It trades wide because all rent depends on CoreWeave, whose bonds sold off to distressed levels on 14-16 Oct 2026, and because ERCOT Batch Zero classification remains conditional.

deal_index.bond: Elk Grove Village Property LLC 7.50% Notes due Jun-2031 (144A)
deal_index.headline: $900mm 5-year 7.5% notes of a Prime Data Centers SPV financing a 72MW build-to-suit data center in Elk Grove Village, Illinois, reported to be fully leased to CoreWeave for 15 years (about $2.2bn of rent). Credit is effectively CoreWeave (S&P B+/positive) plus re-letting value in the Chicago market; rated Ba3/BB-/BB- per Moody's, S&P and Fitch (secondary sources). About 20% amortizes in the 5-year life, leaving a large 2031 refinancing. All primary documents are private, so most terms are press-sourced.

deal_index.bond: SE Cosmos, LLC 8.875% Senior Secured Notes due 1-May-2031 (144A/Reg S)
deal_index.headline: $999mm bullet notes of SB Energy's SE Cosmos, LLC financing the ~50MW Cosmos Technology Campus on the former 3M site in Austin (Travis County), Texas, leased 15 years triple-net to SoftBank affiliate Silver Bands 3 (US) Corp. with a SoftBank Group Capital Limited guaranty (about $2.9bn exposure), plus an uncapped completion guaranty from parent Energy Global. Credit rests on SoftBank-group support and on-time delivery (rent by 11-Dec-2026 or RFS; full RFS May 2027), not on OpenAI or Milam County, which are separate SB Energy projects.

deal_index.bond: WULF Compute LLC 7.750% Senior Secured Notes due 15-Oct-2030
deal_index.headline: $3.2bn amortizing senior secured notes issued by TeraWulf's WULF Compute LLC to build Lake Mariner buildings CB-3, CB-4 and CB-5, leased for 10 years to Fluidstack with a Google backstop of about $3.2bn that becomes effective building by building as leases commence. $600mm of that support turned on in July 2026 when CB-3 was delivered; CB-4 is commissioning and CB-5 slipped to early 2027, and Fluidstack can terminate for delay beyond 180 days without triggering Google. Until commencement, support is TeraWulf's completion guarantee, a $447mm initial reserve and pledged Google warrants.

deal_index.bond: Yondr JK 1, LLC 6 7/8% Senior Secured Notes due 30-Jun-2031 (Yondr Group / JK Land Holdings, Loudoun County, VA)
deal_index.headline: $715mm 6.875% senior secured notes due June 2031, issued in late June 2026 by a Yondr Group/JK Land Holdings JV to partly fund a 48MW turnkey data center on about 14.3 acres in Loudoun County, Virginia. Public documents confirm the notes, security (first liens plus HoldCo equity pledge) and use of proceeds, but not the tenant, lease or ratings; the Oracle tenancy and Ba3/BB ratings are seed-only. The spread over Oracle's 2031 notes reflects single-asset, short-tenor, high-balloon risk, unverified lease terms and Loudoun zoning/grandfathering uncertainty; on 6-Oct-2026 the Board tabled any repeal of grandfathering.

deal_index.bond: CoreWeave, Inc. 9.750% Senior Notes due 1-Oct-2031
deal_index.headline: $2.75bn of unsecured 9.75% senior notes (a $1.75bn issue on 14 Apr 2026 plus a $1.0bn tap at 102 on 21 Apr) from the AI cloud provider that is the tenant behind the CORZ and GALAXY bonds. Credit rests on a $104bn contracted backlog and 1.5 GW active power against about $35.6bn of debt, $29bn of lease payments and $6bn+ of quarterly capex, with net interest of $640mm a quarter. On 14-16 Oct 2026 its bonds and CDS sold off to distressed levels (2032s about 78c, CDS above 1,000bp) and the CEO responded with an internal memo saying backlog covers debt.

deal_index.bond: Oracle Corporation 4.950% Senior Notes due 4-Feb-2031
deal_index.headline: $3.5bn of Oracle's 4.950% unsecured senior notes due 4-Feb-2031, one of eight series in a $25bn offering priced on 2-Feb-2026 (alongside a $5bn mandatory convertible and a $20bn ATM that Oracle has since fully used). It is the parent/tenant comparable for Oracle-leased project bonds: priced at T+115bp, now rated BBB- at S&P (cut 9-Jul-2026), Baa2 negative at Moody's and BBB at Fitch as last confirmed. Credit story is heavy AI capex (Q1 FY27 capex $28.5bn, FCF -$5.4bn), $125bn of debt and $288bn of not-yet-commenced data center leases against a $664bn backlog.

HUTBPA.title: Beacon Point DC LLC 6.129% Senior Secured Notes due 30-Nov-2042
HUTBPA.headline: $4.25bn fully amortizing, non-recourse 144A notes issued 9 Jun 2026 by a Hut 8 SPV to build the 352 MW first phase of the Beacon Point campus in Nueces County, Texas, secured by the project and a 15-year triple-net take-or-pay lease to an unnamed tenant rated AA- or better (reported by the FT to be NVIDIA). Moody's rates the notes Baa2 and they priced at T+165bp. Credit rests on one tenant and on energization and delivery in Q1-Q3 2027; Phase 2 (a second 352 MW lease), NVIDIA's disclosure that it expects to reassign leases to third parties, and the reported Lambda/Anthropic usage raise assignment and end-user questions, with indenture limits on assignment to Qualifying Tenants or Creditworthy Transferees the main protection.

items.label: Issuer
items.text: Beacon Point DC LLC, a Delaware LLC; indirect wholly-owned subsidiary of Hut 8 Corp.

items.label: Notes
items.text: 6.129% Senior Secured Notes due 2042; senior secured obligations of the Issuer.

items.label: Principal
items.text: $4,250mm aggregate, issued at 100% of par. Original and current principal are the same: no amortization before 30 May 2030. The indenture permits Additional Notes (conditions not retrieved).

items.label: Coupon / day count
items.text: 6.129% fixed, 30/360 (twelve 30-day months); interest accrues from 9 Jun 2026; payable semi-annually 30 May and 30 Nov, first payment 30 Nov 2026; record dates 15 May and 15 Nov.

items.label: Pricing / issue date
items.text: Priced 4 Jun 2026 (purchase agreement dated 4 Jun); issued and indenture dated 9 Jun 2026. Priced at T+165bp, 20bp inside the River Bend notes' issuance spread; substantially oversubscribed.

items.label: Maturity
items.text: 30 Nov 2042 (about 16.5 years from issue).

items.label: Offering format
items.text: Rule 144A / Regulation S. J.P. Morgan Securities LLC represented the initial purchasers (lead bookrunner); Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC bookrunner. The 144A offering memorandum is dated 4 Jun 2026 and is not public.

items.label: ISIN / CUSIP
items.text: ISIN US07367AAA79 and CUSIP 07367AAA7 are seed leads; the form of note filed with the indenture leaves the identifier fields blank, so they could not be verified. Reg S identifiers not found.

items.label: Denominations
items.text: Minimum $2,000 with integral multiples of $1,000 above that.

items.label: Trustee / agents
items.text: Wilmington Trust, National Association: trustee, collateral agent, paying agent and registrar.

items.label: Governing law / jurisdiction
items.text: New York law (Sec. 13.06(a)); exclusive jurisdiction of New York Supreme Court (New York County) and SDNY.

items.label: Optional redemption
items.text: Before the Par Call Date (30 May 2042): make-whole at the greater of 100% and discounted value at Treasury Rate + 25bp (Sec. 3.08(a)). On or after 30 May 2042: 100% plus accrued. A 90% tender clean-up call exists (Sec. 3.08(e)). Seed call date and price (5/30/42 at 100) are consistent.

items.label: Special redemptions and offers
items.text: 100% plus accrued after a Data Center Lease Termination Event (Sec. 3.08(c)); partial redemption at 100% if DSCR is below 1.10x after the Initial Commencement Date, sized to restore about 1.10x (Sec. 3.08(d)); Termination Fee Offer at 100% within 15 Business Days of a Data Center Lease Termination Default, funded by the lease termination fee (Sec. 3.10); optional Underbudget Amount Offer at 100% (Sec. 3.11).

items.label: Change of control
items.text: Holders may put at 101% plus accrued (Sec. 4.11). Before the Initial Commencement Date a Change of Control means a non-Permitted Holder acquiring over 50% of Hut 8 Corp. voting power; it is also triggered if neither Hut 8 nor affiliates (nor, after commencement, a Qualified Operator controlling 200MW+ of US data centers) keeps primary operational control of the site. A Trigger Event additionally needs a Ratings Decline by at least two agencies within 60 days.

items.label: Mandatory amortization
items.text: Semi-annual installments at 100% on 30 May / 30 Nov from 30 May 2030: 26 installments summing to $4,250mm (checked). First $39.0mm (30 May 2030), then $82.9mm; peak $286.9mm on 30 May 2042; final $98.3mm at maturity 30 Nov 2042. Back-loaded: installments through Nov 2035 total about $1.30bn (about 31% of principal). Installments reduce pro rata on redemptions and may be deferred after a Data Center Lease Termination Event (Sec. 14.04(b)).

items.label: Security package
items.text: First-priority security over the Issuer's equity interests and all Issuer property plus Project Accounts, via a Security Agreement, mortgages and account control agreements; Beacon Point Holding LLC pledges its Issuer equity. Excluded Property and Adjacent Property are not collateral. No guarantors appear in the indenture text retrieved.

items.label: Trading levels (seed)
items.text: Seed: yield 6.99%, spread +200bp on 15 Sep 2026; comp NVDA 4.95% 2036. Not verified.

items.label: Borrower chain
items.text: Hut 8 Corp. (Nasdaq: HUT) -> indirect subsidiaries -> Beacon Point Holding LLC (HoldCo, party to the indenture, pledges Issuer equity) -> Beacon Point DC LLC (Issuer, landlord under the Data Center Lease and owner of the project).

items.label: Obligor / guarantees
items.text: Issuer is the sole obligor. Notes are non-recourse to Hut 8 Corp. (company statement; Hut 8 says the parent keeps zero recourse debt). No parent guarantee identified.

items.label: Ring-fencing
items.text: Special-purpose covenants (Sec. 4.19): no material assets beyond the project, no subsidiaries, no employees, no commingling, independent director consent to a bankruptcy filing; restrictions can be lifted only with a Rating Agency Confirmation. HoldCo has a negative-pledge covenant (Sec. 4.20).

items.label: Campus sharing
items.text: The indenture contemplates Shared Facilities and Commercial Property Association arrangements and carves Adjacent Property out of the collateral, which fits a campus where later phases are developed alongside. How Phase 2 sits relative to this SPV is not disclosed.

items.label: Equity contribution
items.text: Not quantified in documents retrieved. Hut 8 says it does not expect to issue equity to fund the project. The campus was originally underwritten to serve affiliate American Bitcoin Corp. before the third-party lease.

items.label: Sponsor
items.text: Hut 8 Corp., Miami-based developer/operator (formerly bitcoin miner) now building AI data centers. Contracted AI portfolio 949 MW (704 MW Beacon Point, 245 MW River Bend), about $26.6bn base-term contract value (company figures).

items.label: Other financings
items.text: $3.25bn River Bend notes (Hut 8 DC LLC, Apr 2026); $1.07bn parent revolver closed 24 Sep 2026 (JPMorgan agent, undrawn at closing, Term SOFR + 1.50-2.00%, minimum liquidity 40% of commitments from 31 Mar 2027 falling to 25% after the Stabilization Date); FalconX $200mm bitcoin-backed facility refinanced to 7.0%; Coatue $150mm convertible converted.

items.label: Parent liquidity
items.text: About $8.1bn total liquidity at 30 Jun 2026 including $7.6bn attributable to Hut 8 (largely project cash) and $497mm at American Bitcoin. Consolidated restricted cash was $6.79bn at 30 Jun 2026.

items.label: Revolver relevance
items.text: The revolver is parent-level with first lien on substantially all assets of Hut 8 and guarantors; bondholders are structurally separate (non-recourse), but the revolver's covenants bear on sponsor capacity to support the project.

items.label: Lease document
items.text: Data Center Lease dated 12 Mar 2026 between the Issuer (landlord) and the Tenant, amended 29 Apr 2026. The lease itself is not filed.

items.label: Tenant identity (official)
items.text: Hut 8 filings do not name the tenant. The 8-K says the lease is to a tenant rated AA- or higher as of 9 Jun 2026; Hut 8 calls it a 'high-investment-grade' tenant.

items.label: Tenant identity (reported)
items.text: The Financial Times, citing five people, reported NVIDIA as the tenant behind both Beacon Point leases, and Bloomberg reportedly concurred. NVIDIA and Hut 8 have not confirmed. The indenture's Qualifying Tenant list names NVIDIA, Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet (Google) and Meta, consistent with but not proof of NVIDIA.

items.label: Lease structure
items.text: 15-year base term, triple net, take-or-pay; 352 MW IT; $9.8bn base-term contract value for Phase 1; fixed rent with 3.0% annual escalator (stated for Phase 2 as substantially the same terms); three 5-year renewal options (campus value $50.2bn with all options, per company). The CEO reportedly said there is no termination for convenience.

items.label: Rent economics
items.text: Company illustration: Phase 1 cumulative NOI about $9,788mm over the base term; revenue about $63mm in 2027 rising to about $776mm in 2041; implied stabilised average NOI about $655mm/yr, roughly $1.86mm per MW-year (derived). Seed base rent of $1.57mm/MW is not confirmed.

items.label: Commencement
items.text: Initial data hall delivery targeted Q3 2027; seed shows rent commencement Aug 2027 to Apr 2028 (unverified). The lease 'Commencement Date' is defined per Critical Power Phase; the Initial Commencement Date is the first phase.

items.label: Assignment and termination protections in the indenture
items.text: The Issuer may not consent to a tenant assignment unless the transferee is a Qualifying Tenant or Creditworthy Transferee (AA-/Aa2 stable with at least $25.0bn tangible net worth) (Sec. 4.21(b)). Lease termination alone is not an Event of Default: it needs the lease ceasing, no Qualifying Data Center Lease within 6 months (12 with conditions), and failure to run a Termination Fee Offer (Sec. 6.01(9)).

items.label: Termination fee
items.text: A Data Center Lease Termination Fee payable by the Tenant exists (amount not disclosed); it is paid into a Designated Account and used to repurchase notes at 100%.

items.label: SLA credits, delay rights, extension mechanics
items.text: Not found: lease not public.

items.label: Location / size
items.text: About 521 acres in Nueces County, Texas; six data halls; 352 MW critical IT; on-site substation. Press describes about 525 acres.

items.label: Campus
items.text: Beacon Point is a 1 GW campus (1,000 MW AEP Texas interconnection agreement). Phase 2 (500 MW of utility capacity, a further 352 MW) is a separate lease; total contracted 704 MW.

items.label: NVIDIA DSX redesign
items.text: The Phase 1 data hall was redesigned to NVIDIA's DSX reference architecture, giving about 57% more IT capacity within the same land and utility footprint (company statement).

items.label: Cost per MW / facility cost
items.text: Seed: facility cost $3,871mm, $11.0mm/MW, 97% debt-funded. Not verified, and hard to square with $4.25bn of notes (which also fund reserves and capitalised interest). Capex budget not found.

items.label: Cooling / density
items.text: Not found in documents retrieved.

items.label: Grid connection
items.text: Grid-connected via AEP Texas; 1,000 MW interconnection agreement for the campus. Advancing through the ERCOT process; Contribution in Aid of Construction funded and substation construction started as of May 2026.

items.label: Energization
items.text: Initial energization targeted Q1 2027 (company). Phase 2 is supported by 500 MW of the 1,000 MW; no incremental capacity needed.

items.label: Permits / ERCOT large-load approvals
items.text: Not found in documents retrieved; no county or PUCT records reviewed.

items.label: Status at 16 Oct 2026
items.text: As of 4 Aug 2026: Phase 1 construction and campus substation underway; initial data hall delivery Q3 2027. Phase 2 initial hall Q2 2028, site preparation underway, long-lead equipment procured. No later milestone disclosure found.

items.label: Contractor / contract type
items.text: Not disclosed for Beacon Point in documents retrieved. The indenture refers to Full Budgeted Cost of Construction, Unused Contingency and Underbudget Amount mechanics, implying a budget with contingency; no GMP mention found for this deal (unlike River Bend).

items.label: Construction-period liquidity
items.text: Debt Service Reserve Required Amount during construction: $481.9mm (estimated accrued interest during construction) less interest paid, plus 50% of next interest payment and 50% of the first amortization installment.

items.label: Completion guarantee / yield-on-cost
items.text: None found. Overrun risk sits with the Issuer / Hut 8; unused contingency at commencement may be distributed once (Sec. 4.05(b)(6)).

items.label: Seed schedule
items.text: Seed: construction start early 2026; commencement Aug 2027 to Apr 2028.

items.label: Debt
items.text: The $4,250mm notes are the only project debt disclosed; fully amortizing, non-recourse. A construction-debt basket allows up to Full Budgeted Cost of Construction less the notes (Sec. 4.04(a)(21)); post-commencement pari passu debt needs a Rating Agency Confirmation.

items.label: Company illustrative metrics
items.text: DSCR 1.34x in sculpted years, initial ICR 2.01x, peak leverage 7.95x (debt/NOI); cumulative NOI $9,788mm, interest $2,569mm, levered FCF $2,860mm; amortization sculpted to repay by end of initial lease term. Seed leverage 7.7x not confirmed.

items.label: Sources and uses
items.text: Not disclosed in detail. Uses: construction, substation, debt service reserves, fees. Unlike River Bend, no reimbursement of sponsor equity is listed.

items.label: Reserves
items.text: DSRA funded at issue (see Construction); after construction, 50% of next interest plus 50% of next installment. May be satisfied with cash, securities, letters of credit or equity.

items.label: Refinancing risk
items.text: Fully amortizing to maturity from lease cash flows. The 15-year base lease from commencement (roughly 2027-2028 to 2042-2043) is about co-terminous with the Nov 2042 maturity, leaving little tail beyond the base term; final installment is $98mm.

items.label: Parent recourse
items.text: None: non-recourse to Hut 8 Corp.

items.label: Third-party credit support
items.text: No tenant-parent guarantee or Google-style backstop is disclosed. Credit rests on the tenant's own obligation (AA- or better per the 8-K). If the tenant is an NVIDIA subsidiary, whether NVIDIA parent guarantees the lease is not disclosed; the indenture treats controlled affiliates as Qualifying Tenants only where the parent guarantees.

items.label: Replacement-tenant provisions
items.text: A Qualifying Data Center Lease with a Qualifying Tenant plus Rating Agency Confirmation cures; 6-month window, up to 12 months with an LOI and funded DSRA.

items.label: Lease termination fee
items.text: Fee paid by tenant into a Designated Account and applied to par repurchase of notes.

items.label: Waterfall
items.text: Revenue Account applied in order: operating expenses; Notes debt service (with DSRA); DSRA replenishment; then any purpose not prohibited (Sec. 4.23(f)). The Notes Proceeds Account funds construction and debt service pre-commencement. Lease termination fees go to a Designated Account.

items.label: Distribution test
items.text: Restricted Payments from Available Retained Excess Cash Flow only if DSCR exceeds 1.10x; other payments allowed only if pro forma DSCR stays at or above 1.10x. Tax distributions require a fully funded DSRA. No separate cash-sweep percentage found.

items.label: Debt and lien limits
items.text: General debt basket $50.0mm, secured asset debt $50.0mm, finance leases $50.0mm, letters of credit $100.0mm; non-pari passu secured credit facilities need DSCR of at least 1.10x.

items.label: Events of default
items.text: Interest 30 days; principal/premium 3 Business Days; covenant breach 90 days (150 for reporting); cross-default and judgment threshold $50.0mm (judgment unstayed 90 days); lease-termination default per Sec. 6.01(9).

items.label: Reporting
items.text: Quarterly reports within 60 days (75 for specified quarters); annual within 120 days (150 for FY2026, may be unaudited); annual compliance certificate within 120 days.

items.label: Lease protection covenant
items.text: No termination or materially adverse amendment of the lease without majority holder consent, Rating Agency Confirmation, or other listed exceptions (Sec. 4.21).

items.label: Moody's
items.text: Baa2 per the company press release; outlook not found. Moody's own release not retrieved.

items.label: S&P / Fitch
items.text: Seed shows NR. No S&P or Fitch rating found for Beacon Point (both rated River Bend). The change-of-control test uses the first rating assigned within 60 days of issue.

items.label: Rating drivers and triggers
items.text: Not found because the agency report was not accessed.

items.label: Uses
items.text: (1) Development and construction of the turnkey 352 MW, six-hall data center on about 521 acres in Nueces County and the on-site substation; (2) debt service reserves; (3) offering fees and expenses.

items.label: Tenant identity and credit
items.text: Tenant is unnamed in filings; AA- or higher at issuance per the 8-K. If NVIDIA (reported), standalone credit is strong, but several protections hinge on tenant rating and Qualifying Tenant status.

items.label: NVIDIA reassignment disclosure
items.text: NVIDIA's 10-Q for the quarter ended 26 Jul 2026 reports $20bn of data center leases not yet commenced 'for third parties' (about 15-year terms, commencing fiscal 2028-2029) and says it expects to reassign these leases to third parties; it separately lists $25bn of its own not-commenced data center leases. The filing does not name Hut 8 or Beacon Point; the $20bn figure and 15-year tenor are consistent with, but do not prove, the two Beacon Point leases ($19.6bn base value). If assigned, the indenture lets the Issuer consent only to an assignee that is a Qualifying Tenant or Creditworthy Transferee (Sec. 4.21(b)); a sublease with NVIDIA remaining liable is not addressed in public documents.

items.label: Lambda / Anthropic
items.text: WSJ, with Reuters single-source confirmation, reported a $35bn, six-year Anthropic cloud deal with NVIDIA-backed Lambda using about 350 MW at Beacon Point; NVIDIA reportedly holds the lease, Lambda runs the GPUs and Anthropic buys the compute. Hut 8 has not confirmed how much of the 704 MW is involved. Credit read: the end-user is a fast-growing AI lab, not an investment-grade entity, so repayment depends on NVIDIA staying the obligor (or an AA-/Aa2 transferee). NVIDIA's 10-Q notes AI clouds can stop supplying NVIDIA and sell to others, which shows circularity risk.

items.label: Construction and schedule
items.text: Energization Q1 2027 and first hall Q3 2027 are company targets; interconnection and substation progress are on the critical path. Delay defers revenue (about $63mm in 2027 in the company illustration) while interest accrues; the DSRA is sized for construction interest of $482mm.

items.label: Cost overrun
items.text: No completion guarantee identified; overruns are covered only by contingency or sponsor equity, and a construction-debt basket exists.

items.label: Back-loaded amortization / tail
items.text: Amortization is light until the late 2030s; $4.25bn of debt against a 15-year base lease leaves limited residual tail and reliance on renewal or re-leasing for any shortfall.

items.label: Technology obsolescence
items.text: The Phase 1 hall was redesigned for NVIDIA DSX architecture (higher density); the value of a purpose-built shell to a replacement tenant is uncertain.

items.label: Phase 2 spill-over
items.text: Phase 2 (same tenant) concentrates exposure on one counterparty at the campus; its financing is under evaluation. Shared power capacity and Shared Facilities arrangements could create cross-dependencies with Phase 2.

items.label: 20 Jul 2026
items.text: Second 15-year, 352 MW lease signed with the same tenant ($9.8bn base value; campus $19.6bn; about $655mm/yr NOI per phase); Phase 2 hall delivery Q2 2028; financing not specified.

items.label: 4 Aug 2026
items.text: Q2 results: Phase 1 on track for Q1 2027 energization and Q3 2027 first hall; Phase 2 financing structures under evaluation.

items.label: 26 Aug 2026
items.text: NVIDIA 10-Q discloses expectation to reassign $20bn of not-yet-commenced third-party data center leases.

items.label: 31 Aug - 1 Sep 2026
items.text: WSJ/Reuters report Anthropic $35bn capacity deal with Lambda at Beacon Point; NVIDIA reported as lease holder.

items.label: 24-28 Sep 2026
items.text: Hut 8 closed a $1.07bn parent revolver (undrawn), adding parent liquidity independent of project notes.

items.label: Trading
items.text: Seed shows +200bp / 6.99% on 15 Sep 2026 versus +165bp at pricing (about 35bp wider); not verified.

The Data Center Lease (12 Mar 2026, amended 29 Apr 2026) is not publicly filed: rent per MW, any parent guarantee, termination rights, delay damages, SLA credits and sublease terms are unknown. Seed rent of $1.57mm/MW could not be verified.

Sources and uses, equity contribution, construction budget, contingency and EPC/GMP contractor are not disclosed in documents retrieved; the 144A offering memorandum is private.

The indenture was read in 100k-character chunks through a summarising fetch tool; some definitions (e.g. Qualifying Tenant detail beyond the list, Rating Agency Confirmation) were not captured for this deal, and the Additional Notes conditions were not seen.
Hut 8 Q2 2026 10-Q notes (debt, commitments, restricted cash detail) could not be retrieved; only the front financial statements were visible.

HUTRBA.title: Hut 8 DC LLC 6.192% Senior Secured Notes due 15-Nov-2042
HUTRBA.headline: $3.25bn fully amortizing, non-recourse 144A notes issued 30 Apr 2026 by a Hut 8 SPV to build the 245 MW River Bend campus in West Feliciana Parish, Louisiana, secured by the project and a 15-year triple-net lease to Fluidstack (unrated) whose rent and certain other obligations are backstopped by Google LLC. Rated BBB- by S&P and Fitch (per press). The credit is effectively Google's for rent, but the backstop's cap and conditions are not public; no warrants to Google are disclosed (the company said none were issued). Execution risk remains until the first hall energizes in Q2 2027 at about 95% loan-to-cost.

items.label: Issuer
items.text: Hut 8 DC LLC, indirect wholly-owned subsidiary of Hut 8 Corp.; direct parent Hut 8 DC Member LLC ('HoldCo') is also a party to the indenture.

items.label: Notes
items.text: 6.192% Senior Secured Notes due 2042; senior secured obligations of the Issuer.

items.label: Principal
items.text: $3,250mm issued at 100% of par; original equals current (amortization starts 15 May 2028). The launch 8-K referred to $3,248mm and the company's illustrative schedule funds $3,248mm; the indenture defines Initial Notes as $3,250,000,000. Treat $3,250mm as the face amount.

items.label: Coupon / payment dates
items.text: 6.192% per annum, paid semi-annually in arrears on 15 May and 15 Nov, first payment 15 Nov 2026. Day count and record dates not captured (form of note not retrieved); 30/360 is typical but not verified.

items.label: Pricing / issue date
items.text: Priced 27 Apr 2026; indenture dated and closing 30 Apr 2026 (seed shows 30 Apr issue date, consistent). Initial price talk was about 213bp over the benchmark; final spread not stated in filings (Beacon Point priced 20bp inside River Bend at T+165, implying about T+185).

items.label: Maturity
items.text: 15 Nov 2042 (about 16.5 years).

items.label: Offering format
items.text: Rule 144A / Regulation S; J.P. Morgan Securities LLC as representative of initial purchasers; Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley also named as underwriters in press.

items.label: ISIN / CUSIP
items.text: Seed: ISIN US44813DAA46, CUSIP 44813DAA4. Not verified (form of note not retrieved).

items.label: Trustee
items.text: Wilmington Trust, National Association, trustee and collateral agent.

items.label: Optional redemption
items.text: Make-whole (Treasury-based; spread in basis points not captured) before the Par Call Date of 15 May 2042; 100% plus accrued on or after it. 100% after a Data Center Lease Termination Event; partial 100% redemption if DSCR is below 1.10x after the Initial Commencement Date, sized to restore about 1.10x.

items.label: Mandatory offers
items.text: Change of control: put at 101%. Asset sales (excess proceeds over $15.0mm), Data Center Lease Termination Default (Termination Fee Offer within 15 Business Days) and Underbudget Amount (GMP reduction) offers at 100% plus accrued; the underbudget offer is at the Issuer's option.

items.label: Mandatory amortization
items.text: Semi-annual installments from 15 May 2028 (Amortization Commencement Date). The indenture's installment schedule (Art. 14) could not be retrieved. Company illustration (sculpted to 1.31x DSCR, $mm): 2028 63, 2029 96, 2030 112, 2031 128, 2032 146, 2033 165, 2034 185, 2035 208, 2036 232, 2037 258, 2038 286, 2039 316, 2040 348, 2041 383, 2042 323; total 3,248; fully repaid by maturity. Seed 'mid-2028 start' is consistent.

items.label: Security package
items.text: First-priority liens on substantially all assets of Hut 8 DC LLC, a pledge of its equity by HoldCo (HoldCo Pledge Agreement), mortgages and Project Accounts; Excluded Property and Adjacent Property are not collateral. Google Guarantee is a Project Document. No guarantors identified.

items.label: Trading levels (seed)
items.text: Seed: yield 6.74%, spread +178bp on 15 Sep 2026; comp GOOGL 4.8% 2036. Not verified.

items.label: Borrower chain
items.text: Hut 8 Corp. -> indirect subsidiaries -> Hut 8 DC Member LLC (HoldCo) -> Hut 8 DC LLC (Issuer, landlord under the Fluidstack lease at River Bend).

items.label: Recourse
items.text: Non-recourse to Hut 8 Corp. (company). The Issuer is the only obligor; Google backstops the tenant, not the Issuer.

items.label: Ring-fencing
items.text: Standard SPE covenants: no unrelated business, no subsidiaries, no general partner interests, affiliate-transaction limits, restrictions on modifying the lease, the Google Guarantee or organizational documents.

items.label: Equity
items.text: Project funded at about 95% loan-to-cost per company; $184mm of prior Hut 8 equity returned at closing from note proceeds; Hut 8 expects no incremental equity. Notes plus $184mm is $3.43bn, implying a total cost near $3.4bn (derived, about $14mm per MW), above the $9-11mm per MW build cost targeted in Dec 2025.

items.label: Sponsor
items.text: Hut 8 Corp. (Nasdaq: HUT), Miami. Contracted AI portfolio 949 MW including 245 MW at River Bend, supported by 1,330 MW utility capacity (company).

items.label: Related financings
items.text: $4.25bn Beacon Point notes (Jun 2026, Baa2); $1.07bn parent revolver closed 24 Sep 2026, undrawn, first-lien on substantially all parent and guarantor assets, minimum liquidity covenant of 40% of commitments from 31 Mar 2027; FalconX bitcoin-backed loan refinanced to 7.0%.

items.label: Anthropic partnership
items.text: December 2025 partnership with Anthropic and Fluidstack: Hut 8 and Anthropic may jointly develop up to 1,050 MW of additional optional capacity, up to 2,295 MW in total, with River Bend as the anchor. This is not a commitment of the River Bend notes' credit.

items.label: Tenant
items.text: Fluidstack USA IV Inc., a Delaware corporation (subsidiary of Fluidstack Ltd., a private AI infrastructure provider); not rated. Anthropic is reported as the workload provider.

items.label: Lease document
items.text: Data Center Lease dated 15 Dec 2025 between the Issuer (landlord) and Fluidstack USA IV Inc.; not filed in full.

items.label: Lease terms
items.text: 15-year base term, triple net, build-to-suit, 245 MW critical IT supported by 330 MW utility capacity (PUE 1.35); fixed rent with 3.0% annual escalator; three 5-year renewal options (up to 30 years); base-term contract value $7.0bn; $17.5-17.7bn with all renewals (the company's two slides differ).

items.label: Rent / NOI
items.text: Company: expected cumulative NOI $6.9bn over base term, about $454mm per year or about $1.85mm per MW. Illustrative revenue $171mm in 2027, $373mm in 2028 rising to $547mm in 2041. Absolute base rent per MW not disclosed; seed $1.50mm/MW is below the company's $1.85mm average and unverified.

items.label: Expansion right
items.text: Fluidstack holds a right of first offer on up to 1,000 MW of additional IT capacity, subject to expanded power; excluded from pipeline figures.

items.label: Commencement
items.text: Initial data hall Q2 2027 (company), more halls through the rest of 2027; seed commencement Apr-Oct 2027. Lease Commencement Date is defined per Critical Power Phase.

items.label: Assignment / replacement
items.text: Novation or assignment under the project documents, including by Google or its affiliates, is permitted without breaching covenants. Qualifying Tenant: NVIDIA, Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet (incl. Google), Meta or controlled affiliates; any NASDAQ/NYSE-listed hyperscaler or technology company with market cap or EV of at least $50.0bn; or a party approved by a majority of holders. Replacement needs a Rating Agency Confirmation.

items.label: Operations Services Agreement
items.text: A separate OSA between Hut 8 and Fluidstack is expected to be backed by an additional Google backstop; it is not part of the notes' collateral as described.

items.label: Delay, termination, SLA terms
items.text: Not found: lease not public. The 10-K lists construction delay penalties or liquidated damages to customers as a risk factor in general.

items.label: Location
items.text: River Bend campus, St. Francisville, West Feliciana Parish, Louisiana (MISO); 627 owned acres with potential expansion to 2,988 acres (company, Dec 2025).

items.label: Capacity
items.text: 245 MW critical IT of turnkey data center plus substation; first of four data halls reported (local source). 330 MW utility capacity under construction.

items.label: Cost
items.text: Dec 2025 target build cost $9-11mm per MW; derived all-in near $3.4bn (see Equity). Seed facility cost $3,057mm and $12.5mm/MW not verified.

items.label: Water
items.text: Hut 8 reportedly committed about $16mm to a new well and about eight miles of water main to be transferred to the parish.

items.label: Utility
items.text: Entergy Louisiana: initial 330 MW with potential for up to 1,000 MW more; 330 MW available from 1 Jul 2026 (company); a 16-year electric service agreement is reported by secondary press.

items.label: Site works
items.text: Grading, Entergy access roads, switchyard construction and transmission line preparation underway as of Dec 2025; campus substation under construction at Aug 2026.

items.label: Permits
items.text: Not found in documents retrieved; no parish or Louisiana PSC records reviewed.

items.label: Contractor
items.text: Jacobs is EPCM / design-build partner working with Vertiv for critical power and cooling; indenture refers to a Guaranteed Maximum Price contract in effect on the Issue Date and an Underbudget Amount mechanism if a revised GMP is signed.

items.label: Schedule
items.text: Initial data hall energization and commissioning targeted Q2 2027; remaining halls in phases through 2027.

items.label: Status at 16 Oct 2026
items.text: As of 4 Aug 2026: vertical construction started, campus substation continuing, initial long-lead equipment received. A local report in Oct 2026 cites over 1,200 workers and first hall operating early 2027.

items.label: Overrun protection
items.text: GMP contract with Jacobs per indenture/press; GMP terms (cap, liquidated damages, completion security) not disclosed. No sponsor completion guarantee found.

items.label: Construction DSRA
items.text: $293.475mm (interest on next three payment dates) less interest paid, plus 50% of next interest and 50% of the first installment due 15 May 2028.

items.label: Debt
items.text: Single tranche $3,250mm fully amortizing notes; about 95% LTC; non-recourse. Post-commencement pari passu debt needs a Rating Agency Confirmation; general basket $10.0mm, secured/finance leases $20.0mm combined, letters of credit $50.0mm, construction debt up to the budgeted cost less the notes.

items.label: Company illustrative metrics
items.text: DSCR 1.31x for 2028-2041 (1.74x in 2027), initial leverage 9.20x falling to 4.61x in 2035 and 0.58x in 2041, initial ICR 1.74x; cumulative interest $1,982mm; levered FCF $1,670mm. Seed leverage 8.8x differs.

items.label: Fitch forecast
items.text: Fitch forecasts minimum DSCR 1.31x and average 1.32x (secondary report of the agency view).

items.label: Refinancing risk
items.text: None by design (fully amortizing to zero by Nov 2042); the 2042 company year shows final-year DSCR 1.82x. Tail is thin: maturity roughly coincides with end of the 15-year base lease.

items.label: Google backstop (scope)
items.text: Google LLC provides a financial backstop (the 'Google Guarantee', governed by a guarantee of the 15 Dec 2025 lease) covering all rent and certain other financial obligations under the lease, described by the company as lease payments and related pass-through obligations for the 15-year base term. Google is an Alphabet subsidiary (S&P AA+, Moody's Aa2 at the Dec 2025 announcement).

items.label: Google backstop (cap, conditions, effectiveness)
items.text: No cap, dollar limit, term beyond the base term, conditions precedent, notice or demand mechanics, or default definition were found in public documents; the guarantee instrument is not filed. Indenture treats the Google Guarantee as a Project Document that the Issuer cannot terminate or materially adversely amend without holder consent or Rating Agency Confirmation, and permits novation or assignment by Google or its affiliates (Sec. 4.21(a)(iv)). A Google Guarantee ceasing is not listed as a standalone event of default in the portion read.

items.label: Reported structural features
items.text: Secondary press reports (single source) describe novation rights during the first six years and a springing Alphabet guarantee if Google's revenue falls below 50% of Alphabet consolidated revenue. Not verified in primary documents.

items.label: Warrants to Google
items.text: None found. The company's Dec 2025 presentation states that no equity or warrants were issued to secure the transaction. No later disclosure of warrants to Google found in Hut 8 filings reviewed.

items.label: Termination fee / replacement
items.text: Lease termination fee (amount undisclosed) goes to a Designated Account; the Issuer must use commercially reasonable efforts to cause the Tenant, Google or a Qualifying Tenant to pay it; funds repurchase notes at 100%. Lease EoD requires lease termination, no Qualifying Data Center Lease within 6 months (12 with LOI with Google or a Qualifying Tenant and funded DSRA), and failure to run a Termination Fee Offer.

items.label: Parent recourse
items.text: None.

items.label: Waterfall
items.text: Notes Proceeds Account funds project costs and debt service before commencement. Revenue Account excludes termination fees and excluded property; applied under Sec. 4.23(f) in priority (operating costs, debt service, DSRA, then other uses). Project Accounts have springing control agreements.

items.label: Distribution test
items.text: Restricted Payments from Available Retained Excess Cash Flow only if DSCR exceeds 1.10x; other payments only if DSCR stays at or above 1.10x; tax distributions need a funded DSRA; a one-time distribution of unused contingency at commencement.

items.label: DSRA after construction
items.text: 50% of next interest plus 50% of next installment; may use letters of credit (basket $50.0mm plus DSRA-specific LC capacity).

items.label: Events of default
items.text: Cross-default and judgment threshold $25.0mm (judgment 90 days unstayed); lease termination default per Sec. 6.01(9); other EoD details not fully captured.

items.label: Change of control
items.text: 101% put on a Change of Control Trigger Event (Change of Control plus Ratings Decline); control tests tied to Hut 8 voting power before the Initial Commencement Date and operational control (Qualified Operator needs 200MW+ US data center control).

items.label: S&P
items.text: BBB- (preliminary Positive outlook at pricing; later press cites final BBB-). S&P reportedly flagged single-tenant concentration as mitigated by the Google backstop. S&P release not retrieved.

items.label: Fitch
items.text: BBB- (expected at pricing; Stable outlook). Fitch reportedly forecasts minimum DSCR 1.31x. Fitch release not retrieved.

items.label: Moody's
items.text: Not rated (seed shows NR). Hut 8 PR for Beacon Point compared its Baa2 to the BBB- on River Bend from S&P and Fitch.

items.label: Triggers
items.text: Rating-agency upgrade/downgrade triggers not found; indenture Applicable Rating is the lower of the first rating within 60 days and the rating at announcement of a change of control.

items.label: Uses
items.text: (1) Finance part of the development and construction of the turnkey 245 MW data center and substation at River Bend; (2) reimburse Hut 8 for part of prior equity contributions (about $184mm per press); (3) fund debt service reserves; (4) fees and expenses.

items.label: Tenant credit
items.text: Fluidstack is an unrated private company; the lease is investment grade only through the Google Guarantee. The cap and conditions of that guarantee are the key unknown.

items.label: Backstop effectiveness
items.text: Public documents do not show whether Google pays on first demand, whether it covers termination payments, damages or only rent, whether it survives lease amendment or assignment, or the cap. The reported Alphabet springing guarantee and six-year novation right are unverified.

items.label: Anthropic dependence
items.text: Anthropic is reported as the workload provider; Anthropic is not a lease party or guarantor. If Fluidstack loses the end-customer, the lease continues but Google exposure grows.

items.label: Construction
items.text: Q2 2027 first hall with phased halls through 2027; ~95% LTC leaves little equity cushion; cost overrun beyond GMP is on Hut 8 DC LLC. Revenue starts 2027 at $171mm illustration; DSRA sized to three interest payments during construction.

items.label: Thin tail
items.text: Debt amortizes fully by Nov 2042 and base lease runs about 15 years from 2027; no residual beyond the base term.

items.label: Power
items.text: Entergy Louisiana 330 MW; energization on the critical path for the Q2 2027 date; local water/infrastructure scrutiny reported.

items.label: Technology obsolescence / replacement
items.text: Replacement tenant must be a Qualifying Tenant plus Rating Agency Confirmation, a high bar for a purpose-built AI shell.

items.label: Q2 2027 delivery on track
items.text: 4 Aug 2026: vertical construction started, substation under way, initial long-lead equipment received; Fluidstack ROFO on 1,000 MW remains.

items.label: Parent revolver
items.text: 24-28 Sep 2026: $1.07bn revolver closed (undrawn).

items.label: Local status
items.text: Oct 2026 local report: over 1,200 workers on site; first hall expected early 2027.

items.label: Trading
items.text: Seed: +178bp / 6.74% on 15 Sep 2026; unverified.

RPLDCI.title: Beignet Investor LLC 6.581% Senior Secured Notes due 30-May-2049
RPLDCI.headline: A single-tranche, fully amortising 144A project bond (about $27.3bn) issued in Oct 2025 to fund the Hyperion data centre campus in Richland Parish, Louisiana, owned by a joint venture in which Blue Owl funds hold 80% and Meta 20%. Debt service is meant to come from Meta's lease rent plus a Meta residual value guarantee (RVG), so the credit is essentially Meta's; S&P rates it A+ (one notch below Meta), per press reports. Meta consolidates nothing: it treats the JV as an unconsolidated VIE, but discloses $46.0bn of maximum exposure to loss as of 30-Jun-2026. Main watch items are construction and power delivery (the campus was announced in Jul 2026 to scale to 5 GW) and what happens at the end of each four-year lease block.

items.label: Issuer / notes title
items.text: Beignet Investor LLC, 6.581% Senior Secured Notes due 30 May 2049 (fixed rate).

items.label: ISIN / CUSIP
items.text: ISIN US076912AA21, CUSIP 076912AA2 as held in a US mutual fund N-PORT filing (fund holdings report, not the indenture). Reg S identifiers not found.

items.label: Coupon and maturity
items.text: 6.581% fixed; maturity 30-May-2049. N-PORT reports the same coupon and maturity date. IFR describes a 23.6-year tenor.

items.label: Size
items.text: About $27.3bn, single tranche, senior secured, amortising, 144A/Reg S format (IFR). Seed outstanding $27,293.8mm. No official document found that states the exact original principal.

items.label: Pricing and issue date
items.text: Priced 16-Oct-2025 at a reported spread of about T+225bp (IFR / Global Data Center Hub). JV signing announced 21-Oct-2025; seed issue date 2025-10-21 is consistent with closing.

items.label: Ranking and amortisation
items.text: IFR describes a single-asset, long-dated, fully amortising bond; proceeds held in Treasuries and drawn down during construction; investors accepted no make-whole. The amortisation schedule itself was not found. Seed: amortisation starts mid-2029 at about 1% p.a. (seed, unverified).

items.label: Call / redemption
items.text: Seed shows next call 30-Nov-2048 at par (6 months before maturity). Not verified against an indenture.

items.label: Trustee, governing law, denominations, clearing
items.text: Not found: indenture and offering memorandum are private (data-room access under NDA per IFR).

items.label: Joint venture ownership
items.text: In Oct 2025 Meta and an affiliate of Blue Owl-managed funds formed a JV to co-develop the Louisiana campus. After closing, Meta holds a 20% membership interest and the Blue Owl investor 80%. Meta contributed about $4.3bn of held-for-sale assets (mostly construction in progress and land), net of liabilities; the investor contributed $7.0bn cash; Meta received a one-time $2.6bn distribution.

items.label: Press release figures differ slightly
items.text: The joint press release (as relayed by Hubbis) says Meta received a one-time distribution of about $3bn and cash from Blue Owl was about $7bn; Meta's 10-Q says $2.6bn. The 10-Q is used as the authoritative figure.

items.label: Funding commitment
items.text: The parties committed to fund their pro rata shares of approximately $27bn of total estimated development costs (buildings plus long-lived power, cooling and connectivity infrastructure).

items.label: Structure in words
items.text: Per IFR and Global Data Center Hub, Beignet Investor is a Blue Owl fund-sponsored issuer sitting above the JV (JV Co) that owns the campus; Meta leases the campus from the JV. Bondholders have no direct recourse to the underlying data centre assets (reported). The exact security package (pledge of JV equity vs mortgage) was not confirmed from an offering document.

items.label: Services by Meta
items.text: Meta provides construction management, administrative and property management services to the JV.

items.label: Equity quantum
items.text: Global Data Center Hub reports about $2.5bn of equity alongside $27.3bn of debt (plus accrued interest income during construction) and a total capital base of about $28.8bn; the numbers do not fully reconcile in the source. Seed facility cost $28,800mm is consistent with this.

items.label: Sponsor
items.text: Funds managed by Blue Owl Capital (rated BBB by S&P per IFR) hold the 80% equity and formal governance. The JV was arranged by Morgan Stanley, which was exclusive financial adviser to Meta and sole bookrunner on the private offering.

items.label: Meta role
items.text: Meta is 20% JV partner, developer/construction manager, property manager, sole tenant and RVG provider. Meta guided that Hyperion is part of a larger AI buildout and announced a scale-up to 5 GW in Jul 2026.

items.label: Other Blue Owl financings
items.text: Not researched in detail: no document found linking Blue Owl's own capital position to this deal beyond the equity commitment.

items.label: Tenant
items.text: Meta Platforms (and subsidiaries) enters multiple operating leases with the JV for properties on the campus. Meta corporate rating AA-/Aa3 per IFR.

items.label: Lease term
items.text: Each leased property has an initial four-year term, with renewal options for a total lease period of up to 20 years. Leases commence in 2029.

items.label: Aggregate initial lease commitment
items.text: About $12.31bn for the initial four-year terms (company disclosure, contractual). Simple arithmetic implies roughly $3.1bn a year, or about $1.5mm per MW-year on the seed 2,064 MW (estimate; the 12.31bn may reflect staggered commencement dates, so this is not the contractual rent per MW). Seed base rent $1.23mm/MW and 2% escalator are not verified.

items.label: Lease type
items.text: Reported as triple-net with rent payable in full during construction delays; abatement only for force majeure or landlord default (Global Data Center Hub). Seed also says triple net. Lease documents not seen.

items.label: Rent start
items.text: Seed/third parties cite rent commencement June 2029 (IFR: completion slated June 2029).

items.label: Payment guaranty
items.text: Global Data Center Hub reports Meta provides a payment guaranty plus the RVG; S&P-related commentary elsewhere disputes whether a guarantee of rent exists. Not confirmed in any Meta filing.

items.label: Location and scale
items.text: Richland Parish, Louisiana. Seed critical IT 2,064 MW (about 2.1 GW; IFR also 2.1 GW). Meta confirmed on 13-Jul-2026 a scale-up to 5 GW across 3,200 acres with total investment above $50bn (secondary report of Meta announcement). It is not clear whether the expansion sits inside the notes' collateral perimeter.

items.label: Cost
items.text: About $27bn estimated development cost per Meta's filings; capital base about $28.8bn per Global Data Center Hub. Implied capex per MW about $13-14mm (seed $14.0mm).

items.label: Buildings and phases
items.text: Earlier plans reported nine buildings delivered in phases through 2030; first 2 GW online by about 2030 and full 5 GW about 2032 (news). Groundbreaking Dec 2024 with an initial $10bn budget (news).

items.label: What the notes finance
items.text: The campus the JV owns and Meta leases: buildings and long-lived power, cooling and connectivity infrastructure (Meta's description of the $27bn cost base).

items.label: Utility and first approval
items.text: Entergy Louisiana serves the campus. The Louisiana Public Service Commission approved, on 20-Aug-2025 by 4-1, three new gas plants totalling about 2.26 GW: two in Richland Parish (expected late 2028) and one at Waterford in St. Charles Parish (expected end 2029). Meta subsidises costs for the first 15 years per press reports.

items.label: Electric service agreement
items.text: Entergy states an electric service agreement with a subsidiary of Meta was previously executed for the first north-Louisiana data centre. In March 2026 Entergy Louisiana signed a second ESA with Evest LLC, a Meta subsidiary, for a second north-Louisiana data centre, secured partly by a Meta guaranty and conditional on LPSC approval. That second ESA and the related application are separate from the Hyperion notes unless the site is the expansion; Entergy does not use the name Hyperion.

items.label: Pending large generation application
items.text: March 2026 application to the LPSC for seven combined-cycle units totalling 5,278 MW (about $12.9bn), four near the customer site in Richland Parish and three at Pointe Coupee, with in-service dates in 2030-2031, plus a 500 kV line (about $1.4bn). Decision targeted at the LPSC December 2026 meeting; intervenors obtained a ruling in Jul 2026 on a subpoena to Meta for project information.

items.label: Grid dependence
items.text: Reports say the 5 GW scale-up depends on plants still under regulatory review; Meta funds the Smalling substation (groundbreaking Jun 2026) and a reported 2.5 GW of renewables.

items.label: Start and status
items.text: Construction began late 2024 (groundbreaking Dec 2024 reported); construction described as well underway with thousands of workers in Oct 2025. Meta is construction manager. Entergy said construction started in earnest early 2026 (secondary).

items.label: Schedule
items.text: Leases commence in 2029 per Meta; rent start June 2029 per IFR / seed. No official phase-by-phase delivery schedule was found.

items.label: Overrun protection
items.text: Meta's 10-K says its exposure includes its estimated future funding commitments to the JV. Detailed completion guarantee or cost-overrun terms were not found. IFR says Meta bears construction and demand risk.

items.label: Advisers
items.text: Arup (independent engineer), Arthur D. Little (commercial diligence), Marsh (risk and insurance), Latham & Watkins (Meta counsel), Kirkland & Ellis (Blue Owl counsel), Milbank (Morgan Stanley counsel).

timeline.text: Groundbreaking at Hyperion with an initial $10bn budget (reported).
Louisiana PSC approves, 4-1, Entergy Louisiana's three gas plants (about 2.26 GW) to serve the Meta data centre.
Beignet Investor prices roughly $27.3bn single-tranche 144A notes at about T+225bp; S&P A+.
Meta and Blue Owl funds sign JV agreement; Meta contributes about $4.3bn of assets and receives $2.6bn distribution, Blue Owl funds contribute $7.0bn.
Joint announcement of the roughly $27bn JV (80/20) and Meta RVG for first 16 years.
Meta Q3 10-Q discloses the JV, leases ($12.3bn initial commitment), RVG and unconsolidated VIE treatment.
Meta 10-K: maximum exposure to loss $45.95bn; RVG payments not probable.
Entergy Louisiana signs second Meta ESA (Evest LLC) and files for seven new CCGTs totalling 5,278 MW.
Meta Q1 10-Q: same lease and RVG terms; judgment on consolidation explained.
Entergy breaks ground on Smalling Substation, funded by Meta (reported).
Meta announces Hyperion scale-up to 5 GW and over $50bn (reported).
Meta Q2 10-Q: JV equity carrying value $2.92bn; maximum exposure $46.03bn.
Mutual fund N-PORT filing confirms notes terms (coupon, maturity, ISIN).
