Post-issuance news up to 16-Oct-2026 not exhaustive: Meta Q3 2026 results (expected late Oct) are not yet available.

TXEDCI.title: Sopaipilla Investor LLC 7.534% Senior Secured Notes due 30-Nov-2048
TXEDCI.headline: A roughly $12.3-12.6bn 144A senior secured bond issued in late Jul 2026 to fund Meta's El Paso, Texas data centre campus (about 1 GW, about $14bn total cost), owned by a JV in which BlackRock-managed funds (GIP and HPS) hold 80% and Meta 20%. Meta is sole tenant, developer and operator, pays rent from Dec 2028 whether or not the campus is complete, and provides a residual value guarantee (up to about $13bn per its 10-Q). Ratings reported at A+ (S&P, preliminary) and AA- (Fitch, expected); the one-notch gap reflects the absence of an asset mortgage. Seed 7.534% coupon, ISIN and maturity are confirmed by a fund holdings filing, but almost everything else rests on press and newsletter coverage because the offering memorandum is private and Meta has not yet filed its post-closing 10-Q.

items.label: Issuer / notes title
items.text: Sopaipilla Investor, LLC, 7.534% Senior Secured Notes due 30 Nov 2048 (the N-PORT shows the coupon rounded to 7.53%).

items.label: ISIN / CUSIP
items.text: ISIN US83577VAA89, CUSIP 83577VAA8 as reported in a US mutual fund N-PORT (Hartford Mutual Funds II, period 31-Jul-2026). Reg S identifiers not found.

items.label: Maturity and coupon
items.text: Fixed rate; maturity 30-Nov-2048 per N-PORT. Seed coupon 7.534% matches the issue title; N-PORT shows 7.53.

items.label: Size
items.text: Launched at $12.3bn on 23-24 Jul 2026 (bookrunners JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley); other press reports about $12.5bn sold after a nearly week-long process with weaker-than-expected demand. Seed shows $12,639.5mm outstanding; no official document confirms the final amount.

items.label: Issue date
items.text: Seed issue date 30-Jul-2026; priced in the week of 27-Jul-2026 per press. Not confirmed from an indenture.

items.label: Ranking, call, amortisation, trustee, law
items.text: Described as senior secured; call (seed: 30-May-2048 at par), amortisation schedule (seed: starts late 2028, about 1% p.a.), make-whole, denominations, trustee and governing law are not found in any accessible document.

items.label: JV ownership
items.text: Funds managed by BlackRock (through GIP and HPS) hold 80% of the JV that owns the El Paso campus; Meta holds 20%. Meta is construction manager, property manager and sole tenant. Announced 28-Jul-2026.

items.label: Meta disclosure
items.text: Meta's Q2 10-Q (30-Jul-2026) says that in July 2026 it entered an exclusivity agreement to co-develop an El Paso campus through a venture in which it would hold a 20% interest; subject to definitive agreements and closing, expected Q3 2026. Meta expects to contribute about $2.3bn of held-for-sale assets (net) and receive a one-time distribution of about $1bn.

items.label: Contributions
items.text: Press release (via TNW): BlackRock contributes about $4.9bn cash at financial close; Meta contributes land and construction in progress worth about $2.3bn and receives about $1bn to align ownership; about $12.5bn of debt is raised at the venture level.

items.label: Obligor and security package
items.text: Issuer is a holding vehicle tied to Project Sopaipilla Holdings, LLC, the JV owning the campus; Meta is not the issuer. Notes are secured by the issuer's accounts, revenues and equity interests in the JV, with no direct mortgage on land and buildings (per Global Data Center Hub). Reg-level pledge documents not seen.

items.label: Closing status
items.text: As of the Q2 10-Q, closing was still expected in Q3 2026. Press reports say the deal was due to close within days of 28-Jul-2026; no Meta filing yet confirms closing (Meta Q3 10-Q due late Oct 2026).

items.label: Sponsor
items.text: BlackRock, via GIP and HPS funds, is the 80% equity owner. Press cites BlackRock's Aligned Data Centers acquisition ($40bn) as context. Equity returns and sponsor liquidity were not researched beyond this.

items.label: Template
items.text: Same 80/20 structure as Meta's Hyperion/Beignet financing with Blue Owl (see RPLDCI), arranged by Morgan Stanley there and JPMorgan/Morgan Stanley here.

items.label: Tenant
items.text: Meta (a Meta subsidiary on the lease). Meta rated AA- by S&P per Global Data Center Hub.

items.label: Term
items.text: Four-year initial term with four extension options, up to about 20 years in total (press release as reported; seed agrees). Meta will enter leases for properties to be developed.

items.label: Rent commencement
items.text: Base rent starts December 2028 whether or not the campus is complete; deferral only for force majeure, landlord funding default or landlord-directed stoppage; abatement for landlord-directed delay capped at $218mm and offset by delayed start-up insurance (Global Data Center Hub reading of offering materials).

items.label: Lease type and SLAs
items.text: Triple-net: Meta pays property taxes, utilities, insurance, routine maintenance, capital repairs and structural replacement. No uptime or performance SLAs reported.

items.label: Rent per MW / escalator
items.text: Seed: $1.38mm per MW-year, 2% escalator. Not verified; Meta's 10-Q gives no aggregate lease commitment for El Paso.

items.label: Location and size
items.text: About 1,000 acres in northeast El Paso, Texas. Campus is about 1 GW (seed critical IT 960 MW) with total development cost about $14bn (seed facility cost $13.7bn). Meta filed in Jul 2026 to add 12 buildings of nearly 26 million sq ft, completion pushed to Feb 2029 (news).

items.label: Phasing and jobs
items.text: Five phases reported; groundbreaking Oct 2025 with an initial $1.5bn commitment, raised to over $10bn in Mar 2026 as the target grew to about 1 GW by 2028; over 4,000 construction workers at peak and about 300 permanent jobs.

items.label: Local incentives
items.text: Dec 2023 city incentive deal with Wurldwide LLC (Meta affiliate): up to 80% city property-tax abatement for 15 years if at least $800mm invested (worth up to about $110mm per El Paso Times).

items.label: Cooling
items.text: Closed-loop liquid cooling reported; Meta says it will match facility consumption with 100% clean/renewable energy (not detailed).

items.label: Utility and bridge plant
items.text: El Paso Electric (EPE) plans to supply through McCloud Generation, a 366 MW plant of 813 modular gas generators next to the site, filed with the Public Utility Commission of Texas. It would serve the data centre exclusively for an initial five-year bridge period starting 2027, separate from EPE's transmission system, with all costs recovered from Meta under a commission-approved rate.

items.label: Load
items.text: Original request 220 MW (Wurldwide LLC); projected over 440 MW by 2027 and potentially 1 GW by 2029 per the amended filing. After the bridge period EPE would seek to connect McCloud to the grid and fold costs into retail rates.

items.label: Discrepancy with brief
items.text: The request describes 1.0 GW grid with 225 MW on-site generation. Sources found show 366 MW on-site (813 modular units, a $473mm line item online by 2027) and 1 GW total; the 225 MW figure was not found in any source.

items.label: Approvals
items.text: McCloud requires approval from the PUCT (certificate of convenience and necessity amendment) and the TCEQ. The city of El Paso intervened; opposition groups have pushed for contract termination and cite ozone and water concerns. Outcome of the PUCT docket was not found.

items.label: Start and status
items.text: Groundbreaking Oct 2025; construction under way, about 2,300 on site in Jul 2026 per press release coverage. Meta is the construction manager.

items.label: Schedule
items.text: Servers expected online 2028, rent from Dec 2028 (seed lease commencement Dec 2028 consistent); expanded buildings to Feb 2029 (news, not reconciled with the 2028 target).

items.label: Overrun protection
items.text: Meta funds cost overruns above 105% of the fixed construction budget (budget amount not stated), per Global Data Center Hub.

items.label: Contractor / contract type
items.text: Not found.

items.label: Sources and uses (reported)
items.text: About $14bn total development cost funded by about $12.5bn of venture-level debt plus equity (BlackRock about $4.9bn cash, Meta about $2.3bn of assets; Meta receives about $1bn). The sums do not reconcile exactly in the source.

items.label: Leverage
items.text: Seed: 90% debt funded, 9.3x leverage at issuance; seed amortisation start late 2028. Not verified.

items.label: Reserves and refinancing
items.text: Not found: reserve accounts, DSRA, capex reserve and amortisation profile are in the private offering memorandum.

items.label: Residual value guarantee
items.text: Meta will provide RVGs with a maximum aggregate exposure of about $13bn (company disclosure). Reported as sized to outstanding principal and triggered if Meta declines to renew at lease expiry.

items.label: Overruns
items.text: Meta funds cost overruns above 105% of budget; rent does not abate for construction delay except narrow cases.

items.label: Accounting
items.text: Meta's Q2 10-Q only describes the venture as a subsequent event with leases and RVG; consolidation treatment (expected unconsolidated VIE like Hyperion) is not yet disclosed because closing is pending.

items.label: Documentation
items.text: No covenant, waterfall, DSCR, lock-up or events-of-default detail found. Offering memorandum is private.

items.label: S&P
items.text: Preliminary A+, stable outlook; one notch below Meta's AA-, attributed to the absence of an asset pledge (Global Data Center Hub). S&P report not accessed.

items.label: Fitch
items.text: Expected AA-(EXP), level with Meta, reasoning that transfer of construction, operating and power-supply risk to Meta makes physical security largely academic (secondary). Fitch release not accessed.

items.label: Moody's
items.text: No Moody's rating found; seed NR.

items.label: Triggers
items.text: Not found; ratings are in effect linked to Meta's own rating (analyst inference).

items.label: Use
items.text: Fund the JV's development of the El Paso campus (about $14bn total development cost). Exact allocation of notes proceeds not found.

items.label: Power
items.text: Bridge plant (366 MW) still needs PUCT and TCEQ approval for 2027 operation; long-term grid supply for 1 GW depends on EPE expansion; local opposition and intervenors.

items.label: Tenant and renewal
items.text: Four-year lease blocks; at non-renewal the notes rely on the Meta RVG (about $13bn maximum exposure).

items.label: Scope changes
items.text: Expanded footprint (12 more buildings, completion Feb 2029) versus the 2028 target.

items.label: Weak demand at issue
items.text: Press reports weaker-than-expected demand and a long marketing process.

items.label: No asset mortgage
items.text: Security is equity and revenues, not land and buildings; hence S&P/Fitch split.

items.label: Closing
items.text: Meta expects closing in Q3 2026; no closing filing found as of 16-Oct-2026.

items.label: Fund holdings
items.text: Mutual funds already hold the notes (Hartford fund N-PORT at 31-Jul-2026 shows $1.56mm face).

items.label: Market
items.text: Seed: yield 7.22%, spread 222bp at 15-Sep-2026.

Notes held by funds (N-PORT) with ISIN US83577VAA89.

RDMICH.title: RD Michigan Property Owner I LLC 7.50% Senior Secured Notes due 2045 (Related Digital / Blackstone, Oracle campus, Saline Township, MI)
RDMICH.headline: $14bn 7.500% senior secured notes due 2045 issued in spring 2026 by a Related Digital/Blackstone SPV to fund a 974MW Oracle data center campus in Saline Township, Michigan, anchored by PIMCO. Cash flows come from four triple-net leases to Oracle America Cloud Services guaranteed by Oracle Corporation, so the credit is essentially Oracle (S&P BBB-, Moody's Baa2 negative per Feb-2026 data) plus construction risk; KBRA rates it BBB Stable. The spread over Oracle's own bonds reflects project, construction, power-approval litigation and 144A illiquidity.

items.label: Issuer
items.text: RD Michigan Property Owner I LLC (KBRA's name; the seed/Bloomberg short name reads 'RD Michigan Pro Owner I'), a special-purpose entity formed by sponsors Related Digital and Blackstone.

items.label: Notes title and size
items.text: $14,000mm 7.500% senior secured notes due 2045, offered under Rule 144A (Bank of America structuring agent).

items.label: Maturity day
items.text: 30-Mar-2045 per seed/Bloomberg; documents read confirm only the year 2045.

items.label: Issue price
items.text: Reported at 98.75 (percent of par) per Bloomberg-sourced coverage; implied yield at issue is therefore above 7.5% (not computed).

items.label: Issue date
items.text: 30-Apr-2026 per seed; KBRA final rating on 1-May-2026 and the law-firm announcement on 5-May-2026 are consistent with an end-April/early-May closing.

items.label: ISIN / CUSIP
items.text: US74941YAA01 / 74941YAA0 per seed (144A). Not confirmed in any official document read; Reg S identifiers not found.

items.label: Ranking and security
items.text: Senior secured. Security package details are not published in documents read (offering memorandum not accessible).

items.label: Initial purchasers
items.text: Bank of America Securities (structuring agent/financial advisor), Goldman Sachs & Co., Wells Fargo Securities, Credit Agricole Securities; Paul Hastings LLP advised the initial purchasers.

items.label: Call schedule
items.text: Next call 30-Apr-2029 at 100.0 per seed (user brief: callable from 2029). Make-whole terms and premium schedule not available.

items.label: Amortization
items.text: KBRA says the notes do not rely on lease renewal for amortization. Seed says amortization starts mid-2032 at about 1.0% per period; schedule not confirmed.

items.label: Trustee, governing law, denominations, clearing
items.text: Not found: the 144A offering memorandum and indenture are not public and the issuer files nothing with the SEC.

items.label: Issuer SPV
items.text: RD Michigan Property Owner I LLC, formed by Related Digital and Blackstone; finances construction of the 974MW campus.

items.label: Sponsors and equity
items.text: Equity from Related Digital and Blackstone-affiliated funds; total project financing announced at $16bn (equity amounts not disclosed in the release).

items.label: Equity amount (Blackstone)
items.text: About $2bn (Bloomberg-sourced, secondary; not in the press release).

items.label: Structure in words
items.text: Sponsor-owned property-owning SPV holds four buildings; each building is leased to Oracle America Cloud Services LLC under a separate triple-net lease with Oracle Corporation guaranteeing; noteholders are secured on the SPV's collateral pool. Detailed ring-fencing and guarantor mechanics are not published.

items.label: Collateral pool changes
items.text: KBRA flags asset sales, building releases, casualty and condemnation as items that could lower debt service coverage.

items.label: Developer
items.text: Related Digital, part of The Related Companies (more than $100bn of assets owned or under development per the company). Related Digital cites a $45bn development pipeline with more than 5 GW of near-term power across the US and Canada.

items.label: Co-sponsor
items.text: Blackstone Real Estate (Blackstone has more than $1.3tn of AUM per the release).

items.label: Original financing partner
items.text: The FT reported in Dec-2025 that Blue Owl would not back the then-$10bn Saline project, citing lenders seeking stricter lease and debt terms. Oracle said Related Digital chose the best equity partner from competitive options. Blackstone was announced as co-equity partner in Apr-2026.

items.label: Parent construction support
items.text: The Related Companies, L.P. provides a limited parent guaranty covering construction completion.

items.label: Tenant
items.text: Oracle America Cloud Services LLC, guaranteed by Oracle Corporation.

items.label: Lease structure
items.text: Fully leased under four triple-net leases, one per building (Core / Building 1, Compute 1 / Building 2, Compute 2 / Building 3, Compute 3 / Building 4).

items.label: Operating responsibilities
items.text: Tenant bears all operating responsibilities for the core and data halls at its own cost; after final completion the landlord has no maintenance obligation, including for structure. No SLAs expected in the leases.

items.label: Rent commencement and termination
items.text: Each lease has a date-certain rent commencement; tenant has no termination option for late delivery; termination and abatement rights are limited.

items.label: Assignment and sublease
items.text: Assignment requires landlord's written consent except to a tenant affiliate; subleasing permitted, with landlord consent needed if the sublessee is a landlord affiliate.

items.label: Lease term and renewals
items.text: Seed: 17.5 years with two 10-year renewals. Not confirmed in any document read; KBRA says amortization does not depend on renewal.

items.label: Rent per MW and escalator
items.text: Seed: about $1.43mm per MW per year, 3.0% escalator. Not confirmed (lease not public).

items.label: Tenant credit
items.text: Oracle expected ratings at Feb-2026 bond pricing: Baa2 (negative) / BBB (negative) / BBB (stable) at Moody's / S&P / Fitch. S&P later cut Oracle to BBB- (stable) on 9-Jul-2026 per secondary reports.

items.label: Oracle disclosure of lease commitments
items.text: Oracle's 10-K (31-May-2026) discloses $260bn of data center lease commitments not yet commenced (15-19 year terms, commencing FY27-FY29) and the 10-Q (31-Aug-2026) $288bn; neither names the Saline lease or the developer.

items.label: Stargate link
items.text: Oracle's construction release and press describe the campus as part of Oracle's work with OpenAI (Stargate); OpenAI is not a party to the notes or lease per documents read.

items.label: Location
items.text: Saline Township, Washtenaw County, Michigan (campus nicknamed 'The Barn' after a preserved red barn on Michigan Avenue).

items.label: Critical IT capacity
items.text: 974MW per KBRA (seed 974 confirmed). Developer describes 'more than one gigawatt'.

items.label: Buildings
items.text: Press release: three single-story buildings. KBRA: four buildings/leases (the Core plus Compute 1-3). Discrepancy unresolved. One news summary cites about 550,000 sq ft per data center building.

items.label: Acreage
items.text: Data center occupies about 250 of 575 rezoned acres north of Michigan Avenue; developer also preserves 750+ acres of open space, farmland and wetlands (company) while the settlement describes about 200 acres preserved.

items.label: Cooling
items.text: Closed-loop cooling; campus targeted for LEED certification (not yet certified). Settlement reports site water will not be used for cooling; own well and waste treatment system.

items.label: Cost
items.text: $16bn total financing for the campus (company). Seed facility cost $15,543mm ($16.0mm per MW) not verified.

items.label: Capex per MW
items.text: About $16.4mm per MW using $16bn / 974MW (derived).

items.label: Jobs and tax
items.text: 2,500+ union construction jobs, 450+ permanent onsite jobs, 1,500+ county-wide; developer cites at least $1.6mm per year to the township through 2039 and $8mm per year to schools.

items.label: Supplier
items.text: DTE Energy supplies 100% of power from existing resources plus a new battery storage investment financed entirely by Oracle; DTE expects about $300mm of savings for existing customers.

items.label: MPSC approval
items.text: Michigan Public Service Commission unanimously approved, ex parte and with conditions, DTE special contracts on 18-Dec-2025 (case U-21990) for about 1.4 GW (1,383 MW per one summary). Customer entity is Green Chile Ventures LLC, an Oracle subsidiary.

items.label: Conditions
items.text: DTE must bear costs of serving the data center that it cannot recover from the customer, and must track and assign those costs; generation, reliability and rate impacts deferred to IRP and later rate cases.

items.label: Service term
items.text: Oracle says DTE will serve it under an existing rate schedule for 17+ years (from a search summary of an Oracle blog; not read directly).

items.label: Challenge
items.text: Michigan AG Nessel appealed to the Michigan Court of Appeals (April 2026) against the ex parte approval; opening brief filed early Aug-2026; environmental groups also challenge. Nessel seeks remand for a contested case. No ruling found as of 16-Oct-2026.

items.label: Energization date
items.text: DTE reportedly expects the data center online by Dec-2027 (low-confidence summary); interconnection details and energization milestones not published.

items.label: General contractor
items.text: Walbridge Aldinger, LLC.

items.label: Start
items.text: Construction began November 2025 per KBRA (seed says early 2026).

items.label: Schedule
items.text: Staggered substantial completions expected between December 2026 and January 2028 (KBRA). Developer says on schedule with first buildings underway; June 2026 reports say all buildings are under construction and the first is nearing completion.

items.label: Permits and equipment
items.text: All key permits secured; owner-furnished contractor-installed equipment procured, with final fit-out purchase orders pending (preliminary) or procured (final).

items.label: Cost protections
items.text: Contractor replacement cost estimated at 7%-13% of GMP; contingency about 12.4% of project budget; limited Related Companies, L.P. completion guaranty during construction.

items.label: Construction risk view
items.text: KBRA rates construction risk elevated because of scale, equipment procurement and labor, but well mitigated, with substantial schedule cushion against date-certain rent commencement.

items.label: Ceremony
items.text: Oracle, Related Digital, Blackstone, OpenAI, Walbridge and Governor Whitmer held a construction celebration on 1-Jun-2026.

items.label: Total financing
items.text: $16bn: $14bn senior secured notes plus equity from Related Digital and Blackstone-affiliated funds.

items.label: Debt share
items.text: About 87.5% of $16bn (derived from $14bn / $16bn). Seed says 90% debt-funded and 10.1x leverage at issuance; not verified.

items.label: Anchor investors
items.text: PIMCO-managed funds and accounts anchored the debt; Bloomberg reports about $10bn of the $14bn.

items.label: Debt service coverage
items.text: KBRA average rating-case DSCR 1.14x (final; 1.13x preliminary).

items.label: Reserves
items.text: Interest, debt service and capex reserve sizes not found.

items.label: Refinancing
items.text: KBRA states the notes amortize without reliance on lease renewal, implying no balloon dependent on renewal.

items.label: Oracle guaranty
items.text: Oracle Corporation guarantees the four leases.

items.label: Construction guaranty
items.text: Limited parent guaranty from The Related Companies, L.P. for construction completion.

items.label: Date-certain rent
items.text: Rent commencement dates are fixed regardless of delivery delay; no tenant termination for late delivery.

items.label: Replacement tenant or termination payments
items.text: Not disclosed.

items.label: Covenants and waterfall
items.text: Not publicly disclosed: indenture and offering memorandum not accessible. KBRA's downgrade triggers (construction delay, contractor replacement, collateral changes, tenant credit) show what matters but are not covenants.

items.label: KBRA
items.text: BBB, Stable, final on 1-May-2026 (preliminary 24-Apr-2026). Drivers: Strong KPRS, well-mitigated construction risk, no reliance on lease renewal. Upgrade unlikely during construction; downgrade if construction slips, contractor replaced with a weaker counterparty, collateral changes reduce DSCR, or lessee credit deteriorates.

items.label: Moody's / Fitch
items.text: Seed lists Baa3 (Moody's) and BBB (Fitch). No Moody's or Fitch release found; the BBB may be KBRA's. Treat as unverified.

items.label: Tenant-guarantor trend
items.text: Oracle: Moody's Baa2 negative and Fitch BBB stable at Feb-2026; S&P cut Oracle to BBB- stable on 9-Jul-2026. A further Oracle downgrade is a stated KBRA downgrade trigger.

items.label: Use
items.text: Fund development, construction and ownership of the Saline Township Oracle campus.

items.label: Tenant concentration and Oracle credit
items.text: Repayment rests on one tenant-guarantor now in the BBB- area with negative momentum at Moody's; Oracle's lease commitments are rising sharply ($288bn not-yet-commenced at 31-Aug-2026).

items.label: Power approval litigation
items.text: AG appeal of the MPSC ex parte approval (U-21990) could force a contested case; outcome and timing unknown.

items.label: Construction
items.text: Staggered completion Dec-2026 to Jan-2028; elevated KBRA risk from equipment, labor and scale; GMP replacement cost 7-13%.

items.label: Local opposition and litigation
items.text: Rezoning was denied 4-1 on 10-Sep-2025 and resolved by consent judgment on 15-Oct-2025; a resident's Open Meetings Act intervention was rejected by a judge on 20-Feb-2026. Residual political and legal risk remains.

items.label: Sponsor history
items.text: Original financing partner Blue Owl withdrew in Dec-2025 before the Blackstone equity and PIMCO-anchored bond financing closed.

items.label: Technology and residual value
items.text: Triple-net lease passes hall operation and capex to the tenant; residual-value risk if the lease is not renewed after amortization; not quantified.

items.label: MPSC/AG appeal
items.text: AG opening brief filed Aug-2026; MPSC says her arguments were already rejected. No court ruling found.

items.label: Oracle credit
items.text: S&P downgrade to BBB- (9-Jul-2026); Oracle fully used its $20bn ATM in Q1 FY27 and reported free cash flow of -$5.4bn.

items.label: Construction
items.text: 1-Jun-2026 ceremony; all buildings reported under construction.

items.label: DTE pipeline
items.text: MPSC approved a separate DTE data center contract for Google (Oct-2026); DTE flags 3-4 GW more potential demand.

gaps: 144A offering memorandum, indenture, lease, guaranty and reserve/waterfall terms are not public and could not be accessed. Covenants, DSCR tests, reserves, call premiums, mandatory amortization schedule and trustee are therefore not verified.

QTSODY.title: QTS Central Issuer LLC 6.625% Senior Secured Notes due 1-Sep-2031 (5NC2)
QTSODY.headline: QTSODY is a $3.9bn five-year non-call-2 non-recourse project bond sold by Blackstone's QTS in Aug 2026 (closed 27-Aug) to finance part of the Microsoft-leased Fayetteville, Georgia campus (Project Odyssey). It was reshaped from a larger bond-and-loan package into an investment-grade deal reportedly rated Baa3/BBB-, yet priced at a 7.228% yield. Support is the Microsoft lease and the project; there is little official disclosure because it is a 144A deal with no SEC filings.

items.label: Issuer
items.text: QTS Central Issuer LLC per Bloomberg security name; press describes two special-purpose subsidiaries of QualityTech, LP as issuers. Exact co-issuer names not confirmed from an official document.

items.label: Notes
items.text: Senior Secured Notes due 2031, inaugural construction Rule 144A/Regulation S offering, $3.9bn aggregate principal.

items.label: Coupon
items.text: 6.625% (user brief and Barclays seed); press guided coupon 6.6%-6.9%. Final coupon not seen in an official document.

items.label: Pricing, yield, OID
items.text: Priced about 18-Aug-2026 at a discount: yield 7.228%, about 40bp inside initial guidance (7.63% initial talk; 7.0-7.4% guidance). OID of about 2.5 points per user brief is consistent with a 6.625% coupon vs 7.228% yield over 5 years (not independently confirmed).

items.label: Issue / closing date
items.text: Closed 27-Aug-2026 (issuer counsel); seed agrees.

items.label: Maturity
items.text: 1-Sep-2031 (seed); counsel confirms only 'due 2031'.

items.label: Tenor and call
items.text: 5-year non-call-2 (5NC2); seed next call 1-Sep-2028 at 100.0 (price shown is probably the first par date; the actual premium schedule and make-whole not seen).

items.label: ISIN / CUSIP
items.text: ISIN US74751QAA67, CUSIP 74751QAA6 (144A); Reg S identifiers not found.

items.label: Principal
items.text: $3.9bn original; Bloomberg seed shows $3,900mm outstanding.

items.label: Amortisation
items.text: Seed: amortisation from mid-2029, estimated about 5.5% of principal before maturity; schedule source not seen (broker estimate).

items.label: Ranking and security
items.text: Senior secured, non-recourse single-asset project bond structure (April Fayetteville notes called the first of this type; Odyssey described as the second).

items.label: Trustee, law, denominations, clearing
items.text: Not found (indenture not public; no EDGAR filing).

items.label: Borrower structure
items.text: Two QualityTech special-purpose subsidiaries issue the notes (Bloomberg), financing a venture in Georgia. SPV chain, guarantors and ring-fencing terms not public.

items.label: Project name
items.text: 'Project Odyssey' (Bloomberg label).

items.label: Original marketing
items.text: Goldman Sachs reportedly tested a roughly $5.4bn bond-and-loan package for the same project (user brief: about $4.9bn bonds plus $500mm term loan, marketed as high-yield); this was reshaped into a $3.9bn five-year investment-grade bond. Only the $5.4bn total is confirmed by two secondary sources; the split is single-source.

items.label: Bookrunners
items.text: Citigroup, Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley.

items.label: Demand
items.text: Order book above $8bn; about $10bn IOIs reported at one point; upsized about $1bn versus initial size.

items.label: Parent
items.text: QualityTech, LP (QTS), a Blackstone portfolio company; Blackstone acquired QTS in 2021 in a roughly $10bn take-private through perpetual-capital real estate and infrastructure funds. QTS reports 100+ data centers in 20+ markets, about 99% occupancy, 2,000+ employees.

items.label: QTS public reporting
items.text: QTS Realty Trust, Inc. (CIK 1577368) filed a Form 15 in Sep-2021 and has filed nothing material since; the project issuers are private 144A issuers with no EDGAR filings located.

items.label: Other QTS financings in 2026
items.text: July-2026 inaugural syndicated term loan of $3.25bn backed by a portfolio of completed, fully leased data centers; commentary also cites an ABS of about $1bn across seven data centers and an $870mm July deal (unverified).

items.label: Tenant
items.text: Microsoft (press: 'Microsoft-tied', long-term lease); QTS does not disclose customers and the lease is not public.

items.label: Lease term, renewal, type
items.text: Seed: 15 years with a 15-year renewal, triple net; unverified.

items.label: Rent
items.text: Seed: base rent about $1.74mm per MW per year, 3.0% escalator; unverified broker figures.

items.label: Commencement
items.text: Seed: lease commencement Nov-2027 to Feb-2028 (phased); unverified.

items.label: Microsoft credit
items.text: Microsoft's own rating was not re-verified in this research. Commentary notes Microsoft has $329.1bn of data-center leases signed but not commenced and that landlords like QTS borrow rather than Microsoft. Pricing near 7.2% despite a Microsoft tenant points to project, construction and lease-structure risk rather than tenant credit.

items.label: Termination, delay, SLA, assignment
items.text: Not found; lease not public.

items.label: Location
items.text: Fayetteville, Georgia (Fayette County): QTS campus of about 615 acres where Microsoft's Fairwater Atlanta operates. User brief ties the notes to this campus; press says only 'Georgia' and 'part of a data center campus'. Buildings financed not named officially.

items.label: Critical IT MW
items.text: Seed: 204 MW critical IT; unverified.

items.label: Campus context
items.text: Epoch AI (estimate): four Microsoft buildings; buildings 1-2 live Oct-2025 (about 321 MW), 3-4 live by Jun-2026 (about 636 MW cumulative); two more shells under way as of May-2026. Which buildings back Odyssey is not disclosed (probably the newer phase).

items.label: Design
items.text: Microsoft describes about 140 kW racks, closed-loop liquid cooling, two-storey halls, GB200/GB300 GPUs.

items.label: Cost and capex per MW
items.text: Not disclosed (seed blank).

items.label: Supply
items.text: Grid-connected; Microsoft states the site relies on utility grid power with no on-site generation or UPS. Trackers name Georgia Power / Southern Company as utility.

items.label: Utility agreement and PSC
items.text: Georgia Power 2025 IRP testimony reportedly treats the QTS Fayetteville campus as one large load near 1,500 MW at full build-out (single secondary report, unconfirmed). No project-specific energisation date located.

items.label: Local entitlement
items.text: Fayetteville reportedly adopted a moratorium then a ban on new data centers, grandfathering existing Fairwater and the Dec-2025 East Campus rezoning (secondary).

items.label: Construction start
items.text: Seed: early 2026; unverified. Campus land clearing began Apr-2023 for the original buildings (Epoch estimate).

items.label: Delivery
items.text: Seed: phased lease commencement Nov-2027 to Feb-2028. Status at 16-Oct-2026 not disclosed.

items.label: Contractor, contract type, completion guarantee
items.text: Not found.

items.label: Debt
items.text: $3.9bn 5NC2 notes; a term loan of about $500mm was in the originally marketed package but is not reported as part of the final deal (unconfirmed).

items.label: Sources and uses, equity, reserves
items.text: Not public. Proceeds fund construction, development and operation of part of a campus, Green Finance Framework projects and general corporate purposes (one report adds distributions to QualityTech).

items.label: Leverage
items.text: Seed: 11.0x at issuance, 9.8x at maturity (broker estimate; basis undefined).

items.label: Refinancing risk
items.text: Five-year tenor with small amortisation leaves a large balloon; contrast with the 10-year bullet in QTSQST.

items.label: Support
items.text: No parent or Microsoft guarantee of the notes disclosed; described as non-recourse single-asset project debt relying on the Microsoft lease.

items.label: Covenants
items.text: Not available (offering memorandum private; no EDGAR filing).

items.label: Moody's
items.text: Baa3 (user brief; press expected Baa3 pre-pricing). Moody's release not retrieved; seed agrees.

items.label: Fitch
items.text: BBB- (user brief; press expected BBB- pre-pricing). Fitch release not retrieved; seed shows NR for Fitch, so assignment is unconfirmed.

items.label: Rationale and triggers
items.text: Not retrieved. Lowest IG tier despite Microsoft tenant, consistent with construction-stage risk.

items.label: Use
items.text: Fund and/or capitalise construction, development and operation of part of a data center campus; investments in projects under the QTS Green Finance Framework; general corporate purposes.

items.label: Construction and delivery
items.text: Notes are construction-stage; rent starts only on phased delivery in 2027-28, with no public information on completion guarantees.

items.label: Pricing signal
items.text: Yield about 7.2% for IG paper, roughly 150bp above the April 5.70% 10-year despite shorter tenor; April bond itself traded about 7.16% on 18-Aug-2026.

items.label: Refinancing
items.text: Five-year balloon with minimal amortisation.

items.label: Concentration, power, local
items.text: Single tenant, large campus load on Georgia Power, local ban on new data centers.

items.label: Sector sentiment
items.text: Sep-Oct 2026 AI-credit weakness (e.g. Hyperion bonds at 91, record lows 7-Oct) is a headwind for related paper.

items.label: Post-issue
items.text: No QTS-specific post-issue development (rating action, litigation, trading level) found; commentary of Oct-2026 cites broader AI-debt stress. Barclays 15-Sep: yield 6.90%, spread 176bp.

APLD.title: APLD ComputeCo LLC 9 1/4% Senior Secured Notes due 15-Dec-2030
APLD.headline: APLD ComputeCo LLC's $2.35bn 9.25% senior secured notes due December 2030 are a ring-fenced, project-style financing of two CoreWeave-leased buildings (100 MW and 150 MW, now both live) at the Polaris Forge 1 campus in Ellendale, North Dakota. Applied Digital provides only a completion guarantee, not a payment guarantee; credit rests on CoreWeave rent (now partly owed by a CoreWeave SPV with springing parent guaranty), a DSRA, and a sculpted amortization that leaves roughly 70-75% to refinance at maturity. The sponsor's own model shows coverage near 1.0x in 2028-2029, which together with CoreWeave credit concerns and a heavy parent funding pipeline explains why the notes carry a high-yield spread despite full delivery of the assets.

items.label: Issuer / notes title
items.text: APLD ComputeCo LLC (Delaware; subsidiary of Applied Digital Corporation) - 9.250% Senior Secured Notes due 2030, sold under a 13-Nov-2025 purchase agreement (Morgan Stanley representative) in a Rule 144A / Regulation S offering.

items.label: Principal / issue price
items.text: $2,350mm original principal, issued at 97.000% of par (about $2,279.5mm gross). Company states net proceeds after issuance costs and repayment of the SMBC loan were about $1.9bn. Outstanding at 31-Aug-2026: $2,350mm (no amortization has started).

items.label: Coupon and dates
items.text: 9.250% fixed, payable semi-annually in arrears on 15 Jun and 15 Dec, first coupon 15-Jun-2026 (a long first period from 20-Nov-2025 issue date). Day-count convention not stated in the 8-K.

items.label: Issue date / maturity
items.text: Issued 20-Nov-2025; final maturity 15-Dec-2030 (about 5.1 years).

items.label: Ranking and security
items.text: Senior secured obligations of the issuer. Secured by first-priority liens on substantially all assets of the issuer and subsidiary guarantors (excluded property carved out), all equity of the guarantors held by the issuer, all equity of the issuer held by APLD HPC Holdings 2 LLC, and the indenture Project Accounts.

items.label: Mandatory amortization
items.text: Semi-annual on 15 Jun and 15 Dec starting 15-Dec-2027, in amounts fixed in the indenture (schedule not in the 8-K; adjusts for partial redemptions or add-on notes). Company illustration (not the indenture): 7.75% of original principal per year starting two years after issuance, i.e. about $30mm in 2027 and about $182mm a year in 2028-2030, leaving about $1.77bn (75%) due at maturity before any excess-cash-flow offers.

items.label: Amortization incl. excess-cash-flow offers (model)
items.text: The same Nov-2025 model assumes a 50% excess-cash-flow offer with 100% noteholder uptake, which would cut the balance to about $1.6bn at end-2030 (cumulative amortization plus offers about 32%). Seed 'est. amortization 30.4%' is broadly consistent with that model. Whether the final indenture contains an ECF offer and its exact mechanics was not verified.

items.label: Optional redemption
items.text: Before 15-Dec-2027: callable in whole or part at 100% plus a make-whole premium; up to 40% may be redeemed with proceeds of certain equity offerings at the indenture price. On or after 15-Dec-2027: callable at indenture redemption prices (not disclosed in the 8-K). Seed shows first call price 104.63 (consistent with par plus half a coupon) - unverified.

items.label: Change of control
items.text: Holders may require repurchase at 101% of principal plus accrued interest on specified change-of-control events.

items.label: Trustee / collateral agent
items.text: Wilmington Trust, National Association (trustee and collateral agent).

items.label: ISIN / CUSIP
items.text: Seed: ISIN US00202DAA54, CUSIP 00202DAA5 (144A). No Reg S identifiers found. Not verified against any official document.

items.label: Governing law, denominations, clearing
items.text: Not stated in the 8-K or press releases; indenture exhibit (Ex 4.1) not read in full. Customary 144A/Reg S structure implies DTC / Euroclear / Clearstream clearing, but this is not confirmed in the sources reviewed.

items.label: Borrower chain
items.text: Applied Digital Corporation (NASDAQ: APLD) -> ... -> APLD HPC Holdings 2 LLC (direct parent of the issuer) -> APLD ComputeCo LLC (issuer) -> guarantor subsidiaries. The Macquarie preferred sits at APLD HPC TopCo 2 LLC; the 10-K states TopCo 2's purpose is the North Dakota AI data centers and that Macquarie also funded Polaris Forge 2 through it, so HPC Holdings 2 appears to sit under TopCo 2 (inference; the intermediate holding chart was not published).

items.label: Subsidiary guarantors
items.text: APLD ELN-02 HoldCo LLC, ELN-03 HoldCo LLC, ELN-02 LLC, ELN-03 LLC, ELN-02 LandCo LLC and ELN-03 LandCo LLC. The 10-Q describes them as majority-owned subsidiaries of the Company. Applied Digital Corporation itself is NOT a guarantor of the notes (it provides only the completion guarantee).

items.label: Ring-fencing
items.text: Indenture restricts the issuer and guarantors from holding assets or running operations unrelated to the Ellendale facilities and certain additional projects, limits affiliate transactions and requires Project Accounts. Notes are not cross-collateralised with ComputeCo 2 or ComputeCo 3 (separate SPV chains).

items.label: Facilities financed
items.text: ELN-02 (100 MW critical IT, a 'pilot build', Building 1 / PF1-1) and ELN-03 (150 MW, Building 2 / PF1-2) at the Polaris Forge 1 campus, Ellendale ND (400 MW campus). ELN-04 (Building 3, 150 MW) is financed separately by the ComputeCo 3 notes (ELNFOR).

items.label: Equity contribution
items.text: Company says Macquarie funded $337.5mm into Polaris Forge 1 conditioned on closing of this offering. Under the Macquarie A&R unit purchase agreement Applied Digital funds equity at $750k per MW (less equity already invested). Equity actually invested in ELN-02/03 SPVs not disclosed.

items.label: Sponsor
items.text: Applied Digital Corporation (Dallas TX; CEO Wes Cummins, CFO Saidal Mohmand): designer, builder, owner and operator of AI data centers. 1,410 MW contracted across five campuses (Polaris Forge 1-3, Delta Forge 1-2) with about $36bn of base-term contract value, though only 250 MW is live.

items.label: Parent liquidity (31-Aug-2026)
items.text: $3.7bn cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash against $6.4bn of debt; total assets $11.7bn. Q1 FY27 interest expense $77.4mm, adjusted EBITDA $64.4mm, net loss from continuing operations attributable to common $221.0mm.

items.label: Other parent-level financing
items.text: $450mm 2.75% convertible notes due Jun 2030; $430mm secured revolver (SOFR+2.25%, matures earlier of 29-May-2029 or 91 days before a PEPA date; $82.4mm drawn at 31-Aug-2026, about $65mm of letters of credit at May-2026); Series G convertible preferred equity line (commitment raised to $2.0bn in Jun-2026); $58.5mm Texas Capital note. Revolver is secured by non-data-center-project assets.

items.label: Parent contingent exposure
items.text: Guarantee of Base Electron's obligations under a ~$2.4bn design-build contract for a ~1.2 GW gas plant (related party; terminable by paying a $50mm or $100mm fee or on a Base Electron financing). Applied Digital owns about 10% of Base Electron. In Oct 2026 it signed a PPA with Base Electron.

items.label: Macquarie preferred equity (APLD HPC TopCo 2)
items.text: Perpetual preferred units plus 15% of fully diluted common of TopCo 2. Funded $112.5mm (6-Oct-2025), $450.0mm (25-Nov-2025), $337.5mm (9-Dec-2025) and $925.0mm (29-May-2026) = about $1.8bn, giving Macquarie 13.5% of TopCo 2 common; redeemable NCI carried at about $2.0bn at 31-Aug-2026 including $60.1mm of PIK dividends in the quarter. Macquarie has the right to invest up to $4.9bn more.

items.label: Macquarie preferred economics
items.text: Company term sheet: dividend 12.75% (PIK or cash) in years 0-5, step-ups from year 6 and +2% a year from year 11 to a 16.75% cap; liquidation preference of greater of accreted value plus common FMV or 1.8x MOIC; company call after year 5; Macquarie put on a sale or after year 7. This is structurally subordinated to the notes (equity above the SPV chain) but it is a large claim on the sponsor's distributions.

items.label: Tenant
items.text: CoreWeave, Inc. Originally two leases signed 28-May-2025 by APLD ELN-02 LLC (100 MW, four data halls, operational Oct 2025) and APLD ELN-03 LLC (150 MW), aggregate 250 MW. Applied Digital Corporation guarantees its subsidiaries' obligations to the tenant under the leases (landlord performance guarantee, not a credit support for rent).

items.label: March 2026 restructuring
items.text: On 30-Mar-2026 CoreWeave restructured: (i) ELN-02 lease amended to suspend the term on two of four data halls, which were re-let on substantially the same terms to CoreWeave Compute Acquisition Co. VIII, LLC (a wholly owned CoreWeave SPV) with a springing CoreWeave guaranty; (ii) ELN-03 lease assigned to the same SPV, releasing CoreWeave Inc. from the lease, again with an unconditional springing guaranty of payment and performance; (iii) CoreWeave to post a $50mm letter of credit supporting the ELN-02 lease within 30 days.

items.label: Credit implication
items.text: Rent on ELN-03 and half of ELN-02 is now owed primarily by an SPV with a springing (not direct) parent guaranty; the SPV's own financial profile and the trigger terms of the springing guaranty are not public. Delivery of the $50mm LC was not confirmed in the 10-Q.

items.label: Lease form
items.text: Company describes its leases as 15-year, take-or-pay, non-cancellable gross modified leases (tenant recoveries of operating costs are billed separately: $13.3mm in Q1 FY27); a termination for convenience requires payment of the full remaining contractual value. Seed says 'Modified Gross' - consistent.

items.label: Term and options
items.text: About 15 years from commencement plus three five-year renewal options (Polaris Forge 1 total up to about $27.4bn if all renewals exercised per the company).

items.label: Rent
items.text: Polaris Forge 1 (400 MW, three leases): about $10.7-11.0bn base-term contracted revenue. Nov-2025 model for ELN-02/03 shows total 15-year revenue of $6,764mm, $368mm in 2027 and $379mm in 2028 (about 3% annual growth, implying about $1.5mm per MW per year initially including any recoveries). Seed shows $1.39mm/MW base rent and 3.0% escalator (unverified; the model growth rate supports about 3%).

items.label: Commencement
items.text: Model assumed ELN-03 Phase 1 commencement 30-Jun-2026. Actual: 100 MW (ELN-02) operational Oct 2025; first 75 MW of ELN-03 / Building 2 ready for service 1-Jul-2026; second 75 MW 1-Oct-2026. Contract commencement/Outside Completion Date terms not disclosed.

items.label: Tenant credit support / warrants
items.text: CoreWeave received no support from third parties disclosed here. Applied Digital issued CoreWeave a warrant for up to 13,062,521 shares at $7.19 in connection with the ELN-02/ELN-03 leases (parent equity cost, not an obligation of the issuer).

items.label: Termination-fee coverage (model)
items.text: Company model: remaining lease payments ('termination fee') of $6,743mm at issuance equals 2.9x debt outstanding, rising to about 3.1x in 2030.

items.label: Tenant-side disclosure
items.text: CoreWeave's Q2-2026 10-Q does not name Applied Digital or these leases; no tenant-side corroboration found.

items.label: Location and campus
items.text: Ellendale, North Dakota; Polaris Forge 1 is a 400 MW critical-IT campus in three buildings (100 / 150 / 150 MW). The notes cover Building 1 (ELN-02) and Building 2 (ELN-03).

items.label: Design
items.text: Applied Digital standard AI Factory: ~907,500 sq ft, six data halls per 150 MW building, hybrid liquid plus air cooling with modular units, 4:3 DR electrical architecture with dual 75 MW systems, N+1 substation, diesel backup generation, 625 W/sq ft, 1.15 target PUE; 12-18 month build cycles per 100-150 MW (company statement, reference spec).

items.label: Cost per MW
items.text: Company anticipates capex of $11-13mm per MW for Polaris Forge campuses and expected site NOI margin of 88% +/- 3% for PF1. Seed implies facility cost $3.1bn / $12.4mm per MW (unverified; within company range).

items.label: What the notes finance
items.text: A portion of construction cost of ELN-02 and ELN-03, repayment of the SMBC loan (credit agreement dated 11-Feb-2025 by APLD HPC Holdings LLC), funding the debt service reserve and transaction expenses.

items.label: Grid supply
items.text: The campus is grid-connected; company says use of excess regional grid capacity has returned more than $45mm of electricity credits to local ratepayers. The serving utility, interconnection agreement and any dedicated generation for PF1 are not named in the filings reviewed.

items.label: Portfolio power statement
items.text: Company states each contracted MW is backed by land under its control and/or an executed utility power agreement, and cites about 2.15 GW of gross grid-connected utility power for the 1.4 GW contracted portfolio.

items.label: Base Electron
items.text: Related-party independent power producer developing ~1.2 GW of gas-fired generation in North Dakota (MISO). Applied Digital signed a PPA in Oct 2026. This supports future campuses rather than these notes' buildings.

items.label: Status at 16-Oct-2026
items.text: Building 1 (100 MW) operating since Oct 2025. Building 2: first 75 MW phase ready for service 1-Jul-2026, second 75 MW phase 1-Oct-2026, so both buildings financed by the notes are complete: 250 MW live across ten data halls.

items.label: Versus plan
items.text: Seed lease commencement '4Q25 - 2Q26' vs delivery of ELN-03 at 1-Jul and 1-Oct-2026: Phase 1 was about one day after the model's 30-Jun-2026 assumption; Phase 2 followed one quarter later. Contractual outside dates not known.

items.label: Rent recognised
items.text: Base rental revenue in the quarter ended 31-Aug-2026 was $65.8mm for the whole PF1 campus (about 175 MW live at quarter-end), plus tenant recoveries of $13.3mm; tenant fit-out services revenue of $183.5mm is pass-through type activity.

items.label: Contractor / contract type
items.text: EPC contractor and contract type (GMP vs fixed price) are not disclosed in the filings reviewed.

items.label: Cost-overrun protection
items.text: Applied Digital will provide a customary completion guarantee: it must fund the issuer as necessary to achieve each Commencement Date under the respective lease if note proceeds and available funds (including prior equity contributions) are insufficient. With both buildings now delivered the guarantee's practical relevance for these notes has largely fallen away (inference).

items.label: Sources and uses
items.text: Not published as a table. Uses per 8-K: portion of ELN-02/03 construction, SMBC loan repayment, debt service reserve, expenses. Company's Nov-2025 model assumes total contributions: debt $2,350mm, DSRA $177mm (implied from the DSRA line total).

items.label: Leverage at issuance
items.text: Seed: 7.2x. Derived from the Nov-2025 model: $2,350mm / 2028 cash available for debt service of $340mm = about 6.9x (estimate). Seed debt-funded 66% and facility cost $3.1bn unverified.

items.label: Debt service sculpting (model)
items.text: Model cash available for debt service of $340mm / $350mm / $361mm in 2028 / 2029 / 2030 against net interest of $170mm / $154mm / $138mm plus amortization of $182mm gives coverage of about 0.97x / 1.04x / 1.13x (estimate), with DSRA draws used as a plug in 2028 ($12mm). The model assumed an 8.5% coupon, below the actual 9.25% (about +$16mm interest a year before interest income on reserves), so headroom is thin by design.

items.label: Maturity / refinancing
items.text: Balloon at 15-Dec-2030 of roughly $1.6-1.8bn depending on ECF offers (model). Refinancing depends on a seasoned, fully delivered CoreWeave-leased asset with 11+ years of remaining lease term, at which point the lease SPV credit change matters.

items.label: Market value
items.text: Company-estimated (level 2) fair value of the 2030 notes about $2.5bn at 31-Aug-2026 versus $2.35bn par (about 106 on a rounded basis; the 10-Q rounds to $0.1bn). Seed: 15-Sep yield 7.60%, spread 236 bp.

items.label: Parent completion guarantee
items.text: Customary completion guarantee from Applied Digital Corporation (see Construction). No parent payment guarantee of the notes; no parent guarantee of rent.

items.label: Debt service reserve
items.text: DSRA funded at closing from proceeds ('fund debt service reserves'); model shows about $177mm in total and a small draw of $12mm in 2028.

items.label: Lease termination protection
items.text: Take-or-pay leases where termination for convenience requires payment of full remaining value (company statement). CoreWeave springing guaranty on the SPV leases and a $50mm LC on ELN-02.

items.label: Replacement-tenant / residual value
items.text: No third-party residual value guarantee found. Company argues North Dakota power and campus scarcity supports re-leasing value.

items.label: Negative covenants
items.text: Limits on additional debt and guarantees, restricted payments, investments, liens, asset sales, sale-leasebacks, unrelated business, affiliate transactions and mergers, each with exceptions.

items.label: Events of default
items.text: 'Customary events of default' only; specific lock-up, DSCR and cash-sweep triggers are not described in the 8-K and the indenture was not read in full.

items.label: Excess cash flow offer
items.text: Nov-2025 model assumes 50% of excess cash flow is offered to noteholders at par starting soon after closing (illustrative $5mm / $90mm / $61mm in 2025-2027). Actual indenture terms not verified.

items.label: Reporting / waterfall
items.text: Waterfall, DSCR tests, Project Accounts mechanics and reporting package are in the offering memorandum and indenture exhibits not reviewed.

items.label: S&P / Fitch / Moody's
items.text: Seed: NR (Moody's) / BB- (S&P) / BB- (Fitch). No rating-agency release was accessible; only a retail social-media post references an expected BB- at Fitch pre-pricing. Treat as unverified.

items.label: Triggers
items.text: Not available (agency reports not accessed). Key credit drivers one would expect: tenant SPV credit, DSCR near 1.0x in model years, parent liquidity for completion.

items.label: Stated uses
items.text: (1) Fund a portion of construction and associated costs of ELN-02 (100 MW) and ELN-03 (150 MW) at the 400 MW Ellendale campus; (2) repay the SMBC loan (Credit and Guaranty Agreement of 11-Feb-2025); (3) fund debt service reserves; (4) pay transaction expenses.

items.label: Net proceeds
items.text: Approximately $1.9bn after issuance costs and SMBC repayment (company, 10-K).

items.label: Tenant concentration and credit migration
items.text: 100% CoreWeave exposure; March-2026 restructuring moved ELN-03 and two ELN-02 halls to an SPV under springing guaranty.

items.label: Thin modelled coverage
items.text: Debt service coverage around 1.0x in 2028-2029 in the sponsor's own model, using a coupon 75 bp below the actual; reliance on DSRA and on 3% rent escalators.

items.label: Balloon and refinancing
items.text: About 70-75% of principal falls due at 15-Dec-2030.

items.label: Sponsor capital intensity
items.text: Parent has $6.4bn of debt, a related-party gas-plant guarantee and must fund more than $13bn of pipeline (broker estimate) which could compete for liquidity; Macquarie preferred accretes at 12.75%.

items.label: Disclosure gaps
items.text: Indenture covenants (lock-up, ECF offer, additional debt tests) not reviewed; ratings unverified.

items.label: Macquarie funding
items.text: Further $337.5mm (Dec 2025) and $925mm (May 2026) preferred draws into TopCo 2.

items.label: CoreWeave restructuring
items.text: 30-Mar-2026 lease amendment and assignment to CoreWeave SPV VIII; $50mm LC; springing guaranties.

items.label: Operations
items.text: Building 2 delivered 1-Jul and 1-Oct-2026 (250 MW live). Notes valued at about $2.5bn at 31-Aug-2026.

items.label: Parent financing
items.text: June-2026 $1.59bn ComputeCo 3 notes, revolver upsized to $430mm, Series G commitment to $2.0bn; Delta Forge 2 lease (210 MW, $5.2bn) on 5-Jun-2026.

items.label: Sell-side
items.text: JPMorgan cut APLD/PFORGE project bonds to Neutral from Overweight (about 12-Oct-2026), citing supply overhang of about $7.8bn of debt needed for three Meta-linked campuses (the tenant is named as Meta only by the bank, not by the company).

items.label: Delta Forge financing and Investor Day
items.text: No filing, press release or rating report found for a Delta Forge debt financing being marketed in Sept 2026; management says Polaris Forge 3, Delta Forge 1 and Delta Forge 2 are the next financings. No Aug-2026 Investor Day disclosure found; the June-2026 investor presentation was used instead. Supply of $13bn of new project debt is the relevant read-across for these notes' spread.

timeline.text: ELN-02 (100 MW) and ELN-03 (150 MW) leases signed with CoreWeave; CoreWeave warrant issued.
Third CoreWeave lease (Building 4 / ELN-04, 150 MW) signed, taking Polaris Forge 1 to 400 MW contracted.
First 100 MW building at Polaris Forge 1 operational.
Macquarie initial closing: $112.5mm preferred units in APLD HPC TopCo 2.
$2.35bn senior secured notes offering announced with investor presentation.
Notes priced at 97.000% with a 9.250% coupon.
Notes closed; indenture signed with Wilmington Trust; SMBC loan repaid.
Third Macquarie closing ($337.5mm), tied to this offering for Polaris Forge 1.
CoreWeave restructuring: ELN-03 assigned to CoreWeave SPV VIII, two ELN-02 halls re-let to SPV, $50mm LC.
Fourth Macquarie closing ($925mm); total funded about $1.8bn.
Memorandum of understanding with CoreWeave on assigning the Polaris Forge 1 Building 3 lease to an investment-grade subsidiary (relevant to ELN-04).

Phase 2 of Building 2 ready for service; 250 MW live across two buildings.
10-Q: notes carried at fair value of about $2.5bn; $3.7bn cash vs $6.4bn debt at the parent.
JPMorgan downgrades APLD/PFORGE project bonds to Neutral on supply overhang.

PFORGE.title: APLD ComputeCo 2 LLC 6 3/4% Senior Secured Notes due 15-Mar-2031
PFORGE.headline: APLD ComputeCo 2 LLC's $2.15bn 6.75% senior secured notes due March 2031 finance the 200 MW Oracle-leased Polaris Forge 2 campus in Harwood, North Dakota, through a ring-fenced chain of lessor SPVs with an Applied Digital completion guarantee. The 15-year take-or-pay lease and sculpted amortization (about 81% balloon, about 1.0x modelled coverage, $148mm DSRA) put the bond between investment-grade-tenant and high-yield sponsor risk; the campus is still under construction, with first ready-for-service now guided to 2H CY2026 after a model date of 1-Oct-2026, and the notes marked in the mid-90s at 31-Aug-2026 after a sell-side downgrade on supply overhang.

items.label: Issuer / notes title
items.text: APLD ComputeCo 2 LLC (Delaware; subsidiary of Applied Digital Corporation) - 6.750% Senior Secured Notes due 2031, sold under a 3-Mar-2026 purchase agreement (Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC representative), Rule 144A / Regulation S.

items.label: Principal / issue price
items.text: $2,150mm original principal, issued at 98.000% of par (about $2,107mm gross; company says net proceeds about $2.1bn). Outstanding at 31-Aug-2026: $2,150mm (no amortization yet).

items.label: Coupon and dates
items.text: 6.750% fixed, semi-annual in arrears on 15 Mar and 15 Sep, first payment 15-Sep-2026. Day count not stated in the 8-K.

items.label: Issue date / maturity
items.text: Issued 10-Mar-2026; matures 15-Mar-2031 (about 5.0 years).

items.label: Ranking and security
items.text: Senior secured. First-priority liens on substantially all assets of the issuer and guarantors (excluded property carved out) and on all equity of the issuer held by APLD FAR Holdings LLC (its direct parent); Project Accounts (including the debt service reserve) are part of the indenture package.

items.label: Mandatory amortization
items.text: Semi-annual on 15 Mar and 15 Sep, beginning on the first payment date after the final Commencement Date under all data center leases in effect on the issue date, in indenture-specified amounts. Sponsor model (illustrative): 4.25% of original principal initial annual amortization rising 0.375 pt a year, i.e. $61mm in 2027, $99mm in 2028, $108mm in 2029, $116mm in 2030, with $1,767mm outstanding at end-2030 and about $1.75bn (about 81%) due at maturity.

items.label: Optional redemption
items.text: Before 15-Mar-2028: 100% plus make-whole; up to 40% with certain equity offering proceeds at the indenture price. From 15-Mar-2028: indenture redemption prices (not disclosed; seed first call price 103.38 = par plus half a coupon, unverified). Change of control put at 101%.

items.label: Escrow feature
items.text: At closing the issuer deposited cash equal to the gross proceeds into a segregated escrow account with Goldman Sachs Bank USA (separate from the Project Accounts) until release conditions were met. The 10-K says the escrow release condition was satisfied and a release certificate delivered on 18-Jun-2026.

items.label: Trustee / collateral agent
items.text: Wilmington Trust, National Association.

items.label: ISIN / CUSIP
items.text: Seed: ISIN US03772CAA18, CUSIP 03772CAA1 (144A). Not confirmed in any official document; no Reg S identifiers found.

items.label: Governing law, denominations, clearing
items.text: Not stated in the 8-K; indenture exhibit not read in full.

items.label: Borrower chain
items.text: Applied Digital Corporation -> (Macquarie-preferred APLD HPC TopCo 2 LLC, inferred) -> APLD FAR Holdings LLC (direct parent) -> APLD ComputeCo 2 LLC (issuer) -> guarantors. The 10-K says Macquarie's preferred funding included $450mm for Polaris Forge 2, so the FAR chain appears to sit under TopCo 2 (inference).

items.label: Subsidiary guarantors
items.text: APLD FAR-01 HoldCo LLC, FAR-02 HoldCo LLC, FAR-01 LLC, FAR-02 LLC, FAR-01 LandCo LLC and FAR-02 LandCo LLC (majority-owned per the 10-Q). FAR-01 and FAR-02 are also the lessors under the Oracle lease. Applied Digital Corporation is not a guarantor of the notes.

items.label: Ring-fencing
items.text: Indenture limits business to the Polaris Forge 2 facilities and certain additional projects; limits affiliate dealings, debt, liens and restricted payments. Separate SPV chain from ComputeCo / ComputeCo 3.

items.label: Structure in words
items.text: Single-tenant, two-building (about 150 MW each, 200 MW leased) campus owned through lessor SPVs (FAR-01, FAR-02) that guarantee a holdco-level issuer; escrowed proceeds funded construction after release.

items.label: Sponsor
items.text: Applied Digital Corporation (NASDAQ: APLD): 1,410 MW contracted over five campuses, $6.4bn debt and $3.7bn cash/restricted cash at 31-Aug-2026, only 250 MW live (all at Polaris Forge 1).

items.label: Parent financing relevant to PF2
items.text: $50mm Macquarie Equipment Capital bridge to APLD FAR-01 (8% PIK, drawn Sept 2025, repaid 28-Nov-2025 with a 1.10x return hurdle) funded land, transformers and early works at Harwood; Macquarie Asset Management preferred: $450mm of the Nov-2025 draw earmarked for completing Polaris Forge 2.

items.label: Macquarie preferred (TopCo 2)
items.text: About $1.8bn funded of up to $5.0bn (plus $4.9bn remaining right); 12.75% PIK/cash preferred with 15% of common; carried at about $2.0bn at 31-Aug-2026. Terms: perpetual, company call after year 5, Macquarie put after year 7 or on sale, 1.8x MOIC floor.

items.label: Other parent facilities
items.text: $430mm secured revolver, $450mm 2.75% converts due 2030, Series G preferred line up to $2.0bn, Base Electron guarantee (~$2.4bn contract; $50mm/$100mm termination fee).

items.label: Tenant
items.text: Oracle, per Applied Digital's 8-K ('currently leased to Oracle'). Company elsewhere describes the tenant only as a U.S.-based investment-grade hyperscaler. The contracting Oracle entity, any Oracle Corporation guaranty and Oracle's credit ratings were not found in the sources reviewed.

items.label: Lessors and date
items.text: Lease dated about 20-Oct-2025 (announced 22-Oct-2025) between APLD FAR-01 LLC / APLD FAR-02 LLC and the hyperscaler for 200 MW critical IT, phased across two buildings.

items.label: Term and options
items.text: About 15 years base term plus two five-year renewal options (all other Applied Digital leases have three).

items.label: Contract value
items.text: Approximately $5.0bn base-term contracted revenue per the 10-K ($4.8bn in the June-2026 deck chart; sponsor model sums to $4.66bn over 2026-2040). Differences likely reflect pass-throughs, ramp and rounding.

items.label: Rent and escalator
items.text: Model revenue $232mm (2027), $274mm (2028), $281mm (2029), $288mm (2030): about $1.4mm per MW per year on 200 MW in 2029 with a 2.5% annual escalator (company model; derived, includes any recoveries). Seed: $1.34mm/MW and 2.5% (consistent, unverified).

items.label: Lease form
items.text: Company describes its leases as 15-year, take-or-pay, non-cancellable gross modified leases; termination for convenience requires payment of the full remaining contract value. Company expects 86% (+/-3%) site NOI margin for PF2.

items.label: Commencement
items.text: Model assumes FAR-01 Phase 1 commencement 1-Oct-2026 and FAR-02 Phase 1 commencement 1-Mar-2027. Company guidance: initial ready for service 2H CY2026, full capacity early CY2027. Seed: Nov-2026 to Jun-2027.

items.label: Expansion rights
items.text: The hyperscaler holds a first right of refusal on an additional 800 MW at the Harwood campus (full 1 GW potential), per company.

items.label: Delay / termination / SLA / assignment terms
items.text: Not disclosed publicly. 10-K risk factor: lessees may have the right to terminate leases for significant construction delays. Completion guarantee references the lease 'Outside Completion Date' (as extendable).

items.label: Location
items.text: Harwood, North Dakota (campus designated 'Polaris Forge 2', 300 MW critical-IT campus under construction with 200 MW leased).

items.label: Buildings and design
items.text: Two 150 MW standard-design buildings (PF2-1, PF2-2): ~907,500 sq ft, six data halls per building, hybrid liquid/air cooling, N+1 substation, diesel backup, 625 W/sq ft, 1.15 target PUE (company reference spec).

items.label: Cost per MW
items.text: Company expects capex $11-13mm per MW. Seed facility cost $2.39bn / $12.0mm per MW and 80% debt-funded (unverified, within range).

items.label: Groundbreaking
items.text: Groundbreaking 18-Aug-2025 on an initial 200 MW data center.

items.label: Power supply
items.text: Serving utility, interconnection agreement and any dedicated power for Harwood are not named in the filings reviewed. Company says each contracted MW is backed by land under control and/or an executed utility power agreement and cites about 2.15 GW of gross grid-connected utility power for the contracted portfolio.

items.label: Regional context
items.text: Base Electron (related party, ~10% owned by Applied Digital) plans ~1.2 GW of gas generation in North Dakota (MISO) with a PPA signed Oct 2026; relevant to expansion at the campus, not to the 200 MW leased capacity.

items.label: Status at 16-Oct-2026
items.text: Two PF2 buildings under construction. As of the 7-Oct-2026 10-Q, initial ready-for-service is expected in 2H CY2026 and full capacity in early CY2027; company expects initial PF2 operations to lift delivered North Dakota capacity to 300 MW (from 250 MW today) by end of calendar 2026. No PF2 ready-for-service announcement was found as of 16-Oct-2026.

items.label: Versus model
items.text: The March-2026 model assumed FAR-01 Phase 1 commencement on 1-Oct-2026; that date has passed without a reported ready-for-service, so first rent is running behind the illustrative assumption (contractual dates unknown).

items.label: Contractor / contract type
items.text: EPC contractor and GMP/fixed-price terms are not disclosed in the filings reviewed.

items.label: Completion guarantee
items.text: Applied Digital must fund the issuer as needed to complete the Construction Period and, where applicable, achieve the first Service Commencement Date before the Outside Completion Date (as extended under the lease) if note proceeds and available funds are insufficient.

items.label: Capex funding
items.text: Notes of $2.15bn at 98 (about $2.1bn net) after escrow release 18-Jun-2026, plus Macquarie-funded equity ($450mm earmarked) and parent equity of $0.75mm per MW (company contribution requirement under the Macquarie agreement).

items.label: Sources and uses
items.text: Uses per 8-K: development and construction of 200 MW of critical IT load at Polaris Forge 2 plus Project Accounts (incl. DSRA) and expenses. A full sources-and-uses table was not published.

items.label: Reserve
items.text: Model note: an additional Debt Service Reserve Account of $148mm to be maintained throughout the notes (excluded from DSCR calculations); upfront fee assumed 1.25%; opex ~$3mm in year 1; initial maintenance capex begins eight years after commencement.

items.label: Leverage and coverage (model)
items.text: Model NOI $249mm (2029) and $256mm (2030) versus $2,150mm notes gives about 8.6x / 8.4x (estimate; seed 9.1x). Cash flow available for debt service against interest plus amortization is about 1.0x in 2027-2029 and about 1.07x in 2030 (estimate), with small DSRA draws/replenishments.

items.label: Maturity / refinancing
items.text: About $1.75bn (roughly 81%) due 15-Mar-2031, when the lease still has about 10 years left; refinancing risk is a core part of the trade.

items.label: Market value
items.text: 10-Q (level 2) fair value of about $2.0bn at 31-Aug-2026 versus $2.2bn at 31-May-2026 on $2.15bn principal, i.e. roughly 91-95 from about 102 (both rounded to $0.1bn). Seed: 15-Sep yield 7.93%, spread 314 bp.

items.label: Parent support
items.text: Completion guarantee only; no parent guarantee of the notes or of rent. Applied Digital Corporation does guarantee its subsidiaries' obligations to tenants in other leases (CoreWeave) - whether the same applies to the PF2 lease was not found.

items.label: Tenant support
items.text: No parent guaranty of the lease found; a termination fee equal to remaining rent is described generically for the portfolio.

items.label: Reserves
items.text: DSRA $148mm (model) plus escrow mechanism before release.

items.label: Replacement-tenant rights
items.text: Not disclosed.

items.label: Covenants
items.text: Limits on debt, restricted payments, investments, liens, asset sales, sale-leasebacks, unrelated business, affiliate transactions and mergers; 101% CoC put; customary events of default.

items.label: Excess cash flow
items.text: The PF2 model shows no excess cash flow offer line (contrast with the ELN-02/03 model). Lock-up and DSCR test terms not disclosed in sources reviewed.

items.label: Moody's / S&P / Fitch
items.text: Seed: Ba3 (Moody's) / NR (S&P) / BB- (Fitch). No agency release accessible; unverified.

items.label: Stated uses
items.text: Fund development and construction of 200 MW of critical IT load at Polaris Forge 2, fund Project Accounts including the DSRA, and pay fees and expenses. Net proceeds about $2.1bn.

items.label: Delivery timing
items.text: Model first-commencement date of 1-Oct-2026 appears missed; rent clock and outside dates unknown; completion guarantor is a cash-burning parent.

items.label: Tenant visibility
items.text: Tenant credit support structure (who signed, whether Oracle Corp guarantees) is undisclosed in official filings.

items.label: Balloon and thin coverage
items.text: About 81% balloon with ~1.0x modelled coverage; DSRA at $148mm.

items.label: Pricing
items.text: Fair value fell from roughly par+ to the mid-90s between May and Aug 2026; JPMorgan downgraded the credit on supply overhang.

items.label: Escrow
items.text: Proceeds sat in escrow for about three months; the release condition is not described.

items.label: Escrow release
items.text: 18-Jun-2026: escrow release condition satisfied; funds released to the issuer.

items.label: Macquarie
items.text: 29-May-2026 fourth Macquarie closing of $925mm (TopCo 2).

items.label: Construction
items.text: 10-Q: initial RFS 2H CY2026, full early CY2027; Oct-2026 release expects PF2 to lift ND capacity to 300 MW by year-end.

items.label: Sell-side / news
