CORZ.title: Core Scientific Finance I LLC 7.750% Senior Secured Notes due 15-May-2031
CORZ.headline: A $3.3bn five-year 144A/Reg S senior secured issue by a ring-fenced Core Scientific subsidiary, secured on five Core Scientific data-center sites (TX, GA, OK, NC) licensed to CoreWeave under 12-year colocation agreements (about 590 MW leased, 395 MW billing at 30 Jun 2026). Parent Core Scientific gives an uncapped completion guarantee on four sites but does not guarantee the notes, so holders rely on CoreWeave-family rent, a cash DSRA and a large balloon (about $2.5bn, 77%) due May 2031. Spreads are wide because the sole tenant, CoreWeave, was itself sold off to distressed yields on 14-16 Oct 2026.

items.label: Issuer
items.text: Core Scientific Finance I LLC, a wholly-owned indirect subsidiary of Core Scientific, Inc. (NASDAQ: CORZ).

items.label: Notes title / size
items.text: 7.750% Senior Secured Notes due 2031; $3,300mm aggregate principal issued 6 May 2026 (priced 22 Apr 2026 at 99.250% of par); estimated net proceeds about $3.24bn after discounts and expenses.

items.label: Coupon and dates
items.text: 7.750% p.a., semi-annual in arrears on 15 May and 15 Nov, first payment 15 Nov 2026. Maturity 15 May 2031. Day count not stated in the 8-K (30/360 is the market norm; not verified).

items.label: ISIN / CUSIP
items.text: Seed shows ISIN US21874LAA08, CUSIP 21874LAA0 (144A). Not shown in the 8-K or indenture text; no Reg S ISIN found.

items.label: Ranking and security
items.text: Senior secured. First-priority liens on substantially all assets of the Issuer and the five subsidiary guarantors (excluded property carved out), a pledge of the Issuer equity held by Core Scientific Finance Holding LLC (HoldCo), and 'Parent Collateral' (Core Scientific assets and rights subject to the ringfencing that had not yet transferred to the Issuer group).

items.label: Guarantors
items.text: Fully and unconditionally guaranteed by Core Scientific Austin LLC, Denton LLC, Dalton LLC, Marble LLC and Muskogee LLC, the Issuer's only subsidiaries at issuance. Core Scientific, Inc. does NOT guarantee the notes.

items.label: Amortization
items.text: Semi-annual installments on 15 May / 15 Nov equal to 11.50% p.a. of the issue-date principal (5.75% each half-year, about $189.75mm), starting on the First Installment Payment Date; reduced pro rata for optional/mandatory redemptions; deferred (not waived) if a Datacenter Lease Termination Event occurs.

items.label: First Installment Payment Date
items.text: First payment date at least 15 days after the later of (x) the Final Commencement Date (all lease rent-commencement conditions satisfied and full rent accruing under every Datacenter Lease) and (y) abatement of all revenue credits granted by Core Scientific to the tenant. Company's 10-Q schedule ASSUMES 15 Nov 2029.

items.label: Scheduled principal profile (derived)
items.text: Per 10-Q maturity table (assumes first installment 15 Nov 2029): $189.75mm in 2029, $379.5mm in 2030, $2,730.75mm 'thereafter' (2031). Implied balloon at the 15 May 2031 maturity is about $2.54bn (about 77% of original principal), derived by difference.

items.label: Optional redemption
items.text: Make-whole (Applicable Premium: greater of 1% or PV of the May-2028 call price plus interest to May-2028 at Treasury +50bp) before 15 May 2028; up to 40% may be redeemed with equity proceeds before then; call prices thereafter 103.875% (2028), 101.938% (2029), par (2030 and later).

items.label: Mandatory redemption / offers
items.text: Par redemption option on a Datacenter Lease Termination Event; 100% of any lease-termination payment (Datacenter Lease MRC) must be applied to redeem at par; asset-sale and casualty proceeds offered pro rata at par; change-of-control put at 101%.

items.label: Denominations
items.text: Minimum $2,000 and integral multiples of $1,000 above that.

items.label: Trustee / collateral agent
items.text: Wilmington Savings Fund Society, FSB.

items.label: Offering format
items.text: Rule 144A and Regulation S; initial purchaser representatives Morgan Stanley and J.P. Morgan.

items.label: Ownership chain
items.text: Core Scientific, Inc. -> Core Scientific Finance Holding LLC (HoldCo) -> Core Scientific Finance I LLC (Issuer) -> five property-level guarantor LLCs (Austin, Denton, Dalton, Marble, Muskogee). Notes are secured on the Issuer group assets plus HoldCo's pledge of Issuer equity.

items.label: Ring-fencing
items.text: Indenture contains a special-purpose-entity covenant, a HoldCo covenant and limits on business outside the 'Facilities' and approved additional projects; only the Issuer, its subsidiaries and HoldCo are bound by the indenture covenants. Parent and its other subsidiaries are not restricted by it.

items.label: Facilities
items.text: Austin, Denton, Dalton (incl. Dalton 3), Marble and Muskogee. Denton campus is about 64 acres.

items.label: Lease counterparty chain
items.text: Datacenter Leases are 'colocation license agreements' between Core Scientific (parent) and the Tenant, defined as CoreWeave, Inc. and permitted successors/assigns. During H1 2026 CoreWeave assigned certain license agreements to 'CW SPV', an indirect CoreWeave subsidiary, with CoreWeave remaining a primary obligor.

items.label: CW SPV assignment
items.text: 10-Q discloses the assignment to an SPV 'financing structure' and warns that practical recourse to CoreWeave would depend on its condition at the time of any default. Terms of the SPV financing are not disclosed in the filings reviewed.

items.label: Structure in words
items.text: Two layers of credit: (1) CoreWeave (via CW SPV) pays rent to the Core Scientific licensor; (2) Core Scientific, Inc. gives an uncapped completion guarantee for four projects but is not a payment guarantor. Bondholders rely on CoreWeave-family rent, the DSRA and the collateral.

items.label: Sponsor
items.text: Core Scientific, Inc. (NASDAQ: CORZ), Austin TX; converting bitcoin-mining sites to high-density colocation (HDC). Colocation was 77% of H1 2026 revenue (12% in H1 2025); self-mining 18%.

items.label: Footprint
items.text: About 2.1 GW gross utility power and about 1.3 GW leasable customer power across 11 data centers in seven states (30 Jun 2026).

items.label: Parent liquidity
items.text: Cash and equivalents $1,769.7mm at 30 Jun 2026 (vs $311.4mm at YE2025); digital assets $49.7mm; restricted cash includes the DSRA ($344.8mm).

items.label: Parent debt outside the notes
items.text: $460mm 3.00% convertible notes due Sep 2029 (conversion price about $11.00) and $625mm 0% convertible notes due 2031; $1.0bn 364-day Morgan Stanley bridge term loan (drawn Mar 2026) repaid in full 6 May 2026. New 25 Aug 2026 JPMorgan facilities: $100mm revolver plus $500mm L/C facility, first-lien on parent assets, minimum liquidity $150mm, $3.0bn minimum market cap to borrow; undrawn at closing.

items.label: Warrant liabilities
items.text: Current warrant liabilities of $1.81bn at 30 Jun 2026 (the $6.81 and $0.01 listed warrants), driving a Q2 net loss of about $1.2bn. Accounting, not cash, but signals equity-value sensitivity.

items.label: Other capital deployment
items.text: Hunt County TX land and ESA acquired 5 May 2026 for about $233mm cash (about 430 MW gross); Polaris DS LLC (Muskogee-adjacent, up to 440 MW) acquired 13 Aug 2026 for about $444.3mm cash (+$40mm if 40 MW more firm power by 31 Dec 2026).

items.label: Failed CoreWeave merger (credit context)
items.text: 7 Jul 2025 all-stock merger agreement with CoreWeave; terminated 30 Oct 2025 after Core Scientific stockholders rejected it. $21.6mm advisory costs, no termination fee. Relevance: the tenant tried to buy its landlord; the commercial relationship continued under the existing license agreements.

items.label: Tenant
items.text: CoreWeave, Inc. (NASDAQ: CRWV) and, for assigned agreements, CW SPV (indirect CoreWeave subsidiary) with CoreWeave remaining a primary obligor. CoreWeave was about 77% of Core Scientific H1 2026 revenue and is the sole colocation customer.

items.label: Contract inventory
items.text: Six colocation license agreements named in the indenture: Denton TX (26 Feb 2024), Muskogee OK (24 Jun 2024), Marble NC (3 Jun 2024), Dalton GA site 1 (3 Jun 2024), Dalton 3 GA (19 Oct 2024), Austin TX (29 Feb 2024).

items.label: Leased and billable capacity
items.text: About 590 MW of leased customer power capacity across five sites; about 395 MW billing at 30 Jun 2026; remaining about 195 MW in construction/commissioning.

items.label: Term
items.text: Initial lease terms of 12 years from commencement for contracts not yet commenced at 30 Jun 2026 (matches 10-K statement for 31 Dec 2025).

items.label: Lease type / extensions / rent per MW
items.text: Seed: modified gross, two 5-year extensions, about $1.2mm per MW per year with 3% escalator. The filings reviewed do not state extension options, rent per MW or escalator; the contract form is a 'license agreement' not a lease.

items.label: Rent commencement
items.text: Rent starts as each phase is delivered; deferred revenue of $287mm at 30 Jun 2026 includes customer prepayments for capacity not yet delivered. Notes amortization is keyed to the later of full rent commencement and abatement of all revenue credits (SLA/delay credits) owed to the tenant.

items.label: Termination / replacement mechanics (indenture)
items.text: A 'Datacenter Lease Termination Event' is any Datacenter Lease ceasing to be in effect. It becomes an Event of Default if no Qualifying Datacenter Lease is signed within 6 months (extendable to 12 months if an LOI is signed, the DSRA is fully funded, no discretionary distributions are made, opex is covered and any termination payment sits in the Designated Account).

items.label: Qualifying Tenant test
items.text: NVIDIA, Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Oracle or Meta (or controlled affiliates); or a listed hyperscaler/tech company with EV or market cap of at least $50bn; or a tenant with a qualifying backstop; or holder-majority approval. Rating Agency Confirmation from two agencies is also required. CoreWeave itself is NOT on the named list.

items.label: Third-party credit support
items.text: None identified in the filings reviewed (no Microsoft/NVIDIA/Meta guarantee of the CoreWeave licenses).

items.label: Assignment / sublease
items.text: Assignment to CW SPV occurred in 2026 with CoreWeave remaining primary obligor; further assignment/sublease rights not disclosed.

items.label: Sites and states
items.text: Austin TX, Denton TX, Dalton GA (two sites incl. Dalton 3), Marble NC, Muskogee OK. The completion guarantee covers Dalton, Denton, Marble and Muskogee but not Austin.

items.label: Critical IT MW
items.text: About 590 MW leased to CoreWeave across the five sites (seed also 590 MW). Per-site MW split not found in the filings reviewed.

items.label: Denton power
items.text: Existing 297 MW approved by ERCOT as longstanding existing load (Base Load, Pathway (a), energized before 25 Mar 2022) and not subject to Batch Zero allocation; additional 74 MW validated in ERCOT's 2025 Regional Transmission Plan and also outside Batch Zero.

items.label: Cost / capex per MW
items.text: Seed: facility cost about $5.5bn, about $9.3mm per critical MW, debt about 56% of cost. Offering memorandum not accessible; the indenture refers to a 'Full Budgeted Cost of Construction' but the figure was not located in the text reviewed.

items.label: What the notes finance
items.text: Net proceeds funded the debt service reserve account and a distribution to Core Scientific; remaining build-out is funded from other available funds with parent completion support.

items.label: Nearby/adjacent growth sites (not part of the collateral unless added)
items.text: Hunt County TX (about 430 MW gross, ERCOT stability study approved, construction started), Pecos TX (existing 300 MW Base Load pathway (b) plus 300 MW Studied Load), Polaris DS adjacent to Muskogee (up to 440 MW).

items.label: Grid status
items.text: Texas sites are ERCOT-connected; Denton's existing 297 MW is classified as longstanding existing load (not subject to Batch Zero). Power arrangements for Dalton GA, Marble NC, Muskogee OK and Austin TX were not described in the filings reviewed.

items.label: ERCOT Batch Zero
items.text: Pecos and Hunt classifications are conditional (final allocation and load ramp only after Batch Zero concludes); Denton is outside the process. Conditionality is therefore a parent-growth risk more than a risk to the Denton collateral.

items.label: Utility credit support
items.text: The Aug 2026 $500mm L/C facility is intended to provide credit support for project obligations under utility agreements.

items.label: Status at 30 Jun 2026
items.text: 395 MW billing vs 590 MW leased; about 195 MW still in construction and commissioning. Timing depends on equipment lead times, labor, permitting, interconnection sequencing and customer deployment pace.

items.label: Completion guarantee
items.text: Uncapped completion guarantee from Core Scientific, Inc. to fund the Issuer as needed to complete the Projects (Dalton, Denton, Marble, Muskogee; not Austin). Backed by a security interest in Parent Collateral. Not a guarantee of the notes.

items.label: Schedule
items.text: Seed: construction from mid-2024, lease commencement late 2024 to early 2027. Official final commencement date not stated; the 10-Q's amortization assumption of 15 Nov 2029 implies the company does not expect the first installment before then.

items.label: Contractor / contract type
items.text: EPC contractor and contract type not found in the filings reviewed.

items.label: Delay economics
items.text: Revenue credits to the tenant for late delivery must be abated before amortization starts (see First Installment Payment Date), so construction slippage delays principal repayment and raises the refinancing balloon.

items.label: Notes
items.text: $3.3bn issued at 99.25 (OID about $24.8mm; issuance costs $42.0mm); effective interest rate 8.3%.

items.label: Debt service reserve
items.text: Funded at issue; $344.8mm on deposit at 30 Jun 2026 (indenture construction-period requirement uses a $343mm estimate plus next-interest and first-installment components).

items.label: Use of proceeds flow
items.text: Notes -> DSRA + distribution to Parent -> Parent repaid the $1.0bn Morgan Stanley delayed-draw bridge in full on 6 May 2026 (loss on extinguishment $5.4mm).

items.label: Leverage at issuance
items.text: Seed: 5.7x at issuance, 3.8x at maturity, debt 56% of cost. Not derivable from filings reviewed.

items.label: Amortization profile and refi risk
items.text: About $759mm of installments (23%) before maturity incl. the May 2031 installment per the 10-Q schedule; seed shows 23.6%, consistent. Roughly $2.5bn due at maturity; refinancing depends on CoreWeave-family credit and the replacement-lease market.

items.label: Parent-level obligations
items.text: Parent has $1.085bn convertibles due 2029/2031 and new revolver/L/C lines; these sit outside the ring-fence, but the parent is also the completion-guarantee provider, so parent liquidity matters.

items.label: Completion guarantee
items.text: Uncapped, from Core Scientific, Inc., four of five sites (not Austin); security interest in Parent Collateral.

items.label: Debt service reserve
items.text: Cash DSRA sized to cover interest plus the next installment (during construction: net of expected project revenue).

items.label: Lease replacement protection
items.text: Replacement within 6-12 months with a Qualifying Tenant plus ratings confirmation or event of default; amortization deferred and par-call right during the cure window.

items.label: Tenant parent support
items.text: No third-party guarantee of the licenses found; CoreWeave named as primary obligor even after assignment to CW SPV.

items.label: Termination payments
items.text: Datacenter Lease MRC (monthly recurring payments on a lease termination, incl. liquidated amounts) must be used to redeem notes at par.

items.label: Negative covenants
items.text: Limits on additional debt, restricted payments, investments, liens, asset sales, sale-leasebacks, non-project operations, amendment/termination of key agreements, affiliate transactions and mergers; customary events of default incl. cross-default to material debt and judgment default.

items.label: Restricted payments
items.text: After the Final Commencement Date, distributions limited to 30% of trailing four-quarter Net Operating Income plus (Full Budgeted Cost of Construction minus notes issued at the issue date); tax distributions allowed only if the DSRA is at its required level.

items.label: Cash waterfall
items.text: Project accounts incl. Revenue Account, DSRA and Designated Account (termination fees); waterfall set out in Section 4.23. Order of priorities not extracted.

items.label: Debt Service Coverage Ratio
items.text: Defined as estimated forward four-quarter NOI over required debt service (good-faith Issuer estimate). No lock-up ratio level located in the sections reviewed.

items.label: Reporting
items.text: Quarterly financials within 60 days (75 days for Q2 2026, Q3 2026 and Q1 2027), annual within 120 days (150 days for FY2026); FY2026 and FY2027 annuals may be unaudited.

items.label: Change of control
items.text: Put at 101% of principal plus accrued interest.

items.label: Seed ratings
items.text: NR / BB / BB- (Moody's / S&P / Fitch ordering as given by Barclays).

items.label: Public hint
items.text: A TradingView listing shows a BB rating for the notes without naming the agency.

items.label: Rating-agency documents
items.text: No S&P, Fitch or Moody's release was accessible; outlook, rationale and triggers are not verified. The indenture requires a Rating Agency Confirmation (two agencies) for any replacement lease.

items.label: Stated use
items.text: Fund the debt service reserve account; remainder distributed to Core Scientific; Core Scientific to use part to repay the delayed-draw term loans under its 364-day Bridge Facility.

items.label: Actual
items.text: Bridge ($1.0bn facility, Term SOFR+2.50%) repaid 6 May 2026; $344.8mm remained in the DSRA at 30 Jun 2026; Parent cash rose to $1.77bn at 30 Jun 2026.

items.label: Single-tenant concentration
items.text: All rent comes from CoreWeave-family entities (about 77% of Core Scientific revenue). CoreWeave's own bonds sold off to distressed levels on 14-16 Oct 2026 (see CRWV dossier).

items.label: SPV layering
items.text: Assignment of licenses to CW SPV adds a structural layer; recourse against CoreWeave parent depends on its financial condition.

items.label: Refinancing balloon
items.text: About $2.5bn (about 77%) due at 2031 maturity on the company's own assumed amortization start.

items.label: Delivery risk
items.text: About 195 MW still in construction at 30 Jun 2026; amortization and rent depend on full commencement and abatement of revenue credits.

items.label: Tenant-replacement test excludes CoreWeave
items.text: A replacement lease must be with a Qualifying Tenant (hyperscaler-type); CoreWeave is not itself listed, so re-letting after a CoreWeave default is a high bar.

items.label: Collateral sites now also hosting new leases
items.text: Core Scientific signed AMD leases (377 MW at Pecos, Muskogee, Hunt County) and Neocloud leases (152 MW at Auburn AL and Dalton Phase 3) on 27 Jul 2026. Muskogee and Dalton are notes collateral sites; whether these are inside the Issuer ring-fence, additional projects or outside is NOT disclosed in what I reviewed.

items.label: Parent equity / warrants
items.text: Large warrant liabilities and the AMD warrant (up to 30mm shares at $23.47) create dilution and accounting volatility but do not affect the notes directly.

items.label: Mining wind-down
items.text: Self-mining is being wound down; $266.5mm impairment in H1 2026; Block contract termination loss $41.9mm.

items.label: AMD relationship
items.text: 27-28 Jul 2026: 15-year leases with AMD for 377 MW (Pecos, Muskogee, Hunt County) and with a Neocloud for 152 MW (Auburn, Dalton 3), each with three 5-year options; AMD has capacity reservation rights for up to 1,925 MW more through 28 Dec 2028; AMD warrant for up to 30mm shares at $23.47 vesting 12,222 shares per MW (about 6.5mm vested at signing). Company describes potential for up to 2.5 GW with a roughly 530 MW anchor.

items.label: Q2 2026 results
items.text: Colocation 77% of H1 revenue; billable 395 MW of 590 MW leased; $1.77bn cash; net loss about $1.2bn in Q2 on warrant revaluation.

items.label: Polaris DS acquisition closed
items.text: 13 Aug 2026, about $444.3mm cash, up to 440 MW of utility power next to Muskogee.

items.label: Credit facilities
items.text: 25 Aug 2026: $100mm revolver + $500mm L/C facility (JPMorgan agent), undrawn.

items.label: ERCOT update
items.text: 10 Sep 2026: Denton outside Batch Zero; Pecos and Hunt conditionally approved.

items.label: Tenant stress
items.text: 14-16 Oct 2026: CoreWeave bonds trade at distressed levels (see CRWV dossier). No Core Scientific response found in filings as of 16 Oct 2026.

Marble NC and Dalton GA site 1 license agreements; Muskogee OK dated 24 Jun 2024; Dalton 3 dated 19 Oct 2024

EDGCOM.title: Edged Compute LLC 7.500% Senior Secured Notes due 2031 (144A/Reg S)
EDGCOM.headline: $1.3bn 5-year senior secured notes of Edged US's SPV financing two build-to-suit data centers: Aurora (Chicago) IL, 72MW, leased 16 years to CoreWeave on a triple-net lease (about 60% of capacity), and Atlanta GA, 42MW, leased 15 years to Alibaba Cloud on a modified-gross lease guaranteed by Alibaba Group Services (about 40%). Fitch expected BB-/Stable, capped by CoreWeave and constrained by US sanctions risk on Alibaba; the notes balloon in 2031 against 15-16 year leases. Both buildings are expected live in H1 2027.

items.label: Issuer
items.text: Edged Compute LLC, wholly owned indirect subsidiary of EDC Venture LLC (Edged US).

items.label: Notes
items.text: $1.3bn 7.500% Senior Secured Notes due 2031, Rule 144A / Regulation S; issued 21-Apr-2026. Seed issue date 29-Apr-2026 equals the law-firm announcement date.

items.label: Tenor / maturity
items.text: Five-year tenor maturing 2031 (Fitch). Seed gives 30-Apr-2031 (exact day unverified).

items.label: Security
items.text: First lien on all assets, contracts and cash flows of the issuer and subsidiaries, subject to excluded assets.

items.label: Pricing / call
items.text: Seed: first call 30-Apr-2028 at 103.75; pricing/yield not found. Make-whole and redemption schedule not seen.

items.label: ISIN / CUSIP
items.text: Seed: ISIN US28002AAA43, CUSIP 28002AAA4 (144A); not verified against an official document. Reg S identifiers not found.

items.label: Amortization
items.text: Fitch: initial-term cash flows fully amortize the debt after refinancing; rating-case average DSCR over the amortization years 2030-2031 is 1.11x, implying amortization starts around 2030. Seed: starts late 2029, ~6.6% of principal repaid by maturity (so ~93% balloon). Schedule not seen.

items.label: Trustee, law, denominations
items.text: Not found (indenture not public).

items.label: Borrower
items.text: Edged Compute LLC finances two build-to-suit sites, Aurora (Chicago) IL and Atlanta GA, under one issuer (Edged calls it the first bond of its kind for multi-site, multi-customer development).

items.label: Ring-fencing
items.text: SPE covenants: separateness, no commingling, no guarantee of parent obligations, business limited to developing and operating these facilities.

items.label: Parent
items.text: EDC Venture LLC (Edged US) is the parent; Edged's wider platform (Council Bluffs 200MW etc.) is financed separately, e.g. a construction loan with TD Securities and Credit Agricole CIB as coordinating lead arrangers.

items.label: Edged US
items.text: Data center developer, cofounded by Koch and entrepreneur Jakob Carnemark; CEO Bryant Farland. Campuses in Atlanta, Chicago/Aurora, Columbus, Dallas, Des Moines, Kansas City, Phoenix and Council Bluffs.

items.label: Capital raised
items.text: About $2bn of financing year-to-date to 28-May-2026, including these notes.

items.label: Sale process
items.text: A July 2026 report says Koch Real Estate Investments is exploring a sale at about $15bn; no deal reported. Unconfirmed secondary source.

items.label: Operating history
items.text: Fitch flags Edged's limited operating history and the sponsors' limited refinancing record as weaknesses.

items.label: Chicago (Aurora IL, ORD01-2)
items.text: 72MW IT (about 60% of capacity). Tenant CoreWeave Inc. (Fitch BB-/Positive). Lease type NNN plus an operating agreement. 16-year term, two 5-year renewals. Tenant maintains and replaces mechanical and electrical equipment.

items.label: Atlanta (ATL01-3)
items.text: 42MW IT (about 40%). Tenant Alibaba Cloud LLC (unrated). Modified gross (MG+E). 15-year term, two 5-year renewals. Lease unconditionally guaranteed by Alibaba Group Services Limited (unrated).

items.label: Reconciliation to Barclays
items.text: Seed split (CoreWeave Chicago NNN 16 yrs; Alibaba Atlanta MG 15 yrs; 72MW + 42MW = 114MW) is confirmed by Fitch. Barclays' 'Chicago IL' is Aurora, Illinois. The 'two 5-year extensions' apply to both leases.

items.label: Rent
items.text: Fitch does not disclose rent. Seed: $1.71mm per MW per year, 3.0% escalator (Fitch models 3% annual escalations). Re-leasing stress uses $125/kW per month (=$1.5mm/MW/yr).

items.label: Service levels / termination
items.text: Tenants may receive outage or service credits against rent. Atlanta lease gives the tenant termination rights for sustained critical deficiencies; in Chicago SLA-linked termination is limited to the operations agreement.

items.label: Delay remedies
items.text: Atlanta: no tenant termination right for late delivery. Chicago: rent credits begin after a 30-day grace period; outside termination date 270 days, extended for permitting, supply-chain or utility delays.

items.label: Pass-through of power
items.text: Power costs are passed through to tenants at both sites.

items.label: Tenant disclosure
items.text: Edged and the law-firm releases do not name tenants; Aurora is described only as fully pre-leased. Names come from Fitch. Neither CoreWeave 10-Q nor any Alibaba filing was found describing the leases.

items.label: Chicago site
items.text: Aurora, IL, 2835 Bilter Road: second building on Edged's Chicago campus (first facility opened Feb 2025). 72MW critical capacity, waterless closed-loop ThermalWorks cooling, liquid-to-chip above 200kW per rack. Topped out Jun 2026.

items.label: Atlanta site
items.text: ATL01-3: 42MW critical capacity on the 169MW Atlanta campus (three buildings, all reported fully leased). Topped out; operational early 2027.

items.label: Cost
items.text: Fitch: total project cost $1.63bn, which it states implies about 71% loan-to-cost for the notes. Note the arithmetic: $1.3bn / $1.63bn is about 80%; the 71% (also the seed's 'debt-funded' figure) would imply ~$1.83bn. Reconcile before use. Seed cost per MW $14.3mm.

items.label: What the notes finance
items.text: Development and construction of the two data centers (Atlanta and Aurora).

items.label: Atlanta
items.text: Substation substantially complete and expected to be energized by May 2026; energy services agreement with Georgia Power (A-/Stable) executed (Fitch, Apr 2026). Energization after that date not verified.

items.label: Chicago
items.text: CAIC agreement with ComEd nearly final at the time of rating; substation construction started under a separate agreement; no ESA executed. Power can be bought directly from ComEd and passed through. Fitch rates supply risk Weaker.

items.label: Contractors
items.text: Brasfield & Gorrie (Atlanta), FCL Builders (Chicago); fixed-price GMP contracts; about 90% of owner-furnished equipment procured (Fitch, Apr 2026).

items.label: Schedule
items.text: Atlanta ATL01-3 operational early 2027; Aurora Q2 2027. Fitch: each phase has two to three months of headroom vs lease-required dates. Seed lease commencement: Atlanta Jan-Jun 2027, Chicago May-Dec 2027.

items.label: Cost protection
items.text: Chicago lease has a yield-on-cost mechanism passing certain cost increases to rent, subject to a cap. No completion guarantee mentioned in Fitch's text.

items.label: Sources and uses
items.text: $1.3bn notes plus sponsor equity against $1.63bn total project cost (Fitch); equity amount not disclosed. Seed: 71% debt-funded, leverage 7.4x at issuance and 6.0x at maturity (unverified).

items.label: Refinancing
items.text: Notes mature 2031 before the 15-16 year leases; Fitch assumes ~$319mm of additional debt in 2031 (85% LTC limit) and rates debt structure Weaker because of refinancing risk. PLCR at refinancing 1.18x base, 1.14x rating case.

items.label: DSRA
items.text: Funded at closing with six months of debt service.

items.label: Metrics
items.text: Base case average DSCR 1.43x (2027-2031); rating case 1.42x, and 1.11x over the amortization years 2030-2031; Alibaba-sanctions scenario about 1.18x average and near 1.00x in 2030-2031 (PLCR 1.03x).

items.label: Alibaba guarantee
items.text: Alibaba Group Services Limited (unrated) unconditionally guarantees the Atlanta lease; sanctions on Alibaba entities would be the main stress (Fitch).

items.label: Chicago
items.text: No guarantee beyond CoreWeave itself; Fitch caps the rating at CoreWeave's profile because it does not give credit for replacing CoreWeave in a tenant-bankruptcy scenario.

items.label: Replacement tenant
items.text: If a lease terminates (including from a sanctions event), a replacement tenant may be an unrated counterparty with market cap above $50bn, subject to rating confirmation from two agencies.

items.label: Debt incurrence
items.text: Additional debt permitted up to 85% LTC pari passu or 95% non-pari passu, with a good-faith NOI-covers-debt-service test; Fitch views several provisions as weaker than standard project finance.

items.label: Other
items.text: Mergers, reinvestment of casualty/asset-sale proceeds and JVs permitted without rating confirmation. Full waterfall, lock-up and EoD terms not seen.

items.label: Fitch
items.text: BB-(EXP), Stable (committee 9-Apr-2026; release 21-Apr-2026). Final rating depended on final documents; final Fitch release not found. Downgrade: CoreWeave below BB-, delays beyond lease-allowed times, DSCR/PLCR below 1.10x (e.g. Alibaba restricted-party designation). Upgrade: CoreWeave above BB-, PLCR above 1.15x and very low sanctions risk.

items.label: S&P
items.text: Seed shows BB+; no S&P document found. Note S&P rates CoreWeave B+ (positive) in press, so a BB+ on a deal with a CoreWeave-leased 60% share would be unusual; treat as unverified.

items.label: Moody's
items.text: Not rated per seed (NR).

items.label: Uses
items.text: Fund construction of the Atlanta (ATL01-3) and Aurora (ORD01-2) data centers; DSRA funded at closing.

items.label: CoreWeave concentration
items.text: About 60% of capacity is leased to CoreWeave and Fitch's rating is capped at CoreWeave (BB-/Positive).

items.label: Alibaba sanctions
items.text: Fitch sees low-to-medium likelihood, moderate-impact US sanctions risk on Alibaba Group as the main rating constraint; Alibaba stress cuts 2030-31 DSCR to ~1.0x.

items.label: Atlanta termination rights
items.text: Atlanta tenant can terminate for sustained critical deficiencies; Chicago has rent credits and a 270-day outside date.

items.label: Power
items.text: Both sites depend on new substations; Chicago has no executed ESA and the CAIC with ComEd was unsigned at rating.

items.label: Refinancing and operator
items.text: 2031 balloon and a sponsor with limited operating and refinancing record.

items.label: Sponsor sale
items.text: Reported Koch-led sale process could change ownership; no covenant detail seen on change of control.

items.label: Aurora topped out
items.text: 72MW building topped out and described as fully pre-leased; operations due Q2 2027 (9-Jun-2026).

items.label: Financing
items.text: Edged announced nearly $2bn of financing YTD on 28-May-2026.

items.label: Sale report
items.text: Koch exploring sale at ~$15bn reported 28-Jul-2026 (unconfirmed).

items.label: Market level
items.text: Seed: 9.30% yield / +453bp on 15-Sep-2026 (Barclays).

Rent per MW ($1.71mm), cost per MW, leverage 7.4x/6.0x, 6.6% amortization and call price 103.75 are seed-only. Rent by site is not disclosed, so the split of revenue between CoreWeave and Alibaba cannot be quantified (Fitch gives 60/40 by MW only).
Discrepancy to resolve: Fitch says $1.63bn cost implies ~71% LTC, but $1.3bn / $1.63bn is ~80%. Either cost is higher (~$1.83bn) or the 71% refers to something else.

TRACTC.title: SV RNO Property Owner 1, LLC 5.875% Senior Secured Notes due 1-Mar-2031
TRACTC.headline: Project-finance 144A notes ($3.8bn) funding a 200 MW critical-IT turnkey data center and substation in Storey County, NV, 100% leased on a 197-month triple net lease to an unnamed AA- tenant reported by Bloomberg to be NVIDIA. Credit rests on the lease and construction/power delivery, not NVIDIA recourse; NVIDIA's 10-Q flags $20bn of leases to be reassigned to third parties without naming Fleet. The NV Energy v. Tract suit concerns the South Valley and Peru Shelf power agreements, a headline risk for energization even though the issuer is not a named party in coverage seen.

items.label: Issuer
items.text: SV RNO Property Owner I, LLC (Bloomberg: SV RNO Property Owner 1), subsidiary of Fleet Data Centers I, LP; equity held through SV RNO HoldCo, LLC.

items.label: Notes
items.text: 5.875% Senior Secured Notes due 1-Mar-2031

items.label: Principal
items.text: $3.8bn original principal (upsized); seed outstanding $3,800mm

items.label: ISIN / CUSIP (144A)
items.text: US78488XAA28 / CUSIP 78488XAA2 (seed)

items.label: Coupon
items.text: 5.875% p.a., semi-annual cash, Mar 1 / Sep 1, first payment 1-Sep-2026

items.label: Issue / closing date
items.text: Priced 13-Feb-2026; delivery expected on/about 24-Feb-2026 (closing release dated 24-Feb)

items.label: Amortization
items.text: Release states 2.500% of original principal, paid semi-annually (wording ambiguous; seed estimates ~8.2% cumulative by maturity from mid-2028, unverified).

items.label: Ranking and security
items.text: Senior secured; first-priority liens on substantially all issuer assets and on issuer equity held by SV RNO HoldCo, LLC.

items.label: Call / redemption
items.text: Seed: next call 1-Mar-2028 at 102.94; make-whole and schedule not verified.

items.label: Offering format
items.text: Rule 144A / Regulation S private placement, not SEC-registered; delivery via DTC.

items.label: Trustee, governing law, denominations
items.text: Not found; offering memorandum and indenture are private.

items.label: Chain
items.text: Fleet Data Centers I, LP -> SV RNO HoldCo, LLC -> SV RNO Property Owner I, LLC (issuer).

items.label: Ring-fencing / guarantors
items.text: Notes secured by first liens on substantially all issuer assets and a pledge of issuer equity held by the HoldCo. Detailed guarantor and separateness provisions not available (no indenture).

items.label: Naming
items.text: Press releases style the issuer 'Property Owner I'; Bloomberg/Cahill style it 'Property Owner 1'. Same entity.

items.label: Sponsor
items.text: Fleet Data Centers is a portfolio company of Tract Capital (Denver); Fleet describes itself as developer/operator of mega-scale single-user campuses and its team as having built/operated 1,000+ data centers.

items.label: Tract land position
items.text: Tract owns roughly 12,000+ acres in northern Nevada (about 12,390 acres across five owned/in-development sites per RGJ), including Peru Shelf Technology Park in TRIC.

items.label: Other Fleet/Tract financings
items.text: Sister Fleet notes (TRACTD, PR RNO Property Owner 1) finance a second 200 MW critical IT project with the same tenant description. Project-name mapping (SV = South Valley, PR = Peru Ridge) is an inference from naming and coverage, not confirmed by an official document.

items.label: Sponsor capital
items.text: Sponsor equity amount not disclosed in public documents located. Seed leverage implies equity of about 17% (seed: 83% debt-funded) of cost.

items.label: Tenant identity (official)
items.text: Fleet press releases describe an unnamed tenant rated AA- by investment-grade agencies with market cap above $3tn; NVIDIA is not named by the issuer.

items.label: Tenant identity (reported)
items.text: Bloomberg (12-Feb-2026) reported NVIDIA would lease the Fleet/Tract site; Tract declined comment, NVIDIA did not respond. RGJ (Sep 2026) repeats that Bloomberg reported NVIDIA leasing South Valley, with neither company commenting. NVIDIA's 10-Q does not name Tract or Fleet.

items.label: Lease type and term
items.text: 100% leased, 197-month (about 16.4-year) triple net lease.

items.label: Extension options
items.text: Two 10-year extensions reported (Bloomberg-sourced).

items.label: Rent and escalator
items.text: Seed: base rent about $2.0mm per MW per year, 3.25% escalator (broker estimate).

items.label: Commencement
items.text: Seed: lease commencement Oct 2027 - Jun 2028 (broker-sourced).

items.label: Termination, delay, SLA, assignment rights
items.text: Not publicly disclosed; lease and offering memorandum not available.

items.label: 10-Q leases not commenced (26-Jul-2026)
items.text: Note 10 shows $25bn of data center leases not yet commenced for NVIDIA's own use (commence Q3 FY2027 to FY2033, terms up to 20 years) and a separate $20bn of data center leases not commenced 'for third party' (about 15-year terms, expected to commence FY2028-FY2029, subject to construction). NVIDIA states it expects to reassign these data center leases to third parties. Total not-yet-commenced $45bn.

items.label: Does it identify Tract/Fleet?
items.text: No. The 10-Q text reviewed contains no mention of Tract, Fleet, Nevada or Reno. Whether any of the $20bn third-party leases relates to these notes cannot be determined from the filing; the roughly 15-year term differs from the 197-month (16.4-year) lease here.

items.label: Guarantees
items.text: 10-Q discloses guarantees for land, power and shell for AI clouds (max gross exposure $3.5bn, $712mm partner escrow, 5-7 year terms) and, as a subsequent event in Aug 2026, SB Energy guarantees capped at $105bn tied to the Ohio PORTS campus for an OpenAI affiliate. No NVIDIA guarantee of the Fleet/Tract notes or lease is disclosed.

items.label: Fleet statement of 14-Sep-2026
items.text: Per seed, Fleet stated that NVIDIA confirmed in writing its reassignment disclosure does not refer to these projects. I could not locate this statement in any public document; treat as unverified.

items.label: Project
items.text: Turnkey data center and electrical substation, 230 MW utility capacity, 200 MW critical IT, Storey County, Nevada (Tahoe-Reno Industrial Center area).

items.label: Site size
items.text: 252 acres per Feb 2026 release (the sister PR RNO release cites 517 acres; other press cites ~256 acres for the Peru Shelf site). Conflicts unresolved.

items.label: Cost and capex per MW
items.text: Seed: facility cost about $4,400mm, about $22.0mm per MW (broker estimate).

items.label: Name mapping
items.text: Inference: SV = South Valley (RGJ: Bloomberg reported NVIDIA leasing South Valley). RGJ lists the South Valley site at 37.4 acres, which conflicts with 252 acres - unresolved.

items.label: Utility agreements
items.text: Seed says project-level NV Energy power agreements of 200 MW each. Press reports state the South Valley and Peru Ridge agreements were signed under NV Energy Rule 9 (cost allocation and construction responsibility; NV Energy says it does not address electricity supply), with Reno Power as Tract's contracting entity. The agreements are confidential and the complaint sealed; MW terms not verified.

items.label: Behind-the-meter interim power
items.text: Fleet applied in Apr 2026 to PUCN for temporary natural-gas plants: 144 MW for South Valley and 218 MW for Peru Ridge. PUCN approved on 17-Sep-2026. Each plant takes about six months to build and would run two to three years; Storey County building permit and air permit still required; construction expected early 2027.

items.label: Grid supply constraint
items.text: NV Energy says it cannot supply the loads immediately; its IRP cites about 22 GW of requested service. Fleet says growth is outpacing NV Energy's ability to build permanent large-load infrastructure. No permanent interconnection date found.

items.label: Tract infrastructure commitments
items.text: Tract says it committed nearly $1bn to NV Energy network upgrades; NV Energy demands $1bn of grid upgrades begin.

items.label: Start
items.text: Press coverage reported groundbreaking on Fleet's first Nevada facility in May 2026; seed says construction start June 2026.

items.label: Rent commencement
items.text: Seed: lease commencement Oct 2027 - Jun 2028 (broker-sourced).

items.label: EPC / contract type / completion guarantee
items.text: Not found in public documents.

items.label: Yield-on-cost feature
items.text: Seed refers to a yield-on-cost feature; no public document found describing its mechanics. Not verified.

items.label: Status at 16-Oct-2026
items.text: Construction under way per press; power depends on interim BTM plants (construction early 2027) and the unresolved NV Energy dispute.

items.label: Debt
items.text: $3.8bn original principal (upsized); seed outstanding $3,800mm

items.label: Sources and uses
items.text: Uses: part of development/construction cost, fees, debt reserves (Feb release). Equity portion and total cost not disclosed in release.

items.label: Leverage and equity (broker)
items.text: Seed: leverage 9.1x at issuance falling to 8.0x at maturity (basis not stated); 83% debt-funded.

items.label: Reserves
items.text: Proceeds fund debt reserves (size not disclosed).

items.label: Refinancing risk
items.text: Bullet balance at 2031 maturity after partial amortization; depends on lease and refinancing market.

items.label: Tenant credit
items.text: Cash flows rely on a AA- rated tenant lease (unnamed in official releases). No parent or NVIDIA guarantee disclosed.

items.label: Sponsor recourse / completion support
items.text: Not disclosed publicly.

items.label: Terms
items.text: Indenture not accessible; DSCR tests, lock-ups, events of default, restricted payments, additional-debt limits not verified.

items.label: Seed ratings
items.text: Ba1/(P)BB+/BB (Moody's/S&P/Fitch); preliminary (P) where shown. Rating agency releases not found publicly.

items.label: Rationale
items.text: Agency rationale and triggers not obtained. Ratings several notches below the AA- tenant imply construction, power, structure and lease-termination risk drive the rating (my inference).

items.label: Broker view
items.text: Barclays upgraded TRACTC to Overweight on 16-Sep-2026 (seed).

items.label: Uses
items.text: Finance part of development and construction of the project, pay fees and expenses, fund debt reserves.

items.label: NV Energy litigation
items.text: NV Energy sued Tract and Reno Power in Washoe County Second Judicial District Court (complaint titled about 24-Jul-2026, filed under seal) to stop private arbitration Tract started in June over power timing and quantity. Named projects are Peru Shelf and South Valley (Peru Ridge also referenced). Issuers are not named as parties in coverage seen, but the power agreements for these projects are the subject, so the dispute can affect energization timing. The seed's party names Tract (LandCo) I LP were not seen in coverage. South Valley is a named project and, by inference, is the SV RNO project, so TRACTC is the more directly exposed.

items.label: Litigation status
items.text: Sealing orders 10 and 24 Aug; disqualification hearing on NV Energy counsel 29-Sep (Judge Scott Freeman); media groups moved to unseal in Oct. No ruling on arbitration or injunction found.

items.label: Power delivery
items.text: Interim BTM gas plants approved 17-Sep but not yet built; air and county permits pending; public opposition at hearing.

items.label: Tenant ambiguity
items.text: Tenant unnamed officially; NVIDIA 10-Q reassign-to-third-parties language creates ambiguity; filing neither links nor excludes these projects.

items.label: Lease terms opacity
items.text: Termination and delay remedies unknown; slippage in construction or rent commencement would pressure coverage during the reserve period.

items.label: Technology/obsolescence
items.text: Single-tenant AI facility; residual value after 2031 depends on renewal or re-leasing.

items.label: Jun 2026
items.text: Tract invoked arbitration against NV Energy.

items.label: 24-Jul-2026
items.text: NV Energy filed suit (date inferred from complaint file name).

items.label: 26-Aug-2026
items.text: NVIDIA 10-Q filed with $20bn third-party leases to be reassigned language.

items.label: 14-Sep-2026
items.text: Fleet statement on NVIDIA written confirmation (seed; unverified).

items.label: 16-Sep-2026
items.text: Barclays digest: TRACTC upgrade to Overweight (seed).

items.label: 17-Sep-2026
items.text: PUCN approves temporary gas plants.

items.label: Oct 2026
items.text: Unsealing motion by media groups in NV Energy v. Tract.

TRACTD.title: PR RNO Property Owner 1, LLC 6.500% Senior Secured Notes due 1-May-2031
TRACTD.headline: Project-finance 144A notes ($4.585bn) funding a second 200 MW critical-IT turnkey data center and substation in Storey County, NV, 100% leased on a 197-month triple net lease to an unnamed AA- tenant (NVIDIA per seed). Higher leverage than TRACTC (about 91% debt-funded per seed) explains the wider spread. Credit depends on construction, power delivery (218 MW interim gas plant approved 17-Sep-2026) and the lease, while the NV Energy lawsuit touches the Peru Ridge/Peru Shelf agreements.

items.label: Issuer
items.text: PR RNO Property Owner I, LLC (Bloomberg/Cahill: PR RNO Property Owner 1, LLC), indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Fleet Data Centers I, LP; equity held through PR RNO HoldCo, LLC.

items.label: Notes
items.text: 6.500% Senior Secured Notes due 1-May-2031

items.label: Principal
items.text: $4.585bn aggregate principal per counsel (press releases round to $4.6bn, upsized)

items.label: ISIN / CUSIP (144A)
items.text: US69393LAA17 / CUSIP 69393LAA1 (seed)

items.label: Coupon
items.text: 6.500% p.a., semi-annual cash, May 1 / Nov 1, first payment 1-Nov-2026

items.label: Issue / closing date
items.text: Priced 28-Apr-2026; closed on/about 1-May-2026

items.label: Amortization
items.text: Release states annual payments of 2.500% of original principal paid semi-annually (wording ambiguous; seed estimates ~7.5% cumulative from mid-2028, unverified).

items.label: Ranking and security
items.text: Senior secured; first-priority liens on substantially all issuer assets and on issuer equity held by PR RNO HoldCo, LLC.

items.label: Call / redemption
items.text: Seed: next call 1-May-2028 at 103.25; make-whole and schedule not verified.

items.label: Offering format
items.text: Rule 144A / Regulation S private placement, not SEC-registered; delivery via DTC.

items.label: Trustee, governing law, denominations
items.text: Not found; offering memorandum and indenture are private.

items.label: Chain
items.text: Fleet Data Centers I, LP -> PR RNO HoldCo, LLC -> PR RNO Property Owner I, LLC (issuer).

items.label: Ring-fencing / guarantors
items.text: Notes secured by first liens on substantially all issuer assets and a pledge of issuer equity held by the HoldCo. Detailed guarantor and separateness provisions not available (no indenture).

items.label: Naming
items.text: Press releases style the issuer 'Property Owner I'; Bloomberg/Cahill style it 'Property Owner 1'. Same entity.

items.label: Sponsor
items.text: Fleet Data Centers is a portfolio company of Tract Capital (Denver); Fleet describes itself as developer/operator of mega-scale single-user campuses and its team as having built/operated 1,000+ data centers.

items.label: Tract land position
items.text: Tract owns roughly 12,000+ acres in northern Nevada (about 12,390 acres across five owned/in-development sites per RGJ), including Peru Shelf Technology Park in TRIC.

items.label: Other Fleet/Tract financings
items.text: Sister Fleet notes (TRACTC, SV RNO Property Owner 1) finance a second 200 MW critical IT project with the same tenant description. Project-name mapping (SV = South Valley, PR = Peru Ridge) is an inference from naming and coverage, not confirmed by an official document.

items.label: Sponsor capital
items.text: Sponsor equity amount not disclosed in public documents located. Seed leverage implies equity of about 9% (seed: 91% debt-funded) of cost.

items.label: Tenant identity (official)
items.text: Fleet press releases describe an unnamed tenant rated AA- by investment-grade agencies with market cap above $3tn; NVIDIA is not named by the issuer.

items.label: Tenant identity (reported)
items.text: Bloomberg (12-Feb-2026) reported NVIDIA would lease the Fleet/Tract site; Tract declined comment, NVIDIA did not respond. RGJ (Sep 2026) repeats that Bloomberg reported NVIDIA leasing South Valley, with neither company commenting. NVIDIA's 10-Q does not name Tract or Fleet.

items.label: Lease type and term
items.text: 100% leased, 197-month (about 16.4-year) triple net lease.

items.label: Extension options
items.text: Two 10-year extensions reported (Bloomberg-sourced).

items.label: Rent and escalator
items.text: Seed: base rent about $2.27mm per MW per year, 3.25% escalator (broker estimate).

items.label: Commencement
items.text: Seed: lease commencement Oct 2027 - Apr 2028 (broker-sourced).

items.label: Termination, delay, SLA, assignment rights
items.text: Not publicly disclosed; lease and offering memorandum not available.

items.label: 10-Q leases not commenced (26-Jul-2026)
items.text: Note 10 shows $25bn of data center leases not yet commenced for NVIDIA's own use (commence Q3 FY2027 to FY2033, terms up to 20 years) and a separate $20bn of data center leases not commenced 'for third party' (about 15-year terms, expected to commence FY2028-FY2029, subject to construction). NVIDIA states it expects to reassign these data center leases to third parties. Total not-yet-commenced $45bn.

items.label: Does it identify Tract/Fleet?
items.text: No. The 10-Q text reviewed contains no mention of Tract, Fleet, Nevada or Reno. Whether any of the $20bn third-party leases relates to these notes cannot be determined from the filing; the roughly 15-year term differs from the 197-month (16.4-year) lease here.

items.label: Guarantees
items.text: 10-Q discloses guarantees for land, power and shell for AI clouds (max gross exposure $3.5bn, $712mm partner escrow, 5-7 year terms) and, as a subsequent event in Aug 2026, SB Energy guarantees capped at $105bn tied to the Ohio PORTS campus for an OpenAI affiliate. No NVIDIA guarantee of the Fleet/Tract notes or lease is disclosed.

items.label: Fleet statement of 14-Sep-2026
items.text: Per seed, Fleet stated that NVIDIA confirmed in writing its reassignment disclosure does not refer to these projects. I could not locate this statement in any public document; treat as unverified.

items.label: Project
items.text: Turnkey data center and electrical substation, 230 MW utility capacity, 200 MW critical IT, Storey County, Nevada (Tahoe-Reno Industrial Center area).

items.label: Site size
items.text: 517-acre property in Storey County per May 2026 release and Cahill (RGJ lists the Peru Ridge plant site at 23.4 acres; conflict unresolved).

items.label: Cost and capex per MW
items.text: Seed: facility cost about $4,435mm, about $22.2mm per MW (broker estimate); $4.585bn notes vs $4.435bn cost implies reserves and sponsor reimbursement uses.

items.label: Name mapping
items.text: Inference: PR = Peru Ridge (TRIC). RGJ links NVIDIA to South Valley, not Peru Ridge; NVIDIA tenancy of PR RNO rests on the seed/Barclays.

items.label: Utility agreements
items.text: Seed says project-level NV Energy power agreements of 200 MW each. Press reports state the South Valley and Peru Ridge agreements were signed under NV Energy Rule 9 (cost allocation and construction responsibility; NV Energy says it does not address electricity supply), with Reno Power as Tract's contracting entity. The agreements are confidential and the complaint sealed; MW terms not verified.

items.label: Behind-the-meter interim power
items.text: Fleet applied in Apr 2026 to PUCN for temporary natural-gas plants: 144 MW for South Valley and 218 MW for Peru Ridge. PUCN approved on 17-Sep-2026. Each plant takes about six months to build and would run two to three years; Storey County building permit and air permit still required; construction expected early 2027.

items.label: Grid supply constraint
items.text: NV Energy says it cannot supply the loads immediately; its IRP cites about 22 GW of requested service. Fleet says growth is outpacing NV Energy's ability to build permanent large-load infrastructure. No permanent interconnection date found.

items.label: Tract infrastructure commitments
items.text: Tract says it committed nearly $1bn to NV Energy network upgrades; NV Energy demands $1bn of grid upgrades begin.

items.label: Start
items.text: Press coverage reported groundbreaking on Fleet's first Nevada facility in May 2026; seed says construction start Summer 2026.

items.label: Rent commencement
items.text: Seed: lease commencement Oct 2027 - Apr 2028 (broker-sourced).

items.label: EPC / contract type / completion guarantee
items.text: Not found in public documents.

items.label: Yield-on-cost feature
items.text: Seed refers to a yield-on-cost feature; no public document found describing its mechanics. Not verified.

items.label: Status at 16-Oct-2026
items.text: Construction under way per press; power depends on interim BTM plants (construction early 2027) and the unresolved NV Energy dispute.

items.label: Debt
items.text: $4.585bn aggregate principal per counsel (press releases round to $4.6bn, upsized)

items.label: Sources and uses
items.text: Uses: part of development/construction, reimbursement of sponsor's prior equity used to buy the property, fees, debt reserves (May release). Debt exceeds seed facility cost, consistent with sponsor reimbursement.

items.label: Leverage and equity (broker)
items.text: Seed: leverage 10.0x at issuance to 8.7x at maturity (basis not stated); 91% debt-funded, higher than TRACTC.

items.label: Reserves
items.text: Proceeds fund debt reserves (size not disclosed).

items.label: Refinancing risk
items.text: Bullet balance at 2031 maturity after partial amortization; depends on lease and refinancing market.

items.label: Tenant credit
items.text: Cash flows rely on a AA- rated tenant lease (unnamed in official releases). No parent or NVIDIA guarantee disclosed.

items.label: Sponsor recourse / completion support
items.text: Not disclosed publicly.

items.label: Terms
items.text: Indenture not accessible; DSCR tests, lock-ups, events of default, restricted payments, additional-debt limits not verified.

items.label: Seed ratings
items.text: Ba1/(P)BB/BB (Moody's/S&P/Fitch); preliminary (P) where shown. Rating agency releases not found publicly.

items.label: Rationale
items.text: Agency rationale and triggers not obtained. Ratings several notches below the AA- tenant imply construction, power, structure and lease-termination risk drive the rating (my inference).

items.label: Broker view
items.text: Barclays upgraded TRACTC to Overweight on 16-Sep-2026 (seed).

items.label: Uses
items.text: Finance part of development and construction, reimburse sponsor for prior equity contributions used to acquire the property, pay fees and expenses, fund debt reserves.

items.label: NV Energy litigation
items.text: NV Energy sued Tract and Reno Power in Washoe County Second Judicial District Court (complaint titled about 24-Jul-2026, filed under seal) to stop private arbitration Tract started in June over power timing and quantity. Named projects are Peru Shelf and South Valley (Peru Ridge also referenced). Issuers are not named as parties in coverage seen, but the power agreements for these projects are the subject, so the dispute can affect energization timing. The seed's party names Tract (LandCo) I LP were not seen in coverage. Peru Ridge is expressly cited as having a 218 MW interim behind-the-meter plant and a Rule 9 agreement; Peru Shelf (Tract land) is also named.

items.label: Litigation status
items.text: Sealing orders 10 and 24 Aug; disqualification hearing on NV Energy counsel 29-Sep (Judge Scott Freeman); media groups moved to unseal in Oct. No ruling on arbitration or injunction found.

items.label: Power delivery
items.text: Interim BTM gas plants approved 17-Sep but not yet built; air and county permits pending; public opposition at hearing.

items.label: Tenant ambiguity
items.text: Tenant unnamed officially; NVIDIA 10-Q reassign-to-third-parties language creates ambiguity; filing neither links nor excludes these projects.

items.label: Lease terms opacity
items.text: Termination and delay remedies unknown; slippage in construction or rent commencement would pressure coverage during the reserve period.

items.label: Technology/obsolescence
items.text: Single-tenant AI facility; residual value after 2031 depends on renewal or re-leasing.

items.label: Jun 2026
items.text: Tract invoked arbitration against NV Energy.

items.label: 24-Jul-2026
items.text: NV Energy filed suit (date inferred from complaint file name).

items.label: 26-Aug-2026
items.text: NVIDIA 10-Q filed with $20bn third-party leases to be reassigned language.

items.label: 14-Sep-2026
items.text: Fleet statement on NVIDIA written confirmation (seed; unverified).

items.label: 16-Sep-2026
items.text: Barclays digest: TRACTC upgrade to Overweight (seed).

items.label: 17-Sep-2026
items.text: PUCN approves temporary gas plants.

items.label: Oct 2026

FLASHC.title: Flash Compute LLC 7.250% Senior Secured Notes due 31-Dec-2030
FLASHC.headline: $1.3bn senior secured notes issued by Flash Compute LLC, the project company for the 168MW Abernathy, Texas data center that FS CS I LLC (originally TeraWulf 50.1% / Fluidstack 49.9%) is building for a 25-year lease to Fluidstack with a roughly $1.3bn Google backstop. TeraWulf sold its entire stake in July 2026 for about $530mm, leaving a Fluidstack-led owner group and a capped $100mm completion guarantee behind the notes. Because of the 2030 maturity, a balloon of several hundred million dollars remains if the lease runs as modeled.

items.label: Issuer
items.text: Flash Compute LLC, wholly owned subsidiary of FS CS I LLC (the 'JV Partners Holdco'). Subsidiary guarantor: Abernathy Data LLC.

items.label: Notes title and size
items.text: 7.250% Senior Secured Notes due 2030; $1,300mm aggregate principal issued at 100% (launched 18-Dec-2025 at $1.275bn, closed upsized at $1.3bn). Sold under a purchase agreement of 18-Dec-2025 to Morgan Stanley as representative of the initial purchasers; Rule 144A and Regulation S.

items.label: Coupon and payment dates
items.text: 7.250% per year, semiannual in arrears on 30 Jun and 31 Dec, first payment 30-Jun-2026.

items.label: Issue date and maturity
items.text: Issue Date 29-Dec-2025; maturity 31-Dec-2030.

items.label: Ranking and security
items.text: Senior secured. Collateral: capital stock of the issuer and each company party, all property of the issuer and guarantor, the Fluidstack USA III lockbox account (once established), pre-completion pledge of the JV Partners Holdco account, and during construction the warrants (as defined). Notes are not guaranteed by JV Partners Holdco.

items.label: Optional redemption
items.text: Before 31-Dec-2027: 100% plus make-whole (Applicable Premium = greater of 1.0% or PV-based amount at Treasury + 50bp). From 31-Dec-2027: 103.625%; 2028: 101.813%; 2029 and after: par. Up to 40% redeemable before 31-Dec-2027 with proceeds of certain equity offerings.

items.label: Mandatory redemption / offers
items.text: No sinking fund other than amortization and the Google termination-fee redemption (Indenture Section 3.11). Semiannual Excess Cash Flow Offer at par for 50% of Excess Cash Flow. Change of control offer at 101%.

items.label: Amortization
items.text: Semiannual installments on 30 Jun / 31 Dec starting after the lease Commencement Date, computed from a Payment Schedule (Section 14.03) using daily amounts on a 30/360 basis; nothing is payable before completion. The schedule table was not extracted; company illustrative model (8.0% coupon, $1.275bn) shows mandatory amortization of $19mm (2026), $75mm (2027), $78mm (2028), $80mm (2029), $82mm (2030).

items.label: Trustee, law, denominations
items.text: Wilmington Trust, National Association (trustee and collateral agent); New York law with exclusive Manhattan jurisdiction; $2,000 minimum and $1,000 multiples.

items.label: ISIN / CUSIP
items.text: CUSIP 33853QAA9 and ISIN US33853QAA94 (144A) as reported in a fund SEC N-PORT holding, with matching coupon and maturity; the identifiers do not appear in the indenture text itself. Reg S identifiers not found.

items.label: Structure
items.text: FS CS I LLC (JV Partners Holdco; at issue 50.1% owned by TeraWulf's Big Country Wulf LLC and 49.9% by Fluidstack CS I Inc., an indirect subsidiary of Fluidstack Ltd.) > Flash Compute LLC (issuer) > Abernathy Data LLC (guarantor, lessor and project owner).

items.label: Sponsor identity
items.text: The sponsor is TeraWulf together with Fluidstack; Cipher Mining is not part of this structure in any filing reviewed. Since 6-Jul-2026 TeraWulf holds no interest (see Recent developments).

items.label: Completion support
items.text: JV Partners Holdco provides a capped completion guarantee of up to $100mm, secured by a first-priority lien on a Holdco reserve account. It is not a guarantee of the notes.

items.label: Special covenants
items.text: Special covenant for JV Partners Holdco (Section 4.20), restriction on modification of project documents (4.21) and holding assets only for the Abernathy HPC Campus; Holdco is a party to the indenture and its default is an Event of Default trigger.

items.label: TeraWulf
items.text: Nasdaq-listed bitcoin miner and HPC developer; paid $450mm cash for 50.1% of the JV, then agreed in July 2026 to sell its entire 50.1% stake for about $530mm, citing monetization and redeployment into wholly owned projects.

items.label: Fluidstack
items.text: Fluidstack Ltd. (private AI cloud) holds the 49.9% via Fluidstack CS I Inc. and leads the buyer group. News headline (not read in full) reports a $750mm raise at a $7bn valuation in April 2026.

items.label: Purchasers of TeraWulf stake
items.text: Fluidstack CS I Inc. and 'certain other purchasers'; one newswire describes an investor group led by Fluidstack. Other purchasers are not named in the 8-K or 10-Q.

items.label: Tenant and lessor
items.text: Datacenter lease dated 26-Sep-2025 between Abernathy Data LLC (lessor) and Fluidstack USA III (tenant) relating to the building.

items.label: Term
items.text: 25-year hosting term (about $9.5bn contracted revenue to the JV); lease term may be shortened to 20 or 15 years under contractual options (consistent with Barclays seed of two 5-year shortening options).

items.label: Lease type and economics
items.text: Modified gross lease with annual escalators; power 100% passed through to the tenant. Company deck shows illustrative year-1 rent of about $264mm (about $1.57mm per MW per year on 168MW) escalating about 3%, opex about $42.7mm, NOI margin about 84% before and about 69% after land lease payments. Seed rent $1.55mm/MW is close but unverified.

items.label: Commencement
items.text: Company model assumed lease commencement 30-Sep-2026. Actual commencement date not disclosed in documents reviewed; TeraWulf described delivery as 2H 2026.

items.label: Google lease recognition
items.text: Lease Recognition Agreement dated 26-Sep-2025 among Abernathy, Fluidstack USA III and Google; replacement tenant mechanics via a 'New Tenant Process'. Google may assume the lease or pay a termination fee.

items.label: Assignment / replacement
items.text: Indenture permits Google or a replacement tenant to assume the lease and novate it at any time, with Google's Financial Support Agreement terminating under a form of Novation Agreement.

items.label: Location
items.text: Abernathy, Texas; 120 acres under a 25-year ground lease (Abernathy Landlord); Phase 1 only is financed.

items.label: Capacity
items.text: 168MW critical IT (240MW gross). Further phases (2027-2028) reserved for the JV beyond the initial 168MW.

items.label: Cost
items.text: Company states $8-10mm per critical MW; the investor deck states the building is worth $1.36bn at cost. Seed shows $1,354mm and $8.1mm/MW.

items.label: Ground lease
items.text: Land lease payments total about $215mm over the modeled horizon per company deck; a ground-lease letter of credit is cash collateralized with up to $75mm funded from notes proceeds.

items.label: Grid
items.text: Southwest Power Pool (SPP) rather than ERCOT; Xcel Energy / Southwestern Public Service Company territory; 345kV interconnection. Energization date and interconnection agreement details not located.

items.label: Cost pass-through
items.text: Power costs are passed through to the tenant under the lease.

items.label: Contractor
items.text: Hypertec Construction LBB, LLC is Contractor under the EPC Agreement. Indenture requires commercially reasonable efforts to obtain additional payment/performance surety bonds equal to the Additional Bond Amount ($1,203,345,600 less bonds delivered before the Issue Date) by 31-Jan-2026, unless TeraWulf or an affiliate assumes Hypertec's role. Outcome not disclosed.

items.label: Schedule
items.text: Construction started in 2025 (seed: Sept 2025, unverified); company said delivery expected 2H 2026; model assumption of 30-Sep-2026 lease commencement.

items.label: Status at 16-Oct-2026
items.text: No post-issuance construction update found. TeraWulf's 10-Q (as of 30-Jun-2026) says the JV had not yet commenced operations and recorded an $11.1mm Q2 equity-method loss.

items.label: Cost overrun protection
items.text: JV Partners Holdco completion guarantee capped at $100mm; construction-period debt service reserve; surety bond covenant.

MERIDI.title: Meridian Arc Holdco LLC 6.25% Senior Secured Notes due 30-Apr-2031
MERIDI.headline: $5.7bn 6.25% five-year senior secured notes of Meridian Arc HoldCo, a Fluidstack and Next Frontier (Coatue) joint venture building two data centers (245MW and 185MW) at New Lebanon, Indiana for a 15-year triple-net Fluidstack lease guaranteed by Google. Credit rests on the Google guarantee of an unrated private tenant, about 92% debt-to-cost, no GMP contract and a first-time sponsor-contractor team (Fitch BB as reported).

items.label: Issuer
items.text: Meridian Arc HoldCo LLC, an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Meridian Compute LLC.

items.label: Notes title and size
items.text: Senior secured notes, 6.25%, US$5.7bn aggregate principal, issued under an indenture in a private (exempt) offering; Latham notes it as the largest AI financing in the high-yield market to date (citing LCD). Described by Cooley as five-year notes.

items.label: CUSIP / ISIN
items.text: CUSIP 58990CAA1, ISIN US58990CAA18; 6.25% fixed; maturity 30-Apr-2031 (as reported in a fund's SEC N-PORT holding).

items.label: Issue date
items.text: Priced mid/late April 2026 (law-firm notes dated 16 and 20-Apr-2026); seed gives issue date 24-Apr-2026 (unverified).

items.label: Call features
items.text: Reported as non-call two. Seed: first call 30-Apr-2028 at 103.13 (unverified). Make-whole, equity claw and ECF terms not available.

items.label: Amortization
items.text: Seed: amortization starts mid-2027 (about 13% estimated by maturity). Indenture not accessible; unverified.

items.label: Trustee, law, denominations, clearing
items.text: Not available (indenture and offering memorandum not public).

items.label: Ownership
items.text: Meridian Compute LLC is a joint venture between subsidiaries of Frontier Development Holdings LP (a Next Frontier affiliate; Next Frontier was launched by Coatue) and Fluidstack Ltd. A secondary report gives 50.1% Frontier Holdings Indiana / 49.9% Fluidstack.

items.label: Structure
items.text: Issuer (Meridian Arc HoldCo) owns the New Lebanon, Indiana land and develops the two data centers and on-site substation, which are leased to Fluidstack (Cooley). Guarantors, ring-fencing and lockbox not disclosed.

items.label: Equity and completion support
items.text: About $505mm of sponsor equity funded at closing; Moody's reportedly cites a $100mm completion guarantee from each sponsor (secondary).

items.label: Next Frontier
items.text: Powered-land venture launched by Coatue Management (over $70bn AUM) to buy land near large power sources; Meridian is its first project.

items.label: Fluidstack
items.text: Private UK-incorporated AI cloud. Form D filings show private equity offerings: $750mm (Jan 2026, $450mm sold), $850mm (May 2026 amendment, $842mm sold) and a new $1.5bn offering from June 2026 ($730mm sold).

items.label: Experience
items.text: Fitch (as relayed) cites limited data-center experience at the sponsor and contractor.

items.label: Tenant
items.text: Fluidstack (tenant legal entity not disclosed in sources reviewed). The notes are rated on the Google guarantee because Fluidstack is unrated.

items.label: Lease
items.text: 100% leased; 15-year triple-net base term with three 5-year extension options.

items.label: Rent
items.text: Seed rent $1.49mm/MW/yr with 3.0% escalator and $5,250mm facility cost; not verified in any official document.

items.label: Replacement tenant risk
items.text: Fitch (as relayed): remote single-purpose AI training campuses are harder to re-tenant; Google may assume the lease or pay a termination fee.

items.label: Site
items.text: About 140 acres in multiple parcels at New Lebanon, Sullivan County, Indiana.

items.label: Capacity
items.text: Two turnkey data centers: 245MW and 185MW critical IT (total 430MW), plus an on-site electrical substation.

items.label: Cost
items.text: Debt about 92% of cost and about $505mm equity (Fitch as relayed) imply total cost about $6.2bn (our arithmetic), about $14mm per critical MW; seed shows $5,250mm and $12.2mm/MW.

items.label: Nearby development
items.text: Site is near Hallador's Merom station and Potentia's proposed 2.1GW Heartland Industrial Park; relationship to Potentia unclear.

items.label: Power agreement
items.text: Multi-Party Service Agreement with Hoosier Energy and WIN Energy provides power capacity; Hoosier is a cooperative and told reporters the agreements need not be filed with the Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission.

items.label: Energization
items.text: No official energization or interconnection schedule found.

items.label: Contractor
items.text: Arco (per Fitch commentary); no guaranteed maximum price contract; contingency and yield-on-cost lease structure mitigate; overruns can be 'rentalized' up to $18mm per MW (S&P as relayed).

items.label: Schedule
items.text: Building 1 about 9.5 months to target floor access for first data hall; Building 2 about 10.5 months; first 65MW hall targeted July 2027. Seed shows lease commencement Aug 2027 - Feb 2028 and construction start May 2026 (unverified). One news reprint gives conflicting earlier dates (300MW by Dec 2026) that do not reconcile with the 65MW July 2027 date.

items.label: Status at 16-Oct-2026
items.text: No post-issuance construction update from an official source; Fluidstack held a public open house in Sullivan County in August 2026.

items.label: Debt
items.text: $5.7bn senior secured notes; Fitch (as relayed) says notes fund about 92% of cost.

items.label: Leverage
items.text: Seed: 8.9x at issuance, 7.1x at maturity, 91% debt-funded (Barclays); unverified.

items.label: Market value
items.text: Fund-reported fair value about 100.5% of par at 31-May-2026 (may include accrued interest).

items.label: Google guarantee
items.text: Google guarantees Fluidstack's lease obligations; on a Fluidstack default it will assume the lease or pay a termination fee. This support underpins the BB rating (Fitch as relayed).

items.label: Alphabet aggregate exposure
items.text: Alphabet's 10-Q shows credit derivatives for data-center backstops with $43,785mm gross notional at 30-Jun-2026 (vs $16,940mm at 31-Dec-2025) and $815mm fair-value liability. Meridian is not named.

items.label: Sponsor completion guarantees
items.text: Each sponsor reportedly provided a $100mm construction completion guarantee (Moody's as relayed).

items.label: Indenture
items.text: Indenture, waterfall, DSCR tests, reserves and covenants not accessible; no SEC filing by issuer.

items.label: Fitch
items.text: BB, Stable, reported assigned April/May 2026 (14-May-2026 per a secondary summary), dependent on the Google guarantee.

items.label: Moody's / S&P
items.text: Seed shows Ba2 (Moody's) and BB- (S&P); a trade report said S&P rating was pending. Not verified from agency releases.

items.label: Use
items.text: Acquire the New Lebanon property; develop and construct two data centers and the substation; fund debt reserves; pay fees and expenses.

items.label: Construction
items.text: No GMP contract; contractor and sponsor have limited data-center experience (Fitch as relayed); aggressive schedule.

items.label: High leverage
items.text: About 92% debt-to-cost with about 8% equity; thin overrun cushion beyond rentalization.

items.label: Google backstop dependence
items.text: Rating relies on Google guarantee; Fluidstack unrated with large private fundraising needs.

items.label: Power and local politics
items.text: Power via cooperative agreements outside IURC filing; local scrutiny in Sullivan County.

items.label: Neighbouring project
items.text: Related Potentia project unclear.

items.label: May 2026
items.text: Next Frontier venture formally publicized; Fitch BB rating reported.

items.label: June 2026
items.text: Fluidstack opened a new $1.5bn private equity offering (Form D filed 30-Jun-2026).

items.label: August 2026
items.text: Fluidstack public open house in Sullivan County; no delay or default news found.

ZENARC.title: Zenith Arc LLC 8.875% Senior Secured Notes due 31-Aug-2031
ZENARC.headline: $2.25bn 8.875% five-year green senior secured notes of Zenith Arc LLC financing a 149MW data center in Okmulgee County, Oklahoma, leased for 15 years triple-net to Jane Street with a lease guaranty, developed by Fluidstack. A county floodplain permit was denied without prejudice in late August 2026 and no resolution is evident by 16-Oct-2026; the bonds fell from 99.5 at pricing to about 91.5 by 30-Sep-2026 on fund collateral marks, with yields near 11% reported.

items.text: Zenith Arc LLC, senior secured 144A notes, 8.875% due 31-Aug-2031 (five-year).

items.label: CUSIP / maturity / coupon
items.text: CUSIP 98935UAA5, 8.875% coupon, maturity 31-Aug-2031 as shown in money-market-fund SEC filings (repo collateral). ISIN US98935UAA51 from seed, unverified.

items.text: $2.25bn; priced 13-Aug-2026 at 99.5 per a search-result snippet of GuruFocus; Bloomberg (13-Aug) headline describes a $2.25bn green bond sale. Seed issue date 18-Aug-2026 unverified.

items.label: Call / amortization

items.text: Not available (144A document not public).

items.label: Sponsors
items.text: Fluidstack is the stated developer on the project website; 9fin links Fluidstack and Coatue to the project; the seed describes a Fluidstack/Next Frontier joint venture. Ownership percentages not found.

items.label: Fluidstack
items.text: Private UK-incorporated AI cloud; Form D filings show private equity offerings of $750mm (Jan 2026), $850mm (May 2026 amendment) and $1.5bn opened June 2026 ($730mm sold at 30-Jun-2026).

items.label: Coatue / Next Frontier
items.text: Coatue-incubated powered-land venture linked to the project by 9fin headline; no filing found.

items.label: Tenant
items.text: Jane Street, quantitative trading firm; seed names tenant entity JS Data Center LLC (not verified in any document).

items.label: Lease
items.text: 15-year absolute triple-net lease: tenant pays base rent and all property expenses (maintenance, taxes, utilities, insurance, electricity). Seed adds two 5-year extensions (unverified).

items.label: Guaranty
items.text: Jane Street provided a customary lease guaranty (per Moody's as reported by Briefs). No Google backstop appears in any source for this deal.

items.label: Rent
items.text: Seed: $1.75mm/MW/yr and 3.0% escalator; implied annual rent about $261mm on 149MW and debt-to-rent about 8.6x (our arithmetic, matching the seed leverage figure). Unverified.

items.label: Location
items.text: About 200 acres west of Okmulgee on the west side of Madison Avenue surrounding Hodges Warehouse, outside city limits; landowner and permit applicant Three Rivers Manufacturing LLC (Tulsa cutlery maker).

items.label: Capacity
items.text: 149MW (critical IT per seed and brief; sources say 149 megawatts).

items.label: Environment
items.text: Site borders Deep Fork Wildlife Refuge; residents cite American burying beetle and migratory birds; closed-loop cooling with one-time fill per Fluidstack.

items.label: Cost
items.text: Seed facility cost $2,120mm ($14.2mm/MW) and 91% debt funded; unverified.

items.label: Utility
items.text: Fluidstack states AEP-PSO is the energy provider and says it will pay for all energy and energy infrastructure; no tariff, interconnection agreement or Oklahoma Corporation Commission filing found.

items.label: Power permits
items.text: The assignment brief states power permits are outstanding; no public record found either way.

items.label: Substation
items.text: Brief states Shipp Engineering substation due June 2027. From the assignment brief; no public source found in this research.

items.label: Contractor and GMP

items.label: Delivery targets
items.text: Fluidstack website: first phase operational by September 2027 and final phase by September 2028 (seed: lease commencement Oct 2027 - Nov 2028).

items.label: Construction status
items.text: Seed says construction start July 2026, but a land-clearing permit existed by July and the floodplain development permit was denied in late August 2026, so ground-disturbing work status is unclear.

items.label: Debt
items.text: $2.25bn notes; at 99.5 gross proceeds about $2.239bn (our arithmetic).

items.label: Leverage
items.text: Seed: 8.6x at issuance, 7.2x at maturity, 91% debt-funded; unverified.

items.label: Secondary trading
items.text: Money-market-fund repo-collateral valuations: about 96.7% of face at 31-Aug-2026 and about 91.5% at 30-Sep-2026 (may include accrued interest). The Information reported yields near 11.3% on 20-Sep-2026, over 2 points wider than issue.

items.label: Lease guaranty
items.text: Jane Street guaranty of the lease; terms (amount, duration, whether full-recourse) not available.

items.label: Other
items.text: No completion guarantee, DSRA or termination payment details found; no third-party backstop reported.

items.label: Covenants
items.text: 144A indenture not accessible; green-bond framework and covenants unavailable.

items.label: Moody's

items.label: S&P
items.text: Reported BB in a search-result snippet of GuruFocus; seed BB.

items.label: Fitch
items.text: Seed shows NR; none found.

items.label: Use

items.label: Pricing
