CRWV.title: CoreWeave, Inc. 9.750% Senior Notes due 1-Oct-2031
CRWV.headline: $2.75bn of unsecured 9.75% senior notes (a $1.75bn issue on 14 Apr 2026 plus a $1.0bn tap at 102 on 21 Apr) from the AI cloud provider that is the tenant behind the CORZ and GALAXY bonds. Credit rests on a $104bn contracted backlog and 1.5 GW active power against about $35.6bn of debt, $29bn of lease payments and $6bn+ of quarterly capex, with net interest of $640mm a quarter. On 14-16 Oct 2026 its bonds and CDS sold off to distressed levels (2032s about 78c, CDS above 1,000bp) and the CEO responded with an internal memo saying backlog covers debt.

items.label: Issuer
items.text: CoreWeave, Inc. (NASDAQ: CRWV), parent of all CoreWeave financing SPVs.

items.label: Notes title
items.text: 9.750% Senior Notes due 1 Oct 2031 (general senior unsecured obligations).

items.label: Principal outstanding
items.text: $2,750mm = $1,750mm issued 14 Apr 2026 plus $1,000mm 'Additional Notes' issued 21 Apr 2026 at an issue price of 102.000% under a First Supplemental Indenture, forming a single class. Seed amount ($2,750mm) and 14 Apr issue date agree.

items.label: Upsizing
items.text: Initial launch (9 Apr 2026) was for $1,250mm of senior notes; the deal priced and closed at $1,750mm.

items.label: Coupon and dates
items.text: 9.750% p.a. cash, semi-annual on 1 Apr and 1 Oct, first coupon 1 Oct 2026; interest accrues from 14 Apr 2026 (also for the additional notes).

items.label: ISIN / CUSIP
items.text: Seed ISIN US21873SAG30 (144A); the additional notes may carry a different CUSIP; not verified. Reg S ISIN not found.

items.label: Ranking and guarantees
items.text: Senior unsecured; guaranteed by certain wholly-owned subsidiaries that guarantee CoreWeave's existing revolving credit facility. Non-recourse SPV borrowers (e.g. the DDTL 4.0 borrower) are not obligors; only the SPVs' equity value reaches the parent.

items.label: Optional redemption
items.text: Make-whole (Treasury + 50bp, PV of the 1 Oct 2028 call price) before 1 Oct 2028; up to 40% of the notes issued on the issue date may be redeemed with equity proceeds at 109.750% (within 180 days of the equity offering, 40% must remain outstanding); thereafter 104.875% (from 1 Oct 2028), 102.438% (from 1 Oct 2029), par (from 1 Oct 2030).

items.label: Change of control
items.text: Put at 101% plus accrued interest on a change of control triggering event.

items.label: Trustee
items.text: U.S. Bank Trust Company, National Association.

items.label: Format / denominations
items.text: Rule 144A (the 8-K for the first tranche refers to 144A; the launch notice refers to 144A and Reg S). Denominations and governing law not extracted.

items.label: Maturity profile context
items.text: Matures after the 2030 9.25% notes and 2031 9.00% notes; maturity 1 Oct 2031 sits inside a heavy 2030-2032 refinancing cluster (see Financing).

items.label: Obligor
items.text: CoreWeave, Inc. on a consolidated basis; recourse debt is either direct CoreWeave debt or guaranteed by CoreWeave, Inc. Non-recourse debt (DDTL 4.0 and some OEM financing) is limited to SPV assets save for customary carve-out guarantees.

items.label: Guarantor group
items.text: Wholly-owned subsidiaries guaranteeing the revolver also guarantee the 9.250% 2030, 9.000% 2031, 9.750% 2031, 9.625% 2032, 8.500% 2032 senior notes and the 1.75% 2031/2032 and 2.875% 2033 converts.

items.label: Structural subordination
items.text: The notes rank behind secured DDTL, revolver and OEM financing at asset level to the extent of collateral; DDTL borrowers (CoreWeave Compute Acquisition Co. VIII, CoreWeave Financing DDTL V / V-V) are indirect subsidiaries with parent guarantee and pledge for DDTL 5.0/5.5 (parent-guaranteed) but not for DDTL 4.0.

items.label: Unconsolidated entities
items.text: CoreWeave has unconsolidated VIE relationships (data center developers and an equipment lessor); maximum exposure per 10-Q: $108mm prepayments plus about $1.8bn committed equipment-lease payments.

items.label: Company
items.text: CoreWeave, Inc. ('The Essential Cloud for AI'), Livingston NJ; Nasdaq-100 member from Q2 2026; chairman and CEO Michael Intrator.

items.label: Q2 2026 financials
items.text: Revenue $2,575mm (+112% y/y); operating loss $(49)mm; Adjusted EBITDA $1,510mm (59% margin); adjusted operating income $128mm (5%); interest expense, net $(640)mm (vs $(267)mm); net loss $(626)mm.

items.label: Cash flow items
items.text: Q2 operating cash flow about $679mm and property and equipment purchases about $6.42bn (news summary of the 10-Q).

items.label: Equity support
items.text: $1bn strategic investment from Jane Street after expanded commercial relationship (Q2 2026 release); Jane Street also committed about $6.0bn of platform usage (announced Apr 2026).

items.label: Litigation
items.text: Putative securities class action Masaitis v. CoreWeave filed 12 Jan 2026 (D.N.J.) against the company and certain officers.

items.label: Credit metrics (derived)
items.text: Gross debt principal $35.55bn vs annualized Q2 Adjusted EBITDA about $6.0bn gives about 5.9x gross debt/EBITDA before leases; with operating and finance lease liabilities ($16.5bn) obligations total about $51.6bn.

items.label: CoreWeave as lessee (adapted section)
items.text: CoreWeave is the tenant behind Core Scientific (590 MW, 12-year licenses) and Galaxy Helios (Phases I-III, 526 MW), plus other landlords. Own obligations: operating lease liabilities $16.3bn and finance lease liabilities $0.2bn at 30 Jun 2026 (YE2025: $8.2bn operating).

items.label: Lease payments
items.text: Undiscounted operating lease payments $29.1bn (remaining 2026 $1.03bn; 2027 $2.12bn; 2028 $2.31bn; 2029 $2.37bn; 2030 $2.29bn; thereafter $19.0bn); weighted-average remaining term 12 years; discount rate 10%.

items.label: Leases not yet commenced
items.text: $35.5bn of undiscounted payments for executed leases (data centers, equipment, offices) not yet commenced, starting 2026-2029, terms 7-16 years; this is on top of the $29.1bn and excludes cost-based leases below.

items.label: Cost-based leases
items.text: One single-site lease with 393 MW undelivered (phased 2026-2028) where rent follows lessor construction costs with a contractual maximum of $14.7bn over 16 years; other cost-based leases with 355 MW undelivered (2026-2028). The 393 MW matches Galaxy's Helios Phase II+III but CoreWeave does not name the lessor (inference).

items.label: Equipment commitments
items.text: CoreWeave must procure and install lessee-owned equipment at some leased premises: estimated $0.5-1.2bn through 2028.

items.label: Landlord credit relevance
items.text: CORZ and GALAXY notes both depend on CoreWeave rent; CoreWeave's own filings do not name them, so lease terms cannot be cross-checked from the tenant side beyond the aggregate disclosure above.

items.label: Capacity footprint (adapted section)
items.text: 51 active data centers; active power about 1.5 GW (expanded by nearly 500 MW in Q2); total contracted power about 3.7 GW per Q2 release (about 4.2 GW per Sept 2026 deck citing the 11 Aug call; difference reflects early-Q3 additions).

items.label: Third-party data center dependence
items.text: Large share of capacity is leased from developers (Core Scientific, Galaxy, others); the 10-K discloses delivery delays announced Nov 2025 by an unnamed third-party provider.

items.label: Customer mix of capacity
items.text: Frontier AI labs, hyperscalers and enterprises; about 10% of backlog from financial services customers (13 Sep 2026).

items.label: Power approach
items.text: Capacity is delivered mainly by third-party landlords with their own utility arrangements; CoreWeave disclosed no direct utility agreements in the documents reviewed.

items.label: Regulatory headwind
items.text: 10-Q cites a July 2026 New York moratorium on data centers using 50 MW or more as an example of moratoria that could raise costs or restrict development.

items.label: ERCOT exposure (via landlords)
items.text: Texas landlords' interconnection (Helios, Denton, Pecos, Hunt) is subject to ERCOT Batch Zero; see CORZ and GALAXY dossiers.

items.label: Undelivered power
items.text: 393 MW at one site and 355 MW at other sites remain undelivered at 30 Jun 2026, expected 2026-2028.

items.label: DDTL draw periods
items.text: DDTL 5.0 commitments run to Sep 2026; DDTL 5.5 to Dec 2026; DDTL 4.0 to Jun 2027; draws fund GPU servers and related infrastructure as contracts deliver.

items.label: Delivery slippage
items.text: 10-K flags delays in certain third-party data centers (announced Nov 2025); delivery delay credits are a component of variable consideration in RPO.

items.label: Amortization sensitivity
items.text: DDTL 4.0 principal payments begin on the earliest of commitment termination, delayed-site amortization dates and top-up draws, so late delivery accelerates amortization.

items.label: Debt stack at 30 Jun 2026 ($mm principal)
items.text: Recourse: DDTL 1.0 1,300 (Mar 2028); DDTL 2.0 3,190 (Aug 2030); DDTL 2.1 3,000 (Mar 2031); DDTL 3.0 2,215 (Aug 2030); DDTL 5.0 1,101 (Nov 2031); 9.25% 2030 notes 2,000; 9.00% 2031 notes 1,750 (Feb 2031); 9.75% 2031 notes 2,750; 9.625% 2032 notes 1,250; 8.50% EUR 2032 notes 2,279 (EUR 2.0bn); 1.75% 2031 converts 2,588 (Dec 2031); 1.75% 2032 converts 4,000; revolver undrawn (Nov 2029); OEM/software financing 4,220; Magnetar loan 189 (Jan 2029). Non-recourse: DDTL 4.0 2,837 (Mar 2032); OEM financing 882. Total $35,551mm principal; recourse net $31.4bn, non-recourse net $3.7bn.

items.label: Post-quarter additions
items.text: DDTL 5.5 ($2.6bn, 7 Aug 2026; SOFR+5.50%; matures 1 Sep 2031; parent-guaranteed; draws to Dec 2026) and $4.2bn 2.875% convertible senior notes due 1 Apr 2033 (closed 22 Sep 2026; initial conversion price about $97.85, 22.5% premium; up to 52.6mm shares).

items.label: DDTL 5.0
items.text: $3.1bn facility (15 May 2026), SOFR+4.50%, matures 15 Nov 2031, parent-guaranteed; $1.1bn drawn at 30 Jun 2026.

items.label: DDTL 4.0
items.text: $8.5bn facility (30 Mar 2026), SOFR+2.25% floating or Treasury+2.00% fixed, matures 31 Mar 2032, non-recourse to parent; $2.84bn drawn.

items.label: 2032 convertible
items.text: $4.0bn 1.75% due 1 Oct 2032 incl. $500mm option; conversion price about $119.60 (30% premium over $91.99 implied); max 43.5mm shares; non-callable before 8 Oct 2029; capped calls purchased.

items.label: Liquidity at 30 Jun 2026
items.text: Cash $5,524mm + marketable securities $15mm + undrawn secured commitments $10,014mm = $15,553mm (YE2025: $6,862mm). Company says liquidity suffices for 12 months.

items.label: Interest cost
items.text: Q2 contractual interest $592mm; interest expense after capitalization $558mm; net interest expense $640mm. Effective rate on the 9.75% 2031 notes shown as 10%.

items.label: Equity programs
items.text: Jane Street $1bn investment; ATM/collared forward programme (see Recent developments).

items.label: 22-Sep-2026 convertible: terms
items.text: $4.2bn 2.875% Convertible Senior Notes due 1-Apr-2033 (144A), upsized. Base $3.7bn (launched 17-Sep at $3.0bn) plus the $500mm option exercised in full = $4.2bn (so the '$3.7bn' in some broker notes is the base deal). Indenture dated 22-Sep-2026, U.S. Bank Trust Company as trustee. Interest 1-Apr / 1-Oct from 1-Apr-2027. General senior unsecured obligations, jointly and severally guaranteed by the wholly-owned subsidiaries that guarantee the 9.25% 2030, 9% 2031, 9.75% 2031, 9.625% 2032 and 8.5% 2032 notes and the 1.75% 2031/2032 converts.

items.label: 22-Sep convertible: conversion
items.text: Initial rate 10.2194 shares per $1,000 (about $97.85 per share, 22.5% premium to the 17-Sep close); maximum rate 12.5187, i.e. up to 52,578,540 shares. Conversion conditions: stock at least 130% of the conversion price (from the quarter after 31-Dec-2026), 98% trading-price test, company call, corporate events; free conversion from 3-Jan-2033.

items.label: 22-Sep convertible: redemption and put
items.text: Provisional redemption at par on or after 5-Apr-2030 if the stock is at or above 130% of the conversion price for 20 of 30 trading days; clean-up redemption if less than $100mm remains outstanding; holders can put at par on a fundamental change.

items.label: 22-Sep convertible: events of default
items.text: Cross-default/acceleration threshold is the greater of $200mm or 5% of LTM EBITDA (30-day cure); 60-day cure on covenant breaches; acceleration by the trustee or 30% of holders. Sole remedy for reporting-covenant failures is additional interest of 0.25% then 0.50% for up to 365 days.

items.label: 22-Sep convertible: proceeds and capped calls
items.text: Net proceeds $4,137.0mm. Part funded capped call transactions (Barclays among the counterparties); the rest is for general corporate purposes. The cap price was not read. The 17-Sep 8-K also announced an at-the-market programme of up to 35mm shares (Equity Distribution Agreement) and the Exhibit 99.2 investor presentation.

items.label: This issue
items.text: Unsecured; benefits only from subsidiary guarantees and structural position. No collateral.

items.label: Customer prepayments
items.text: Deferred revenue $9.7bn at 30 Jun 2026 (vs $8.2bn) and contract assets $179mm; Q2 deals included customer prepayments per management.

items.label: Third-party backing
items.text: NVIDIA reportedly holds about 11.5% of CoreWeave and is obligated to purchase up to $6.3bn of residual capacity through April 2032 (stated in Galaxy's July 2026 presentation; not found in CoreWeave documents I reviewed).

items.label: Asset-level financing
items.text: Secured DDTLs ring-fence GPU/contract cash flows, which senior unsecured holders rank behind.

items.label: Debt incurrence
items.text: Ratio debt permitted if Consolidated Total Leverage Ratio (debt to LTM EBITDA) would be no greater than 6.00x; credit facility basket of $2.5bn plus the greater of $1.0bn and 25% of LTM EBITDA plus secured-ratio capacity (4.00x), the last part capped at the greater of $5,116mm and 100% of LTM EBITDA.

items.label: Investments
items.text: Certain investments conditioned on leverage no greater than 5.75x.

items.label: Asset sale sweep
items.text: Applicable percentage 100%, reduced to 50% if pro forma leverage is at most 2.50x but above 2.00x and to 0% at or below 2.00x.

items.label: Liens
items.text: Secured-leverage ratio limit of 4.00x for ratio liens; other negative covenants on restricted payments, affiliate transactions, mergers, unrestricted-subsidiary designations.

items.label: Events of default
items.text: Customary, incl. cross-default and bankruptcy; the 2032 convertible default threshold is the greater of $200mm or 5% of LTM EBITDA (note: convertible, not this indenture).

items.label: Reporting
items.text: Annual and quarterly reporting per offering-memorandum-style provisions; 8-K current report items mirrored.

sections.name: Debt stack by instrument (30-Jun-2026, with post-quarter changes)

items.label: Overview
items.text: 19 separately identified instruments totalling $35,551mm principal at 30-Jun-2026 (recourse $31,832mm, non-recourse $3,719mm). Post-quarter additions of the DDTL 5.5 draw ($1.2bn), the August revolver draw ($1.2bn) and the 22-Sep convert ($4.2bn) take the total to about $42.2bn before paydowns and FX. Full table: 'CRWV Debt Stack' tab in this workbook and CRWV_Debt_Stack_2026-10-17.xlsx.

items.label: Senior notes (5)
items.text: 9.25% 2030 $2,000mm (ISIN US21873SAB43); 9.00% 2031 $1,750mm (US21873SAC26); 9.75% 2031 $2,750mm (US21873SAG30); 9.625% 2032 $1,250mm (US21873SAK42); 8.50% EUR 2032 EUR 2,000mm (XS3333139288). All unsecured with subsidiary guarantees. Identifiers from the Bloomberg master, not from the indentures.

items.label: Convertible notes (3)
items.text: 1.75% due 1-Dec-2031 $2,587.5mm (US21873SAD09); 1.75% due 1-Oct-2032 $4,000mm (US21873SAH13); 2.875% due 1-Apr-2033 $4,200mm (US21873SAL25). ISINs from the Bloomberg master.

items.label: 1.75% convertible due 2031
items.text: Issued 11-Dec-2025: $2,587.5mm including the $337.5mm option. Conversion rate 9.2764 shares per $1,000 (about $107.80, 25% premium over the 8-Dec-2025 price); maximum rate 11.5955 (30,003,356 shares). Coupons 1-Jun / 1-Dec. Not redeemable before 5-Dec-2028, then at par if the stock is at least 130% of the conversion price for 20 of 30 days. Trustee U.S. Bank Trust Company; guaranteed by the subsidiaries guaranteeing the 9.25% 2030 and 9.00% 2031 notes.

items.label: DDTL 1.0 ($2.3bn, $1,300mm o/s)
items.text: Borrower CoreWeave Compute Acquisition Co. II, LLC; credit agreement 30-Jul-2023; Blackstone Tactical Opportunities and Magnetar as lead lenders, Imperial Capital as arranger. Term SOFR + 9.6196% (base rate + 8.6196%) since 15-May-2024; effective rate about 15%. Quarterly amortisation, final maturity 28-Mar-2028; secured by substantially all CCAC II assets and a pledge of its equity; fully drawn.

items.label: DDTL 2.0 ($7.6bn, $3,190mm o/s)
items.text: Borrower CoreWeave Compute Acquisition Co. IV, LLC; credit agreement 16-May-2024 (originally $7.5bn); U.S. Bank Trust Company as administrative and collateral agent; Blackstone lead lenders with Magnetar as co-lead. Term SOFR + 6.00% to 13.00% by customer rating (investment-grade contracts 6.00-6.50%, non-investment-grade 13.00%). Quarterly amortisation from Jan-2026; each draw matures five years after funding (about Aug-2030 for the last draws).

items.label: DDTL 2.1 ($3.0bn, $3,000mm o/s)
items.text: Incremental tranche added to the DDTL 2.0 agreement by the Fifth Amendment of 29-Sep-2025 (same borrower and agent); SOFR + 4.25% (base rate + 3.25%). Draws until Mar-2026 and each draw matures five years after funding, so final maturity is about Mar-2031 (the 10-K's Dec-2030 refers to the then-latest draw).

items.label: DDTL 3.0 ($2.6bn, $2,215mm o/s)
items.text: Borrowers CoreWeave Compute Acquisition Co. VII, LLC and Co. V, LLC; credit agreement 28-Jul-2025; MUFG administrative agent, U.S. Bank Trust collateral agent. Morgan Stanley and MUFG bookrunners and lead arrangers, Goldman Sachs lead arranger, with other banks in the syndicate (press). SOFR + 4.00%, matures 21-Aug-2030; backed by the OpenAI contract; monthly amortisation from Apr-2026. First Amendment (31-Dec-2025) cut minimum liquidity to $100mm for Mar-Apr 2026, postponed the first DSCR test to 31-Oct-2027 and allows unlimited equity cures before 28-Oct-2026.

items.label: DDTL 3.0 syndicate (secondary)
items.text: Press reports name JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, BBVA, Credit Agricole, SMBC, PNC and Societe Generale as participants. Not confirmed in filings.

items.label: DDTL 4.0 ($8.5bn, $2,837mm o/s)
items.text: Borrower CoreWeave Compute Acquisition Co. VIII, LLC (indirect subsidiary); credit agreement 30-Mar-2026; MUFG administrative agent, MUFG and Morgan Stanley Asset Funding lead arrangers. Floating: daily compounded SOFR + 2.25% (base + 1.25%); fixed: 2.00% over a blended Treasury rate at a 3.14-year weighted average life. Draws to Jun-2027, matures 31-Mar-2032; 0.50% undrawn fee; parent guarantee limited to specified bad acts.

items.label: DDTL 5.0 ($3.1bn, $1,101mm o/s)
items.text: Borrower CoreWeave Financing DDTL V, LLC (holdco CW Financing DDTL V Holdco); credit agreement 15-May-2026; Morgan Stanley Senior Funding administrative agent, MUFG and Morgan Stanley arrangers. SOFR + 4.50% (base + 3.50%); draws to Sep-2026; matures 15-Nov-2031; unconditionally guaranteed by the parent; Bloomberg loan line BL567281 / ISIN US21882DAB64.

items.label: DDTL 5.5 ($2.6bn, $1.2bn drawn post-quarter)
items.text: Borrower CoreWeave Financing DDTL V-V, LLC (holdco CW Financing DDTL V-V Holdco); credit agreement 7-Aug-2026; JPMorgan administrative agent, JPMorgan and MUFG arrangers. Term SOFR + 5.50% (base + 4.50%); draws to Dec-2026; matures 1-Sep-2031; parent guarantee plus borrower-subsidiary guarantees; DSCR at least 1.35x; Bloomberg loan line BL577043 / ISIN US21882EAB48.

items.label: Revolver, vendor financing, Magnetar
items.text: Revolver $2.5bn to Nov-2029 (nil drawn at 30-Jun; $1.2bn drawn Aug-2026; $600mm LC sub-facility). OEM and software-licence financing $4,220mm recourse plus $882mm non-recourse (terms 1-5 years, effective rates 9-11%); Magnetar loan $189mm (refundable $230mm deposit, 12%, Jan-2029).

items.label: Bloomberg loan identifiers
items.text: DDTL 1.0 BL482176 (issued 30-Jul-2023, matures 28-Mar-2028); DDTL 2.0 BL502513 (16-May-2024, 30-Aug-2030); DDTL 3.0 BL510511 (28-Jul-2025, 21-Aug-2030); DDTL 2.1 BL526160 (29-Sep-2025, 30-Sep-2030); DDTL 4.0 floating BL563786 ($1.4bn, ISIN US21881PAB04) and fixed BL563698 ($1.5bn, ISIN US21881PAC86), both 31-Mar-2032; DDTL 5.0 BL567281; DDTL 5.5 BL577043. Matched from the Bloomberg loan screen by issue date, maturity and amount. Bloomberg amounts differ from the 10-Q for DDTL 1.0 (1,438 vs 1,300) and DDTL 3.0 (1,700 vs 2,215).

items.label: Counterparty and nature
items.text: Customer is Microsoft Corporation itself (One Microsoft Way, Redmond). A framework agreement: the dollar commitments sit in separate order forms, which are not filed. Any Microsoft affiliate that signs an order form is bound as if it were a party. No guarantee, letter of credit, collateral or security interest appears in the agreement, so it is a direct contract claim on Microsoft, not credit support for CoreWeave debt.

items.label: Term
items.text: Runs from the effective date until all order forms have expired or been terminated. The agreement itself contains no minimum commitment.

items.label: Termination rights
items.text: Either party may terminate the agreement and each order form only for cause: a material breach uncured after 45 days' written notice, or the other party's insolvency (bankruptcy, receivership, liquidation, assignment for creditors). No termination for convenience was found.

items.label: If Microsoft terminates (CoreWeave breach)
items.text: CoreWeave must refund prepaid fees covering the remainder of the term of the affected order forms. This is a liability behind deferred revenue.

items.label: If CoreWeave terminates (Microsoft breach)
items.text: During the termination period Microsoft keeps paying unpaid fees for the rest of the term, and CoreWeave may set off prepaid amounts. For reserved instances CoreWeave may transfer or sell the contract servers without liability to Microsoft, with the proceeds deducted from what Microsoft owes. CoreWeave must use reasonable efforts to minimise the fees owed. If CoreWeave elects not to keep providing service (non-payment, uncurable violation of law, or gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud), Microsoft pays the lesser of remaining fees less resale proceeds, or the difference between fees paid and CoreWeave's on-demand rates.

items.label: Payment
items.text: Fees for reserved instances or bulk credits are due under the order forms; on-demand use is billed monthly in arrears. CoreWeave does not mark up expenses and does not offset against amounts Microsoft owes unless agreed. Termination never relieves Microsoft of fees for the period before termination.

items.label: Liability cap
items.text: Each party's aggregate liability (with affiliates) is capped at fees paid or payable in the [six months] before the claim (twelve months for certain confidentiality and data-processing breaches; bracketed in the filing). Exceptions include wilful misconduct, gross negligence and infringement indemnities. The cap does not limit Microsoft's payment obligations.

items.label: Assignment and change of control
items.text: Neither party may assign without consent (not to be unreasonably withheld), except in a merger, reorganisation or sale of substantially all assets. Microsoft may assign to its affiliates on notice and reserves the right to terminate if CoreWeave is acquired. If a party is acquired by, or undergoes a change of control in favour of, a direct competitor of the other, the other may terminate. Whether this restricts collateral assignment of receivables to lenders was not checked.

items.label: Read-through for creditors
items.text: Microsoft's credit supports CoreWeave's contract cash flows (take-or-pay order forms, cause-only termination), but no Microsoft guarantee stands behind any CoreWeave debt, and the filings do not say which loan, if any, is backed by a Microsoft order form (DDTL 2.0 prices investment-grade contracts at S+6.00-6.50%).

items.label: Seed
items.text: No ratings in seed for CRWV.

items.label: Secondary pointers (unconfirmed)
items.text: Search summaries point to S&P issuer rating B+ with positive outlook (May 2026) and issue-level B on the 9.00% 2030/2031 notes; Fitch BB- with RR4 on the convertible notes due 2031; Moody's Ba3 per a German-language aggregator. No agency release for the 9.75% 2031 notes was retrieved and no rating action after the Oct 2026 selloff was found.

items.label: Triggers
items.text: Not available from official sources.

items.label: Barclays debt table: ratings
items.text: Issuer Ba3/B+ (Moody's/S&P). Senior unsecured notes (9.25% 2030, 9% 2031, 9.75% 2031, 9.625% 2032, EUR 8.5% 2032) B1/B. DDTL-4.0 ($8.5bn, S+225, 3/2032) A3/A-; DDTL-5.0 ($3.1bn, S+450, 5/2032) and DDTL-5.5 ($2.6bn, S+550, 9/2031) Ba2/BB+. Barclays' footnote says the DDTL ratings are Moody's/Fitch, yet the column header reads Moody's/S&P, so the DDTL agency labels are ambiguous. Not checked against agency publications.

items.label: Stated use
items.text: General corporate purposes, including repayment of outstanding indebtedness, and fees and expenses (both tranches).

items.label: Context
items.text: Same-day financing used $4.0bn convertible proceeds partly for capped calls; Q2 release cites more than $10bn of unsecured debt and convertible bonds raised in the quarter.

items.label: Leverage and interest burden
items.text: Net interest $640mm a quarter on revenue $2.6bn; operating loss; capex about $6.4bn a quarter; funding depends on continued market access.

items.label: Maturity wall
items.text: $15.0bn principal due 2026-2028 (derived), much of it DDTL amortization tied to contract cash flows, plus $4.4bn remaining 2026.

items.label: Customer concentration
items.text: Customer A 36%, B 26%, C 10% of Q2 revenue; A and B each 32% of receivables; Microsoft was about 67% of FY2025 revenue; OpenAI up to about $6.5bn through May 2031; Meta initially up to about $14.2bn through Dec 2031; Jane Street about $6.0bn.

items.label: Backlog quality
items.text: Backlog $104.2bn (RPO $103.7bn: 41% within 24 months, 39% in months 25-48) is not cash; requires delivery of capacity and availability; includes variable consideration estimates.

items.label: Lease obligations
items.text: $29.1bn operating lease payments plus $35.5bn not yet commenced; fixed obligations front-run revenue.

items.label: Market stress Oct 2026
items.text: Bonds and CDS at record distress; refinancing costs rising; equity down sharply; 2032 bond about 78c.

items.label: Structural subordination
items.text: Unsecured notes rank behind secured DDTL and OEM financings at the asset level.

items.label: Dilution / equity funding
items.text: 35mm-share ATM plus convertible overhang (about 52.6mm shares on the 2033 convert at max rate, 43.5mm on 2032).

items.label: Further debt after the 9.75% issue
items.text: $1.25bn 9.625% senior notes due Jul 2032 and EUR 2.0bn 8.500% due Jul 2032 (18 Jun 2026); DDTL 5.0 $3.1bn (15 May); DDTL 5.5 $2.6bn (7 Aug); $4.2bn 2.875% converts due 2033 (22 Sep).

items.label: ATM program
items.text: 17 Sep 2026 Equity Distribution Agreement with eleven agents plus four forward purchasers: up to 35,000,000 Class A shares by at-the-market sales or collared forward sale agreements; commission up to 2.0%; under Form S-3 filed 5 Jun 2026; no sales until at least 30 days after the convertible purchase agreement. Usage to date not disclosed.

items.label: Backlog / demand
items.text: Backlog $104.2bn at 30 Jun 2026 plus more than $25bn net new commitments in early Q3; price increases of about 70% on some SKUs in July 2026 for short-dated contracts (company claim).

items.label: October 2026 selloff
items.text: 14-16 Oct 2026: 2032 unsecured bonds below 80c on 14 Oct and about 78c (yield just over 16%) on 15 Oct; five-year CDS above 1,000bp (record); stock -16% on 14 Oct; trigger cited as a hot US inflation print and fear of a December Fed hike.

items.label: Company response
items.text: CEO Intrator memo (14 Oct) states contracted backlog is sufficient to cover debt obligations and attributes the move to contagion from troubled AI infrastructure IPOs and debt deals; no buyback, tender or new financing action reported as of 16 Oct 2026.

items.label: Price of this bond
items.text: Specific price/yield of the 9.75% 2031 notes during the selloff was not found.

items.label: 22-Sep convertible closed
items.text: $4.2bn 2.875% converts due 2033 closed on 22-Sep (see Financing and capital structure). Adds unsecured parent-level convertible debt ranking alongside the 9.75% notes through the same guarantor group.

items.label: Window and totals
items.text: 25 Form 4s filed between 1-Sep and 14-Oct-2026 (open-market and plan sales, code S): about 2.20mm shares sold, about $191.3mm. 26 Form 144s were filed in the same window. Sales followed the 22-Sep convertible and ran into the October selloff.

items.label: Largest sellers
items.text: Michael Intrator (CEO): 1,617,012 shares, $141.4mm (also option exercises of 355,742 shares and conversions of 323,076). Kristen McVeety (GC): 253,505, $21.9mm. Nitin Agrawal (CFO): 144,927, $12.2mm. Brian Venturo (CSO): 65,616, $5.8mm plus a 62,500-share gift. Chen McBee (CDO): 56,531, $5.0mm. Jones (CRO): 37,380, $2.9mm. Goldberg: 22,429, $2.2mm. Jain and Baker: small.

items.label: Directors
items.text: Directors Boone and Whitman show option exercises only, no open-market sales in the window.

items.label: Read-through
items.text: Sales are concentrated in the CEO (about 74% of the dollar total). Whether these were under Rule 10b5-1 plans was not checked, so the signal is ambiguous; no insider purchases were seen.

items.label: Q2 2026 results
items.text: Revenue about $2,575mm; operating loss $(49)mm; interest expense, net $(640)mm (6M $(1,176)mm); net loss $(626)mm (6M $(1,366)mm); EPS $(1.14). Accumulated deficit about $4.0bn. Interest expense is larger than operating income, so the debt service burden depends on revenue ramp from new capacity.

items.label: Backlog (RPO)
items.text: RPO $103.7bn at 30-Jun-2026: 41% to be recognised within 24 months (to 30-Jun-2028), 39% in months 25-48, remainder in months 49-78. Deferred revenue $9.7bn (from $8.2bn).

items.label: Customer concentration
items.text: Customers A/B/C were 36% / 26% / 10% of Q2 revenue (A 40%, B 23% for the six months). Receivables: A 32%, B 32%. Identities are not disclosed in the 10-Q.

items.label: Liquidity
items.text: Liquidity $15,553mm at 30-Jun-2026: cash $5,524mm, marketable securities $15mm, undrawn availability $10,014mm. Subsequent to quarter end: DDTL 5.5 ($2.6bn, SOFR+5.5%, matures Sep-2031, $1.2bn drawn) and a $1.2bn revolver draw in Aug-2026.

items.label: Debt at 30-Jun-2026
items.text: Recourse: DDTL 1.0 $1,300mm; DDTL 2.0 $3,190mm; DDTL 2.1 $3,000mm; DDTL 3.0 $2,215mm; DDTL 5.0 $1,101mm; 9.25% 2030 notes $2,000mm; 9% 2031 $1,750mm; 9.75% 2031 $2,750mm; 9.625% 2032 $1,250mm; EUR notes $2,279mm; converts $2,588mm and $4,000mm; OEM/software financing $4,220mm; Magnetar $189mm. Recourse total net $31,405mm (current $6,235mm). Non-recourse: DDTL 4.0 $2,837mm and OEM $882mm, net $3,663mm. At 31-Dec-2025 recourse debt was $20,726mm net, liquidity $6,862mm.

items.label: Leases not yet commenced
items.text: $35.5bn of undiscounted lease payments for leases not yet commenced (commencing 2026-2029, terms 7-16 years). One site lease has 393 MW undelivered with a contractual maximum rent of $14.7bn over 16 years; other leases with variable rent cover a further 355 MW undelivered. Lessee-side equipment commitments of $500mm-$1.2bn.

items.label: DDTL 4.0 security
items.text: Secured by a pledge of the equity of CCAC VIII and substantially all of its assets ($3.3bn of non-current assets at 30-Jun-2026); non-recourse to CoreWeave except limited carve-out guarantees. Requires hedging of at least 95% of floating borrowings; the financing percentage depends on projected DSCR.

items.label: 2032 converts
items.text: $4.0bn 1.75% converts conversion price $119.60, non-callable before 8-Oct-2029 (stock is far below this level).

items.label: Internal controls
items.text: Material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting persist at 30-Jun-2026 (IT general controls, segregation of duties, insufficient accounting personnel). Disclosure controls were concluded not effective; remediation is ongoing and no material misstatement was identified. No litigation expected to be material.

items.label: FY2025 results
items.text: Revenue $5,131mm (2024 $1,915mm, +168%; 2023 $229mm). Operating loss $(46)mm (2024 operating income $324mm). Interest expense, net $(1,229)mm (2024 $(361)mm). Net loss $(1,167)mm (2024 $(863)mm, 2023 $(594)mm). Stock-based compensation $630mm.

items.label: FY2025 backlog and footprint
items.text: RPO $60.7bn at 31-Dec-2025 (from $15.1bn): 43% within 24 months, 38% in months 25-48; weighted-average contract duration about 5 years. 43 data centers, more than 850 MW active power and about 3.1 GW contracted power at year end.

items.label: FY2025 concentration
items.text: Customer A was 67% of 2025 revenue (62% in 2024, 35% in 2023); Customer A was 68% and Customer D 11% of receivables. Customer concentration eased to 36% in Q2 2026.

items.label: FY2025 financing approach and controls
items.text: Stated approach: asset-level debt supported by take-or-pay contracts, supplemented by corporate equity and debt. Material weaknesses in internal control (same three areas as later) were identified in the 10-K. No going-concern language was found.

items.label: Recommendation and thesis
items.text: Maintain Overweight on the 2030-32 unsecured notes, viewing the sell-off as a buying opportunity. The sell-off is attributed mainly to technical selling (hedge-fund de-risking, which holds much of the unsecured paper) plus negative press (social-media posts 13-Oct, a D.A. Davidson 'equity could go to zero' comment, a Gartner neocloud forecast, an FT interview on 14-Oct), not to deterioration in fundamentals. Triggers that would change the view: a rapid slowdown in AI infrastructure demand, a seizure of financing markets, or execution misses against guidance.

items.label: DDTL trading
items.text: DDTLs are only 5-50bp wider since mid-September: DDTL-4.0 at 99.00 / 5.27% / OAS 112bp; DDTL-5.0 at 99.50 / 8.55% / 461bp; DDTL-5.5 at 99.00 / 8.37% / 430bp. Barclays reads this as secured, contract-backed, amortising structures with a lender base weighted to loan and private-credit investors; new DDTLs could price wider if sentiment persists.

items.label: CDS
items.text: 5Y CDS 1,100/1,160bp bid/ask on 15-Oct (from 860bp at 22-Sep). Midpoint curve: 1Y 686, 2Y 762, 3Y 942, 4Y 1,029, 5Y 1,130bp; implied cumulative default probability (30% recovery) 6.4% / 13.2% / 22.9% / 38.3% / 49.9%.

items.label: Funding needs (Barclays estimates)
items.text: About $30bn needed in 2027 (about $24bn secured, $6bn other) and about $95.6bn over 2027-30 in the base case (7GW active power by 2030, below the company's >8GW target), made up of about $81bn FCF usage and $20bn of maturities and amortisation, net of a $6bn 2027 cash draw. About 80% is expected from GPU-backed DDTLs; the other 20% from converts, the 35mn-share ATM (available from late October at the earliest) and strategic equity (NVIDIA, Jane Street). In a no-new-leases case (4.2GW secured) about $57bn would be needed in 2027-28, with net leverage 1.9x by 2030. Barclays does not expect regular-way unsecured issuance near term. Barclays also expects a financing against the about $21bn incremental Meta contract before year-end.

items.label: Leverage and subordination
items.text: Total leverage 8.1x LTM at 2Q26 (Barclays), 7.3x expected at year-end 2026; net leverage modelled at 6.3x 2026E, 4.4x 2027E, 3.7x 2028E, 3.1x 2029E, 2.5x 2030E. Unsecured notes sit behind about 75% secured debt, mostly DDTLs. Barclays believes steady-state leverage should be under 3x.

items.label: Estimates
items.text: Barclays base case: revenue $13.0bn 2026E, $28.3bn 2027E, $44.1bn 2028E, $77.1bn 2030E; adjusted EBITDA $7.8bn, $18.2bn, $29.2bn, $51.7bn; cash interest $2.7bn 2026E, $4.3bn 2027E, $8.4bn 2030E; growth capex $38.0bn 2026E, $47.2bn 2027E; FCF $(30.5)bn 2026E, $(31.8)bn 2027E, $(4.4)bn 2030E; active power 1,850MW 2026E, 3,030MW 2027E, 6,970MW 2030E (1,500MW at 2Q26). Equity value at $69.69 (15-Oct) x 559mn shares = $38.9bn; EV/EBITDA 11.3x 2026E.

items.label: Operating read
items.text: 2Q26 revenue $2.58bn (+112% y/y), adjusted EBITDA $1.51bn (58.6% margin), active power +475MW q/q to 1.5GW. FY26 guidance raised: revenue $12.4-13.2bn, adjusted operating income $960-1,150mn, year-end ARR $18.5-19.5bn, about 1.85GW active power, capex $35-39bn. Backlog $104.2bn at 2Q plus about $25bn signed early 3Q (about $129bn); 2027 capacity nearly sold out; 4.2GW total secured. Meta contracts $35bn (about one third of backlog); OpenAI about 20% of revenue (Barclays belief). Customer identities are Barclays' inference, not company disclosure.

items.label: NVIDIA support
items.text: NVIDIA invested $2bn in Jan-2026, is the second-largest shareholder (about 10%), and agreed to buy up to $6.3bn of unsold capacity through April 2032. Jensen Huang said on 15-Oct that CRWV does not need a bailout. NVIDIA's non-binding $500bn AI infrastructure financing platform may give residual-value support up to 25% of a project; CRWV is 'actively' looking at it (per FT interview with B. McBee).

items.label: Reconciliation with company filings
items.text: Differences versus the 10-Q Q2 and 8-K figures in this dossier: Barclays cites $3.7bn for the September convertible (the base deal; $4.2bn closed with the option); liquidity $16.9bn versus $15,553mm in the 10-Q; backlog $104.2bn versus RPO $103.7bn. The 10-Q/8-K figures take precedence.

ORCL.title: Oracle Corporation 4.950% Senior Notes due 4-Feb-2031
ORCL.headline: $3.5bn of Oracle's 4.950% unsecured senior notes due 4-Feb-2031, one of eight series in a $25bn offering priced on 2-Feb-2026 (alongside a $5bn mandatory convertible and a $20bn ATM that Oracle has since fully used). It is the parent/tenant comparable for Oracle-leased project bonds: priced at T+115bp, now rated BBB- at S&P (cut 9-Jul-2026), Baa2 negative at Moody's and BBB at Fitch as last confirmed. Credit story is heavy AI capex (Q1 FY27 capex $28.5bn, FCF -$5.4bn), $125bn of debt and $288bn of not-yet-commenced data center leases against a $664bn backlog.

items.label: Issuer
items.text: Oracle Corporation (Delaware), sole obligor; Oracle Systems Corporation is no longer an obligor under the indenture.

items.label: Notes title
items.text: 4.950% Notes due 2031 (the '2031 Fixed Rate Notes'), unsecured senior obligations.

items.label: ISIN / CUSIP
items.text: US68389XDX03 / 68389XDX0 (seed ISIN confirmed in the pricing term sheet).

items.label: Principal
items.text: $3,500,000,000 original; no sinking fund; reopenings permitted (additional notes would share the CUSIP). Seed $3,500mm outstanding confirmed at issue; no repurchase disclosed.

items.label: Coupon and day count
items.text: 4.950% fixed, payable semi-annually on 4-Feb and 4-Aug from 4-Aug-2026; 30/360.

items.label: Issue date and maturity
items.text: Trade date 2-Feb-2026; settlement T+2, 4-Feb-2026; matures 4-Feb-2031.

items.label: Price and yield at issue
items.text: Priced at 99.834% of par; yield to maturity 4.988%; spread +115bp over the 3.700% UST due 31-Jan-2031 (yield 3.838%). Underwriting discount 0.200%; net proceeds before expenses $3,487.19mm.

items.label: Ranking
items.text: Equal with all other unsecured, unsubordinated Oracle debt; effectively subordinated to secured debt and structurally to subsidiary liabilities (about $65.4bn of subsidiary liabilities at 30-Nov-2025 out of $174.5bn consolidated liabilities; $108.1bn of senior unsecured borrowings pari passu).

items.label: Redemption
items.text: Par call date 4-Jan-2031 (one month before maturity). Before then redeemable at any time at the greater of par and make-whole at Treasury plus 20bp; at par on or after 4-Jan-2031.

items.label: Change of control put
items.text: None found in the prospectus supplement text (searched).

items.label: Denominations, clearing, trustee, law
items.text: $2,000 and $1,000 multiples; DTC (Euroclear/Clearstream indirect); trustee The Bank of New York Mellon Trust Company, N.A.; New York law.

items.label: Indenture
items.text: Indenture dated 13-Jan-2006 (Oracle Corporation, formerly Ozark Holding Inc., Oracle Systems Corporation and Citibank, N.A.), supplemented 9-May-2007; BNY Mellon successor trustee since 2007. Registered under shelf S-3 No. 333-277990 (prospectus 2-Feb-2026).

items.label: Obligor
items.text: Oracle Corporation only; notes are not guaranteed by subsidiaries.

items.label: Structural subordination
items.text: Notes are structurally subordinate to liabilities of subsidiaries ($65.4bn at 30-Nov-2025).

items.label: Capitalization effect
items.text: Total debt $108.1bn at 30-Nov-2025 rose to $132.9bn as adjusted for the $25bn offering; total capitalization $162.9bn as adjusted (before use of proceeds).

items.label: Concurrent financings
items.text: Concurrently: $5.0bn 6.50% Series D mandatory convertible preferred (100mm depositary shares, $50 liquidation preference each, $5.0bn aggregate) and a $20bn at-the-market common equity program; the notes offering was not conditioned on either.

items.label: Corporate profile
items.text: Oracle Corporation, Austin, Texas; cloud infrastructure (OCI), applications, software, hardware, services. Q1 FY27 (Aug-2026) revenue $19.3bn, up from $14.9bn; cloud infrastructure revenue $7.4bn vs $3.3bn.

items.label: Funding plan
items.text: On 1-Feb-2026 Oracle said it expects to raise $45-50bn gross in calendar 2026, about half equity (mandatory convertible plus up to $20bn ATM) and half through a single investment-grade bond issuance, with no further bonds expected in calendar 2026, to build OCI capacity for customers including AMD, Meta, NVIDIA, OpenAI, TikTok and xAI.

items.label: ATM completed
items.text: Oracle fully used the $20bn ATM in Q1 FY27, issuing about 141 million shares for net proceeds of $19.9bn.

items.label: Balance sheet at 31-Aug-2026
items.text: Cash and equivalents $36.4bn plus marketable securities $0.7bn; notes payable and other borrowings $125.3bn (current $7.6bn, non-current $117.7bn; derived sum); equity $67.2bn; total assets $303.3bn.

items.label: Cash flow Q1 FY27
items.text: Operating cash flow $23.1bn (includes $11.4bn customer prepayments), capex $28.5bn, free cash flow -$5.4bn; interest expense $1.43bn for the quarter.

items.label: Customer concentration and backlog
items.text: Remaining performance obligations $664bn at 31-Aug-2026 ($638bn at 31-May-2026); S&P says OpenAI is about half of RPO.

items.label: Oracle as lessee: balance-sheet leases
items.text: At 31-Aug-2026 operating lease liabilities $34.6bn and finance lease liabilities $9.2bn; undiscounted lease payments $48.1bn operating and $15.2bn finance.

items.label: Off-balance-sheet data center leases
items.text: $288bn of additional lease commitments at 31-Aug-2026, substantially all data centers, generally commencing between Q2 FY27 and FY29 for 15-19 year terms and not on the balance sheet ($260bn at 31-May-2026; $28bn added in Q1 FY27).

items.label: Lessor-debt guarantee
items.text: Among the $260bn is a lease for which Oracle guaranteed up to $3.3bn of the lessor's borrowing, maturing in September 2026; outcome of that maturity not disclosed in documents read.

items.label: Unconditional purchase obligations
items.text: $34.2bn at 31-Aug-2026 (chips/components and data center power), versus $13.3bn at 31-May-2026.

items.label: Third-party lessor projects
items.text: Oracle's filings do not name individual lessors; project bonds for Oracle-leased campuses (for example RD Michigan, where KBRA says Oracle guarantees the leases) rely on Oracle lease credit.

items.label: Risk language
items.text: Oracle warns its lease terms and renewal pricing typically do not align with customer contract duration and that it could be locked into excess space and financing if customers cannot pay.

items.label: OCI capacity build
items.text: Capex rose from $21.2bn in FY25 to $55.7bn in FY26 and $28.5bn in Q1 FY27 alone (vs $8.5bn a year earlier); management expects FY27 capex above FY26 as data center capacity expands in existing and new geographies. Unpaid capex $6.2bn at 31-Aug-2026.

items.label: FY27 capex guidance
items.text: S&P cites Oracle FY27 capex guidance of $90-95bn (secondary; Oracle's 8-K not read).

items.label: Property, plant and equipment
items.text: Net PP&E $127.8bn at 31-Aug-2026 vs $100.0bn at 31-May-2026.

items.label: Power arrangements
items.text: Unconditional obligations include data center power supply arrangements (included in the $34.2bn). No site-level power detail in these filings.

items.label: Not applicable (corporate bond)
items.text: Delivery risk sits in OCI capacity ramp: leases commence Q2 FY27 to FY29; 'delays or development and operational problems with construction of the data centers' are named risk factors in Oracle's funding press release.

items.label: Debt stack
items.text: Total senior notes and other borrowings $130.1bn at 31-May-2026 (principal) vs $92.9bn a year before; $125.3bn carrying value at 31-Aug-2026 after $4.2bn repayments in Q1.

items.label: Cash raised in 2026
items.text: $25bn notes (Feb-2026), $5bn mandatory convertible (Feb-2026) and $19.9bn net ATM proceeds (Q1 FY27), together near the $45-50bn plan.

items.label: Maturity profile near the 2031 notes
items.text: Debt maturing within 12 months $7.6bn at 31-Aug-2026.

items.label: Equity cushion
items.text: Common equity plus preferred increased with ATM proceeds; total stockholders' equity $67.2bn vs $43.1bn at 31-May-2026.

items.label: Support
items.text: None: unsecured, no subsidiary guarantees, no financial covenants. Credit support is Oracle's operating cash flow, liquidity and backlog.

items.label: Negative covenants
items.text: Limitation on liens (equal-and-ratable securing unless within exceptions, including Aggregate Debt not above the greater of 25% of Consolidated Net Worth at lien creation or at issuance of the series); limitation on sale-leaseback transactions; merger covenant (US successor assumes obligations). The covenants do not limit the amount of debt Oracle may incur.

items.label: Events of default
items.text: Non-payment of interest for 30 days, non-payment of principal, covenant breach continuing 90 days after notice, certain bankruptcy events; no cross-default described in the base-indenture summary read.

items.label: At pricing (Feb-2026)
items.text: Expected ratings in the pricing term sheet: Moody's Baa2 (negative) / S&P BBB (negative) / Fitch BBB (stable).

items.label: Moody's
items.text: Baa2 affirmed with negative outlook on 2-Feb-2026 (headline report). A later Moody's action was not found; third-party summary says Moody's warned leverage could temporarily approach 5x EBITDA.

items.label: S&P
items.text: Downgraded to BBB- from BBB on 9-Jul-2026, stable outlook (one notch above speculative grade); cited AI capex of $90-95bn in FY27, FOCF deficit near $42bn, leverage and customer concentration. Downgrade triggers: leverage sustained above 4.5x; no path to positive FOCF by FY29; negative view of Oracle's AI strategy. S&P added $260bn of lease commitments to its analysis.

items.label: Fitch
items.text: BBB IDR, stable outlook, affirmed 2-Feb-2026 with BBB rating on the new unsecured notes; forecast EBITDA leverage above 3.5x in FY26 declining in FY27-28, pre-dividend FCF below -$26bn in FY26 and -$18bn in FY27. Later Fitch action not found.

items.label: Rating of this note today
items.text: S&P BBB-, Moody's Baa2 negative (as of Feb-2026) and Fitch BBB are the last confirmed levels; no post-Jul-2026 Moody's/Fitch actions verified.

items.label: Use
items.text: General corporate purposes, which may include capital expenditures, repayment of indebtedness, future investments or acquisitions, and dividends or share repurchases. Gross proceeds $24.96bn at issue price; underwriting discount $75.0mm; other expenses about $22.6mm; net before expenses $24.89bn.

items.label: Oracle's stated purpose
items.text: The 1-Feb-2026 release says the raise funds OCI capacity to meet contracted demand from large customers.

items.label: Free cash flow and leverage
items.text: Q1 FY27 FCF of -$5.4bn; S&P forecasts FY27 FOCF deficit near $42bn; rating headroom at S&P is one notch above high yield.

items.label: Off-balance-sheet leases
items.text: $288bn of lease commitments not yet on balance sheet, commencing Q2 FY27 to FY29; will increase fixed charges and lease liabilities.

items.label: Customer concentration
items.text: RPO $664bn dominated by a few AI customers (S&P: OpenAI about half).

items.label: Structural subordination
items.text: Notes rank behind subsidiary liabilities and any secured or project-level debt; Oracle-leased project bonds sit alongside this unsecured debt.

items.label: Capital-markets reliance
items.text: Oracle plans said no more bonds in calendar 2026, so further funding relies on equity, cash and project/lessor financing.

items.label: Equity raise completed
items.text: $20bn ATM fully used in Q1 FY27 (ended 31-Aug-2026), net $19.9bn.

items.label: S&P downgrade
items.text: 9-Jul-2026 to BBB- stable (secondary report).

items.label: 10-Q (11-Sep-2026)
items.text: RPO $664bn; lease commitments $288bn; capex $28.5bn in the quarter; repaid $4.2bn of borrowings.

items.label: Dividends
items.text: 8-K of 10-Sep-2026 declared $0.50 per common share and $1,625 per share on the mandatory convertible preferred.

items.label: Chair's share-sale plan
items.text: Larry Ellison cancelled his 10b5-1 plan on 12-Sep-2026 with no shares sold.

gaps: Rating agency releases themselves (Moody's, S&P, Fitch) were not read; ratings after Feb-2026 come from term sheet expectations and secondary reports. No confirmed Moody's or Fitch action after Feb-2026 and no Moody's rationale or triggers.

The executed indenture and supplemental documents were not opened; indenture terms are taken from the prospectus supplement and base prospectus description (cross-default and some definitions not verified).
8-K of 5-Feb-2026 (Items 1.01/3.03/5.03) and the 10-Q footnote on borrowings and credit facilities were not reviewed in detail; revolver or term-loan capacity not captured.
Oracle's FY27 capex guidance ($90-95bn) is from a secondary S&P summary; the Jun-2026 earnings 8-K/press release was not read.
Outcome of the $3.3bn lessor-debt guarantee maturing Sep-2026 is not disclosed in documents read.
Oracle filings do not name individual landlords, so Oracle's lease obligations cannot be mapped to specific project bonds (RD Michigan, Yondr JK 1).
Secondary trading levels and current spread for the 4.95% 2031 not sourced here (the seed set carries no yield for ORCL).

readme: AI credit live workbook. Blue cells are Bloomberg formulas (=BDP) that update while this file is open in Excel with the Bloomberg add-in loaded (same login as the terminal).
If cells show #NAME?: Excel > Bloomberg tab > Log In, then Refresh (F9). 'Requesting Data...' clears after a minute or two on first open.

Principal gained / lost = (live price - 100) / 100 x amount outstanding, in $mn on the whole issue. Negative = trading below par. Also shown: today's change in value (live vs previous close) and, for the Barclays universe, the change since 15-Sep.
Totals per section (IG, HY) give face outstanding, weighted-average price and aggregate principal vs par.

Bond prices and bid/ask are Bloomberg composite quotes that refresh about every 15 seconds; they are not individual trades. Cumulative daily bond volume is not available in Bloomberg fields; 'Last trade size (TRACE)' is the latest print. For the tape use TRAC <GO>. Equity volume (Equities sheet) is real.
Reference data: Barclays IG/HY Data Center Credit Digest, 16-Sep-2026 (Figures 5, 7, 8, 9); Morgan Stanley desk CDS 24-Aug-2026; instrument master and latest snapshot (2026-10-19_1034).
Rebuild: python C:\Users\daniel.grozdea\scripts\build_ai_credit_live.py (after running ai_credit_refresh.py to reset the snapshot reference).

Monitor columns S to Y: First issued (Bloomberg ISSUE_DT), live OAS, tenant comparable bond and its live OAS, live pickup (bond OAS minus comparable OAS), Barclays 15-Sep pickup and the change since. The bond ticker for terminal lookups moved to column Z.

Deal dossiers: the Deal Index sheet links to one tab per bond on the Monitor (built from SEC filings, indentures, company and rating agency releases; each tab lists its sources and what could not be verified). Dossiers live in the dossiers folder and are read at build time.
Caveats: yield changes vs Barclays mix YTW (Barclays) with yield-to-maturity (live), so they are approximate. Converts and loans are measured against par for comparability only.

notes.monitor: Notes: composite quotes refresh about every 15 seconds and are not individual trades. 'Last trade size' is the latest TRACE print (e.g. 5MM+ = $5mm or more); cumulative daily bond volume is not available from Bloomberg fields. Principal vs par excludes accrued interest. Amber yield = 10% or more (MS: HY datacenter deals get pulled near ~10%). Pink = yield up 25bp or more since 15-Sep (Barclays YTW vs live YTM, approximate). Pickup = bond OAS minus the tenant comparable bond's OAS (both live, Bloomberg OAS_SPREAD_MID); Barclays used G-spread on IG non-callables, so IG pickups differ slightly in basis. A negative pickup means the project bond trades tighter than the tenant's own unsecured bond (the CoreWeave comparable is now at about 1,050bp OAS). EDGCOM is measured against CoreWeave 9% 2031 (Chicago, about 60% of the credit); the Alibaba leg (BABA 2.125% 2031) is not blended. First issued = Bloomberg ISSUE_DT (issue / settlement date of the original issue; later taps are not separated).
notes.other: Live formulas as on the Monitor sheet. Snapshot reference: 2026-10-19_1034. Converts and loans are measured against par for comparability; their economic value depends on the equity / loan terms.
notes.cds: CDS_FLAT_SPREAD in bp. MS desk marks are Morgan Stanley Credit Trading, 24-Aug-2026.
notes.equities: Equity volume is real and a good proxy for activity in the credit. Relative volume = today's volume / 30-day average (amber at 1.5x or more).
